# Self Managing vs Hiring Us: Time, Money, Risk

Source: https://listandhost.com/compare/self-managing/
Updated: 2026-10-17
Summary: Running a short term rental yourself or hiring full service: hours, dollars and risks side by side, and when doing it yourself wins. Instant estimate.

Plenty of owners should run their own rental. This page shows where self managing wins, where full service wins and the numbers behind both, so you can decide without a sales call.

Checked October 17, 2026. We are a management company, so we have a stake in your answer. Every outside number names its source, listed at the bottom of the page, and every number of ours says what it is based on.

## Who should do it themselves, and who should not

### Self managing is usually better if

- You live within about 30 minutes of the home and can get there on short notice

- You have one home, flexible hours and you enjoy hosting

- You answer guests fast, nights and weekends included

- You have a cleaner you trust and a backup for the weeks they cannot come

- Most of your stays are long, so there are few turnovers to run

### Full service is usually better if

- You live far from the home or travel often

- You work full time, or you own more than one home

- Your market runs on events and weekends, where a wrong price costs the most

- You want the income without being on call

## Time, money and risk

Your own costs, like utilities, insurance and supplies, are the same in both columns. So are the platform fees.

|  | Managing it yourself | List & Host full service |
| - | - | - |
| Time |  |  |
| Hours a month | About 17 to 38 hours for one home with about eight stays a month (our estimate, basis below). A 2025 PriceLabs survey of more than 1,400 hosts found an average of 8.3 hours a week. | A few hours a year to approve big decisions, block your own dates and read your monthly statement (our estimate, from those three tasks). |
| When the work happens | Whenever a guest writes or something breaks, often at night, on weekends and on holidays. | Our team answers every guest message, every day of the week. Anything over your repair limit comes to you first. |
| Sick days and vacations | You need someone to cover for you. | Covered by our team. |
| Money |  |  |
| Management fee | None. | 20% of booking revenue. No setup fee. Nothing on nights you block for yourself. |
| On a home that books $40,000 a year in nightly rent (an illustration, not a forecast) | $0 in fees. | $8,000 a year in fees. |
| Pricing tools | The platforms' free tools, or pricing software you pay for and watch. | Our own pricing engine, included. |
| Cleaning, repairs and supplies | Guests pay the cleaning fee. Repairs and supplies at cost, and you arrange each one. | Guests pay the cleaning fee. Repairs and supplies at cost with receipts, arranged by us. |
| Revenue | Depends on how often you check your prices against nearby homes and events. | Every night for the next 12 months reviewed each morning, inside a floor you approve. We never promise a revenue number. |
| Risk |  |  |
| Insurance | Triple-I said in March 2026 that standard homeowners insurance typically does not cover commercial activities such as short term renting. Tell your insurer either way. | The same advice applies. We ask for a copy of a policy that allows short term rental before the first guest. |
| Damage | On Airbnb stays, AirCover for Hosts lists up to $3 million in damage protection and $1 million in liability insurance, with exclusions. You document the damage and file the claim yourself. | The same platform protection. Our cleaner checks and photographs the home after every stay, and we document damage and file the claim on time. |
| Pricing mistakes | A missed event week or a price left too low stays live until you notice it. | The engine never sets a price below your floor, never touches a booked night and locks event nights. Every change is logged and read back. |
| Reviews | A slow reply or a missed clean shows up in your reviews. | Routine messages go out by rule and a person handles the rest. Every clean follows a checklist with photos. |
| Leaving | Nothing to cancel. | Term and notice quoted in writing after a free look, before you sign anything. |

Booking revenue is the nightly rent plus any extra guest fees, after the platform's host fee. Taxes and cleaning fees are not part of it. Basis for our hours estimate: our experience running the homes our team runs, for one home with about eight stays a month, checked against the PriceLabs survey average. Your hours depend on how far you live from the home, how many stays you get and how much you automate. The $40,000 home is an illustration only.

## What one hour of your time is worth here

On the $40,000 example, the fee is $8,000 a year. By our estimate it buys back about 200 to 450 hours a year (17 to 38 hours a month, times 12). That works out to roughly $18 to $40 for each hour you no longer spend, before any change in revenue.

The math gets worse for hiring as revenue falls. On a home that books $20,000 a year, also an illustration, the fee is $4,000 and the same hours cost roughly $9 to $20 each. If an hour of your time is worth less than that and you have the hours, self managing keeps the money in your pocket. If it is worth more, or the hours are not there, full service can make sense.

Our [self managing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/self-managing-vs-hiring-an-airbnb-manager/) breaks the hours down task by task.

## Skip us if

- You live close, have the time and like doing it. Self manage, and use our free [owner guides](https://listandhost.com/blog/).

- Pricing is the only part you want help with. Look at remote pricing on our [services page](https://listandhost.com/services/) instead of full service.

- Your home books so few nights that the fee would cost more than your time is worth to you.

- You want full service outside our area. Full service in Fort Worth, the rest of Dallas Fort Worth and the Buffalo River region of Arkansas. Co hosting or remote pricing anywhere else in the United States.

There are middle options too: co hosting, a one time launch package and remote pricing, all on the [services page](https://listandhost.com/services/). Comparing a single co host with full service? Read [solo co host vs full service](https://listandhost.com/compare/solo-co-host/). Weighing a big company? Read [local team vs national managers](https://listandhost.com/compare/national-managers/).

## Questions owners ask

**Is it cheaper to manage my own Airbnb?**

In fees, yes. You pay no management fee and pay with time instead, about 17 to 38 hours a month for one home with about eight stays a month by our estimate. Whether that is cheaper depends on what an hour of your time is worth and how well you price.

**When is self managing the better choice?**

When you live close to the home, have one home and flexible hours, answer guests fast and have a reliable cleaner with a backup. Then the fee buys back time you do not need to buy.

**What does full service with List & Host cost?**

20% of booking revenue, with no setup fee. Booking revenue is the nightly rent plus any extra guest fees, after the platform's host fee. Taxes and cleaning fees are not part of it.

**Can I manage it myself now and hire help later?**

Yes. If your listing is already live, we join it as your host team, so your reviews and booking history stay yours.

## See your own numbers before you decide

Pick your market and your home. The instant estimator shows a low, likely and high yearly estimate, what platform fees and our fee take, and where every number comes from. Then decide which way to run it.

[Try the instant estimator](https://listandhost.com/estimate/)


# Solo Co Host vs Full Service Management

Source: https://listandhost.com/compare/solo-co-host/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: What a solo Airbnb co host covers against full service management: backup, cleaning, repairs, channels and fees, with honest picks. Instant estimate.

A good co host can be a great deal: one person who knows your home, answers fast and often costs less than a company. The gaps show up when that person is sick or away, or when something at the home needs hands. Here is the line by line view.

Checked October 17, 2026. We are a management company, so we have a stake in your answer. Every outside number names its source, listed at the bottom of the page, and every number of ours says what it is based on.

## What a co host is

A co host is someone you add to your listing to help run it. On Airbnb, the owner picks the access level: full access (calendar, pricing, listing details and reservations), calendar and messaging, or calendar only. Only the listing owner can set up or change a co host's payout. You keep the listing, the reviews and the payouts (Airbnb Help Center).

Airbnb launched its Co-Host Network in October 2024 to help owners find local co hosts, and said those co hosts averaged 4.9 stars (Airbnb Newsroom). Fees are agreed between owner and co host. A solo co host can be excellent. The question is what one person can cover.

The full explainer, with duties and costs side by side: [Airbnb co host vs property manager](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-co-host-vs-property-manager/).

## Solo co host against full service

Co hosts differ a lot, so the middle column says what to confirm, not what every co host does.

|  | Typical solo co host (varies by person) | List & Host full service |
| - | - | - |
| Running the listing |  |  |
| Guest messages | Usually included. Ask who answers when they sleep, travel or get sick. | Every message, every day of the week. Routine ones by rule, a person for the rest. |
| Pricing | Often included, by hand or with a tool they set up. Ask how often they check nearby homes. | Our own engine every morning, inside a floor you approve. Every change logged. |
| Listing and photos | Often included. | Written for how guests search, with the photo shoot directed by us. |
| Channels | Co host access on Airbnb gives no access to Vrbo or Booking.com. Each needs its own setup. | Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com on one calendar, so a night sold on one closes on the others. |
| At the home |  |  |
| Cleaning | Some schedule your cleaner. Some leave it to you. | Local cleaners scheduled around every stay, with a checklist and photos. |
| Repairs and emergencies | Depends on whether they live near the home. Ask who goes when a lock fails at night. | Trusted local pros. Anything over your repair limit comes to you first, and a true emergency is handled right away. |
| Supplies | Varies. | Restocked by us, at cost with receipts. |
| Money and backup |  |  |
| Fee | Set between you and the co host. One industry glossary puts typical co host pay at 10% to 30% of booking revenue, higher when they also handle cleaning and maintenance (Hostaway, 2026). | 20% of booking revenue. No setup fee. |
| Payouts | You keep the payouts. On Airbnb, only the listing owner can set up or change a co host's payout share. | Straight to you from the platforms. Guest money never sits with us. |
| Statements | Varies. Often the platform's own payout reports. | A monthly statement by the 10th, every booking and every cost. |
| Backup | One person. Ask who covers for them. | A team, so a sick day or a holiday does not stop the work. |
| Damage claims and reviews | Varies. | Damage documented with photos and filed on time. Every review answered. |

Booking revenue is the nightly rent plus any extra guest fees, after the platform's host fee. Taxes and cleaning fees are not part of it.

## Which one fits your home

### A solo co host is usually better if

- You already have one who answers fast, knows your home and has a backup

- You live nearby, or have a handy person for repairs and a cleaner you trust

- You only list on Airbnb and do not want other channels

- You want the lowest cost and are fine filling the gaps yourself

### Full service is usually better if

- You live far away and nobody near the home can handle a lockout or a leak

- Your co host is one person and you have had gaps when they were away

- You want Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com on one calendar

- You want one monthly statement with every booking and every cost

There is a middle path. We also offer co hosting: you keep your listing and your own cleaner, and we run pricing, guest messages, calendars and reviews, at a price quoted in writing after a [free look](https://listandhost.com/services/#free-look). Details are on the [services page](https://listandhost.com/services/).

## Questions to ask a co host

1. Who answers my guests when you are asleep, sick or on vacation?

2. How often do you check my prices against nearby homes, and with what?

3. Who schedules and checks the cleaner?

4. Who goes to the home for a lockout, a leak or a broken hot tub?

5. What exactly is your fee charged on, and what access do you need?

## Skip us if

- You have a co host you trust who answers fast and has a backup. Keep them. If pricing is the weak spot, look at remote pricing on the [services page](https://listandhost.com/services/).

- You only want help with guest messages and handle everything else yourself.

- You need someone local for hands at the home outside our area. Full service in Fort Worth, the rest of Dallas Fort Worth and the Buffalo River region of Arkansas. Co hosting or remote pricing anywhere else in the United States.

Also weighing other options? Read [self managing vs hiring us](https://listandhost.com/compare/self-managing/) or [local team vs national managers](https://listandhost.com/compare/national-managers/).

## Questions owners ask

**What is the difference between a co host and a full service manager?**

A co host joins your listing with the access you choose, and you keep the listing, the reviews and the payouts. A full service manager also runs everything at the home: cleaners, repairs and supplies, usually on every channel. With us, platform payouts still go straight to you.

**How much does an Airbnb co host charge?**

There is no set rate. Owner and co host agree on it. One industry glossary puts typical co host pay at 10% to 30% of booking revenue, higher for co hosts who also handle cleaning and maintenance.

**Is a solo co host enough for one home?**

Often, yes, if they answer fast, live near the home or have local help, and have someone covering when they are away. The risk is one person: when they are out, the guest still needs an answer.

**Does List & Host offer co hosting too?**

Yes. You keep your listing and your own cleaner, and we run pricing, guest messages, calendars and reviews. The price is quoted in writing after a free look.

## Know what your home could book

Before you choose a co host or full service, see a low, likely and high yearly estimate for your market and your home in the instant estimator, with the basis for every number.

# Local Team vs National Rental Managers

Source: https://listandhost.com/compare/national-managers/
Updated: 2026-10-17
Summary: A local team with its own pricing engine against large national rental managers: who prices, who answers and who fits each. Sourced. Instant estimate.

Large national managers bring scale, years of process and big support teams. We bring a small team that runs homes itself and a pricing engine we built and watch every day. Here is how the two models differ, where each one fits and what to ask either one. We compare no company by name; market figures come from a 2026 fee guide.

Checked October 17, 2026. We are a management company, so we have a stake in your answer. Every outside number names its source, listed at the bottom of the page, and every number of ours says what it is based on.

## What each model does well

### Large national companies

- Work in many states, so one agreement can cover homes in several markets

- Large support teams and processes built over years

- Several plan levels. Limited plans that leave guest issues, cleaning and maintenance with the owner run about 10% to 15% across the market (Awning, 2026)

- Some run their own booking sites on top of the big platforms

### A local team like ours

- The people who price your home run short term rentals every day

- Our own engine reviews every night for the next 12 months each morning, inside a floor you approve

- Every price change is logged and read back, so you can see what moved and why

- You deal with the same small team that runs your home

- Full service only where we have local people, so someone can get to the home

## Local team against national company

The middle column describes the market, not any one company. Companies differ a lot, so get every answer in writing.

|  | Large national company (varies by company) | List & Host |
| - | - | - |
| Where they work | Many markets across the country. Check that they have people near your home. | Full service in Fort Worth, the rest of Dallas Fort Worth and the Buffalo River region of Arkansas. Co hosting or remote pricing anywhere else in the United States. |
| Who sets your prices | Varies: a central revenue team, software or both. Ask how often your home is reviewed, and by whom. | Our own engine every morning, with a person checking nearby homes and approving the big moves. |
| Price guardrails | Ask for their floor rules and a sample of their price change log. | A floor you approve, event nights locked, booked nights never touched, every change logged and read back. |
| Fee | Across the market, most full service fees land around 18% to 25% of revenue. Limited plans run about 10% to 15%, and luxury or resort models about 25% to 40%. Some companies quote per property instead of publishing a fee (Awning, 2026). | 20% of booking revenue for full service. No setup fee. |
| What the fee is charged on | Gross or net revenue, sometimes including cleaning fees. Ask for the revenue definition in the agreement (Awning, 2026). | Booking revenue, defined in writing: the nightly rent plus extra guest fees, after the platform's host fee. Never cleaning fees or taxes. |
| Repairs and supplies | Vendor cost, sometimes plus a coordination markup that varies by company (Awning, 2026). | At cost, with receipts. |
| Agreement | Across the market, terms range from no long term contract to 1 to 3 years, with 90 days notice to cancel at one large company (Awning, 2026). | Term and notice quoted in writing after a free look, before you sign anything. |
| History and size | Often years of history, many homes and a large support staff. | A small team with a short record: the homes our team runs, every number explained on our results page. |
| Guest ratings | Airbnb reported in October 2024 that large managers, those with more than 30 active listings, averaged 4.62 stars, against 4.9 for co hosts in its Co-Host Network. That is a group average, not a score for any one company. | A Guest Favorite rated 4.9 among the homes our team runs. See our results page. |

Market figures come from a 2026 fee guide and an Airbnb announcement, listed at the bottom of the page. The 4.9 rating was read from the public Airbnb listing on October 16, 2026.

## What it does, and what it does not do

Each morning the engine reviews every night for the next 12 months on the homes our team runs. It works from a floor price, weekend and event prices, minimum stays and a fill plan for quiet weeks. It never sets a price below the floor, never touches a booked night and locks event nights so no automatic cut can reach them. Each change is written, read back and logged.

In its first 26 days live, September 21 to October 16, 2026, it logged 133 nightly price changes and 52 minimum stay changes across the homes our team runs (basis: the engine's own change log).

It does not replace judgment. A person checks nearby homes and approves the big moves. It is also not perfect: our October 13 check of nearby homes found open dates at one of our homes priced 11% to 25% under the local median, and we fixed them that day. Our [dynamic pricing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/) explains the rules in plain words.

## Questions to ask any manager, national or local

1. Who sets my prices, how often is my home reviewed, and can I see the change log?

2. What exactly is the fee charged on, in writing? Are cleaning fees included?

3. Is there a setup fee, and are repairs or supplies marked up?

4. How long is the term, and how much notice do I give to leave?

5. Who is my one contact, and who covers for them?

6. Who cleans, and who checks their work?

7. Can I see a real monthly statement from a home you run?

Our [guide to management fees](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-management-fees/) shows how to compare quotes line by line.

## Skip us if

- You own homes in several states and want one company for all of them.

- You want a company with many years of history and a large support staff.

- You want full service outside our area. Full service in Fort Worth, the rest of Dallas Fort Worth and the Buffalo River region of Arkansas. Co hosting or remote pricing anywhere else in the United States.

- You want a fixed monthly rent or a lease instead of a share of bookings. We do not offer that.

- You want the lowest percentage and will handle guest issues, cleaning and repairs yourself. A limited plan elsewhere, or our remote pricing on the [services page](https://listandhost.com/services/), can cost less.

Also comparing other options? Read [self managing vs hiring us](https://listandhost.com/compare/self-managing/) or [solo co host vs full service](https://listandhost.com/compare/solo-co-host/).

## Questions owners ask

**Are national vacation rental companies cheaper than a local manager?**

Sometimes. Across the market, full service fees most often land around 18% to 25% of revenue, and limited plans that leave guest issues, cleaning and maintenance with the owner run about 10% to 15%, according to a 2026 fee guide. Compare what each plan covers and what the fee is charged on, not just the percentage.

**What is different about a local team with its own pricing engine?**

The people who set your prices run homes themselves. Our engine reviews every night for the next 12 months each morning, inside a floor you approve, and logs every change so you can check it. A person approves the big moves.

**When is a national company the better fit?**

When you own homes in several states and want one agreement, or you want a company with years of history and a large support staff. We are a small team, and we offer full service only where we have local people.

**Will you earn more for my home than a national company would?**

Nobody can promise that, and we do not. We show our own results with every number explained, and the instant estimator gives a range for your home with the basis for each figure.

## Start with your own numbers

Whoever you hire, know what your home could book first. The instant estimator shows a low, likely and high yearly estimate for your market and your home, with the basis for every number.

# Glass House Case Study: Buffalo River Region Results

Source: https://listandhost.com/results/buffalo-river-glass-house/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Real numbers from a glass house in the Buffalo River region: 27 of 31 October 2026 nights booked as of Oct 16, a 4.9 rating, and the moves behind it.

A glass house with a hot tub, listed on Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com and a direct booking site, and run every day with our own pricing and messaging engine, which took over its prices on September 21, 2026. Here is what it booked, what it paid out, and the moves behind each number, with the nights booked before that date kept apart.

**4.9** Airbnb rating from 11 reviews, Guest Favorite

**27 of 31** October nights booked

**$502** average October night

**$13,720** October payouts booked, after platform fees

As of October 16, 2026. October is not over, so its figures are booked, not earned. Our pricing engine took over the glass house's prices on September 21, 2026; 15 of the 27 October nights were booked before then and are not its work. How we counted is at the bottom of this page.

At a glance

## Glass house with a hot tub

Sleeps**10**

First stay**July 15, 2026**

Booking sites**3 plus direct**

Stays not from Airbnb**7 of 35**

Average stay**3.4 nights**

Average group**4 guests**

Median days booked ahead**25**

Payouts, July to October, October as booked**$32,143**

Payouts after platform fees, before cleaning and other costs. They include the guest cleaning fee. October is not over, so it counts every October stay booked so far, not money earned. Average stay, average group and days booked ahead count every stay booked so far, through June 2027.

## Nights, rates and payouts

Straight from our booking records and the platform payouts. October is peak fall color here, and the month is still in progress.

More on how we run homes in the [Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/), and the month by month pattern in [Buffalo River cabin income by season](https://listandhost.com/blog/buffalo-river-cabin-income-by-season/).

| Month | Nights booked | Share of nights | Average night | Payouts | Payouts as bars |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| July 2026 | 9 | partial | not shown | $3,092 |  |
| August 2026 | 16 | 52% | $455 | $7,913 |  |
| September 2026 | 25 | 83% | $306 | $7,419 |  |
| October 2026 (booked to date) | 27 | 87% | $502 | $13,720 |  |
| July to October | 77 |  |  | $32,143 |  |

July starts with the first stay on July 15, so no share is shown, and one July stay has no nightly breakdown, so no July average is shown. September had 2 nights blocked; they count as unbooked. October counts nights booked through October 31 as of October 16. Our pricing engine took over the glass house's prices on September 21, 2026: every July and August night, 22 of the 25 September nights and 15 of the 27 October nights were booked before then.

**Already on the books:** 9 more stays, 41 nights and $21,386 in payouts from November 2026 to June 2027, including Christmas nights at $799 and a New Year week that averages $632 a night.

## The moves behind the numbers

Our engine runs a full pricing pass every morning and checks bookings and messages every 30 minutes. Every price change is checked against a floor, read back after it is written, and logged. Big moves go to a person, who approves them with one word.

### Christmas booked at $799 a night

Holidays and peak dates get their own floors and minimum stays, set months ahead. Christmas nights were booked on October 10 at $799. The two October weekends that sold at $749 a night, October 2 to 4 and October 23 to 25, were booked in August and September, before the engine took over this home's prices on September 21, so we do not count them as its work.

### A lost weekend, sold again in eight days

A free cancellation reopened the October 16 to 17 peak color weekend two weeks out. We stepped the price down in three moves while watching the one similar hot tub home still open nearby. It sold on Vrbo the next morning. On October 6 we also moved the listing to a firm cancellation policy, so a late cancellation no longer means a full refund.

October 3**$749 to $649**

October 7**$649 to $599**

October 9**$599 to $549**

October 10**Sold, 2 nights**

### Two single nights that would have sat empty

October 8 and October 18 were single open nights between bookings, too short for the two night minimum. On October 1 the engine dropped the minimum to one night on both. The guest arriving October 9 added October 8, and a Vrbo guest booked October 18 three days ahead. Together they added about $928 in payouts, and the house is now booked 22 nights in a row, October 8 to the October 30 checkout (10 of them booked before September 21).

### No more nights sold under $200

In September, before the hard floor, low leftover prices and last minute discounts sold 11 nights under $200, three of them at $142. On September 28 we set a hard floor of $349 a night on every channel and capped last minute discounts at 10 percent. Every night booked since then has sold at $314 or more: the floor less the capped discount.

### 100% response rate, replies within an hour

That is what the public Airbnb listing shows. Check in details go out on their own before arrival, including what to know about the gravel drive in. When the cabin next door is booked during a stay, the engine sends the main house guest a short heads up three days before arrival, reads it back and logs it.

### 13 of 15 reviews are five stars

That count covers Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com. On Airbnb and Vrbo we review each guest the day they leave, then send a thank you note. Five star reviews get a short public reply. Anything less gets a careful reply, approved by a person and written for the next guest. We never offer anything in exchange for a review.

## 4.9 on Airbnb, a Guest Favorite

Cleanliness 5.0. Accuracy, check in and communication 4.9. Location and value 4.7. From 11 reviews, read on the public listing on October 16, 2026.

“This house was spotless!! Incredibly comfortable and spacious.” Guest, Sep 2026, on Vrbo

“Gorgeous home and beautiful private serene views in every direction.”Guest, Sep 2026

## Event pricing, a fill ladder and a market check

Our engine runs a full pricing pass every morning and checks bookings and messages every 30 minutes. Every price change is checked against a floor, read back after it is written, and logged. Big moves go to a person, who approves them with one word.

### Quiet nights sell, without a fire sale

Open Friday and Saturday nights 22 to 30 days out step down 5 percent a week, never more than 20 percent under their first price and never under the $149 floor (settings as of October 18, 2026). Until October 17 the step was 10 percent a week on every open night 22 to 35 days out. Under that rule, on September 21, Friday and Saturday October 16 and 17 were still open 25 days out. The engine cut both from $249 to $225. A group of six booked both nights the next day.

September 21**$249 to $225**

September 22**Sold, 2 nights**

### A concert weekend priced back up, sold in four hours

The ladder had slid the Friday and Saturday of a November concert weekend at Dickies Arena down to $202. Live comps showed similar homes asking $773 and up for those two nights. We raised both nights to $249 on October 9. They sold on Booking.com about four hours later.

Ladder price**$202**

October 9, after the comp check**$249**

About 4 hours later**Sold, 2 nights**

### Start high, step down, no empty nights

October 8, a Cowboys Thursday night game, was priced at $449. Still unsold five days out, it stepped to $249, then to $199 three days out, and sold the day before. October 7 sold that same morning as a one night stay. The house is booked 23 nights in a row, October 2 to the October 25 checkout.

### 29 future nights raised to market

On October 13 a live comp check found our open nights 11 to 25 percent under the local median. We raised 29 future nights, among them Thanksgiving from $225 to $319 and 23 weekend nights from December to April up to $299 or $319. Each one was read back and put on hold so no automatic cut can undo it. It is too early to show results.

### Big dates set a year ahead

Floors and minimum stays are already in place for the 2027 Fort Worth Stock Show, with a two night minimum and floors of $299 on weekdays and $379 on weekends. Thanksgiving, New Year's Eve and the Cotton Bowl, big Dickies Arena shows and game days, and the night of July 4, 2027 are set too.

### Clean, easy check in, fast answers

On Airbnb, cleanliness, check in and communication all rate 5.0, and 12 of 14 reviews are five stars. Check in details go out on their own before arrival. Early check in and late checkout requests get an answer drafted from who arrives and leaves that day, approved by a person. We never offer anything in exchange for a review.

## 4.9 on Airbnb from 14 reviews

Cleanliness, check in and communication 5.0. Accuracy 4.9. Value 4.8. Location 4.3. Read on the public listing on October 16, 2026.

# Cabin Loft Case Study: Launching a New Listing

Source: https://listandhost.com/results/ozark-cabin-loft/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: How a new cabin loft listing, live since Sep 24, 2026, booked 6 stays in its first 3 weeks, with the launch pricing and gap fills behind it.

A one bedroom loft cabin next to the glass house. It went live on September 24, 2026 with no reviews, and guests trust reviews. Here is the launch plan, and what it booked.

**3 days** from going live to the first booking

**13** nights in a row booked, October 14 to the October 27 checkout

**16 of 31** October nights booked

**$1,709** October payouts booked, after platform fees

As of October 16, 2026. October is not over, so its figures are booked, not earned.

At a glance

## Cabin loft next to the glass house

Layout**Loft bedroom, sleeps 4**

Went live**September 24, 2026**

Booking sites**2 plus direct**

Stays booked by October 14**6**

Average October night**$97**

Airbnb response rate**100%**

First review**5 stars**

Airbnb shows a rating after three reviews. Until then we report each review as it comes in.

## Four moves for a listing with no reviews

A new listing has to earn trust fast. The first three stays matter more than the first three dollars.

More on how we run homes in the [Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/), and the month by month pattern in [Buffalo River cabin income by season](https://listandhost.com/blog/buffalo-river-cabin-income-by-season/).

### Price for the first reviews

$89 weeknights and $149 weekends until the cabin has three reviews. The platform's new listing discount ran on top.

### Make it easy to book

Instant book on Airbnb and Vrbo, and same day bookings until 6 PM.

### Lead with the best photo

The loft as the cover, then the porch swing and the wooded view.

### Show the space right

The listing shows the loft bedroom and the queen bed downstairs, so the sleeps 4 promise is clear.

## Adjust fast, fill every gap

During launch the automatic rules stay off for this cabin. Each price move is approved by a person and then written through the engine, which checks the floor, reads the price back and logs it.

### $169 weekends had no takers

After the first booking, no weekend night sold at $169. On October 7 we cut October 23 and 24 to $149. They booked within a week.

### A two night gap, filled

October 17 and 18 sat between two bookings. On October 4 we allowed one night stays on both. A Vrbo guest booked both nights on October 12, and the cabin now runs 13 nights in a row with no gaps.

### Shared land, handled in writing

Every cabin check in message carries the shared land rules and a photo of where to park. When the cabin is booked during a main house stay, the engine sends that guest a short heads up three days before arrival and reads it back.

### Step the price up as reviews land

The plan once the cabin has three reviews: weeknights back to $109, then $129, each step approved and written through the engine.

## Six stays, 16 nights

All six were booked between September 27 and October 14. Average night is what guests paid after discounts.

| Stay | Nights | Channel | Average night | Payout |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Oct 8 to Oct 11 | 3 | Airbnb | $103 | $233 |
| Oct 14 to Oct 17 | 3 | Airbnb | $114 | $360 |
| Oct 17 to Oct 19 | 2 | Vrbo | $95 | $241 (estimate) |
| Oct 19 to Oct 23 | 4 | Airbnb | $71 | $376 |
| Oct 23 to Oct 25 | 2 | Airbnb | $131 | $293 |
| Oct 25 to Oct 27 | 2 | Airbnb | $78 | $204 |
| October 2026 | 16 |  | $97 | $1,709 |

Payouts after platform fees, before cleaning and other costs. The Vrbo payout is an estimate until the deposit lands.

One review so far, five stars. Response rate 100%, replies within an hour, read on the public Airbnb listing on October 16, 2026.

“The host was incredibly helpful, kind, and responsive throughout our stay.”Guest, Oct 2026

## Buffalo River region owner questions

**How much does cabin management cost near the Buffalo River?**

Full service is one flat 20% of booking revenue. Booking revenue is the nightly rent plus any extra guest fees, after the platform's host fee. Taxes and cleaning fees are not part of it. There is no setup fee, guests pay the cleaning fee, and repairs and supplies are billed at cost with receipts.

**Which towns do you cover?**

Full service in Fort Worth, the rest of Dallas Fort Worth and the Buffalo River region of Arkansas. Co hosting or remote pricing anywhere else in the United States. Here that means the Buffalo River region around Jasper, Ponca and Harrison, wherever we can staff a vetted local cleaning team. [Hot Springs](https://listandhost.com/hot-springs/), [Eureka Springs](https://listandhost.com/eureka-springs/), [Branson](https://listandhost.com/branson/) and other Ozark markets get co hosting or remote pricing.

**When is the busy season?**

October fall color is the peak. May and June are strong too. Winter weekdays are the quietest, so pricing and minimum stays matter most then.

**Can guests count on floating the river?**

Not always. The upper river often runs too low to float in summer and fall, so we sell the home itself: the deck, the hot tub, the trails and the night sky. Floating is a bonus when the water is up.

**What has the glass house your team runs done?**

October 2026 has 27 of 31 nights booked at an average of $502 a night, with $13,720 in October payouts booked after platform fees, as of October 16, 2026. October is not over, so those are bookings, not earnings. Our pricing engine took over the glass house's prices on September 21, 2026, so 15 of its 27 October nights were booked before it ran there and are not its work. It is rated 4.9 on Airbnb and is a Guest Favorite. Past results are not a promise of what your home will earn.

# Airbnb Management in Arlington, TX

Source: https://listandhost.com/arlington/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Airbnb management in Arlington, TX, priced around AT&T Stadium, Globe Life Field and Six Flags. Local cleaning, daily pricing. Free estimate.

Updated October 18, 2026

Arlington books on game days. AT&T Stadium, Globe Life Field, Six Flags and Texas Live! sit within a few miles of each other. We offer full service in Arlington from our Fort Worth base, wherever we can staff a vetted local cleaning team, with nightly prices that move with every event.

The average Arlington, TX short term rental listed at $278 a night, booked 35% of its nights and took in about $25,379 in yearly revenue (AirROI public market data, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026, read October 16, 2026). A market average is not a promise of what your home will earn. Full service runs here for 20% of booking revenue, with local cleaners and repair people we schedule.

## What an Arlington rental earns, by two estimates

| Source | Period | Average nightly rate | Occupancy | Yearly revenue | Listings |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| AirROI | Aug 2025 to Jul 2026 | $278 | 34.8% | $25,379 average | 896 |
| GuestFavorites | Jan to Sep 2026 | $234 | 45% | $38,533 median | 1,005 |

Both windows include June and July 2026, when AT&T Stadium hosted nine World Cup matches. AirROI's highest rates and revenue land in June for that reason. Plan 2027 on a normal football and baseball year, not on that summer.

The spread matters more than the average. GuestFavorites puts the top 10% of Arlington listings near 85% occupancy and $62,576 a year, and the bottom quarter near 11% and $6,367. Same city, same stadium. The gap is pricing, photos, reviews and how fast guests get answers.

Market figures are third party estimates for the period shown. They are not a promise of income. Your estimate is built from your home and its own comparable listings.

## When Arlington fills up

Three stadiums, a theme park and a university keep the calendar busy. These are the dates we price around.

| - | - |

| Friday, December 4, 2026 | Big 12 Championship at AT&T Stadium. |
| Friday, January 1, 2027 | Cotton Bowl Classic, a College Football Playoff quarterfinal, at AT&T Stadium. |

| Late April | Lone Star Smokeout, a barbecue and country music festival at AT&T Stadium, was set for April 24 to 26, 2026. |
| March to September | Texas Rangers home games at Globe Life Field, and stadium concerts on open dates. |
| May and December | UT Arlington graduations bring families for two or three nights. |
| June to August | Six Flags and Hurricane Harbor family trips. |

Not every 2027 date is announced yet. We load each event as it is confirmed and set its price and minimum stay before demand shows up.

## What Arlington guests look for

### How they search

- By venue. Guests type AT&T Stadium, Globe Life Field or Six Flags, so the title, the first photo and the map pin carry the listing.

- By group size. Game day groups travel together, so a 4 or 5 bedroom home with beds for everyone sells to the whole group.

- By parking. Groups arrive in more than one car, so a driveway that fits three cars belongs in the photos.

- By minutes to the gate. Game day traffic is real, and drive time beats distance.

### What moves the rate

- A theme room: $70,843 a year on average with one, $23,310 without. Only 4.4% of Arlington listings have one.

- Mini golf or a big backyard game: $101,051 with, $23,739 without, in 2.1% of listings.

- The basics still decide most of it. Listings with a full kitchen averaged $26,239, against $6,474 without.

- A pool for summer families, and house rules that keep neighbors on your side.

AirROI compares listings with and without each feature, August 2025 to July 2026. It shows correlation, not a promise.

Source: https://listandhost.com/branson/

Summary: Remote pricing and co hosting for Branson homes and condos: show season, Silver Dollar City Christmas and the January dip. Get a free review.

Updated October 18, 2026

Branson is a family and group market. Shows on the 76 Strip, Silver Dollar City and Table Rock Lake fill big homes and resort condos from spring through Christmas. Then January goes quiet. We offer remote pricing and listing work to Branson owners, so the busy months carry the slow ones.

The average Branson, MO short term rental listed at $251 a night, booked 34% of its nights and took in about $25,747 in yearly revenue (AirROI public market data, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026, read October 16, 2026). A market average is not a promise of what your home will earn. We do not run full service here yet. Co hosting or remote pricing does. January averaged 17.4% occupancy in AirROI's data, so no price fills it alone. We lower minimum stays, add weekly discounts, step unsold nights down on a schedule and hold a floor you set, so the quiet months add what they can without giving the house away.

Yes. Resort condos compete on price, pools and views, so pricing and photos carry them. Big houses compete on group size, game rooms and parking, so the listing has to sell the whole group.

By September. Silver Dollar City's An Old Time Christmas runs November 7, 2026 to January 2, 2027, December is a peak month, and Branson guests book about 50 days ahead on average.

# Broken Bow Cabin Pricing and Co Hosting

Source: https://listandhost.com/broken-bow/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Broken Bow and Hochatown cabin pricing and co hosting, run remotely. Cabin supply keeps growing, so daily pricing decides who books. Get a free review.

Updated October 18, 2026

Broken Bow still earns the highest nightly rates of any market we cover: $458 on average in AirROI's data. But supply grew 29.5% in a year while revenue grew 0.2%, and 86% of listings now have a hot tub. Winning here takes pricing and listing work, every day. We do that remotely for cabin owners, from Dallas Fort Worth, about three hours away.

The average Broken Bow, OK short term rental listed at $458 a night, booked 35% of its nights and took in about $51,710 in yearly revenue (AirROI public market data, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026, read October 16, 2026). A market average is not a promise of what your home will earn. We do not run full service here yet. Co hosting or remote pricing does. Remote pricing means our engine sets the nightly rates and minimum stays for a home in any US market while the owner keeps local cleaning and upkeep.

## High rates, crowded calendar

| Source | Period | Average nightly rate | Occupancy | Yearly revenue | Listings |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| AirROI | Aug 2025 to Jul 2026 | $458 | 35.4% | $51,710 average | 3,170 |
| BNBCalc, wider area | 12 months to Sep 2026 | $412 | 34% | $66,965 average | 5,225 |

| Season (AirROI) | Months | Average nightly rate | Occupancy |
| - | - | - | - |
| Peak | March, December, June | $507 | 43.6% |
| Low | January, February, September | $415 | 30.1% |

Supply up 29.5% in a year, revenue up 0.2%. That is more cabins splitting the same guests. The well run cabins hold their weekends and fill weeknights. The rest compete on price alone.

November has the highest occupancy, and November stays are booked 72 days ahead. March brings the most revenue. June brings the highest nightly rates. Stays are short, 2.7 nights on average.

Market figures are third party estimates for the period shown. They are not a promise of income. Your estimate is built from your home and its own comparable listings.

| January to February | The low season. January has the lowest occupancy. |
| All year | Beavers Bend State Park, Hochatown restaurants, wineries and breweries, and weekend drives from Dallas Fort Worth, Oklahoma City, Tulsa and Shreveport. |

# Airbnb Management in Dallas, TX

Source: https://listandhost.com/dallas/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Airbnb management in Dallas for long stays, work trips and State Fair weekends. Daily pricing, guest messages, local cleaning. Get a free estimate.

Updated October 18, 2026

Dallas guests stay a long time: 5.9 nights on average in AirROI's data, against 3.3 in Branson or Hot Springs. They come for work, hospitals, moves and family. Then the State Fair, Texas vs OU and arena nights stack big weekends on top. We offer full service in Dallas from our Fort Worth base.

The average Dallas, TX short term rental listed at $256 a night, booked 38% of its nights and took in about $24,382 in yearly revenue (AirROI public market data, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026, read October 16, 2026). A market average is not a promise of what your home will earn. Full service runs here for 20% of booking revenue, with local cleaners and repair people we schedule.

Dallas books late. The average stay is booked 30 days ahead, and February stays only 19 days ahead, in AirROI's data. A price set once in the spring is wrong by the time most guests look. Ours moves every day.

The best homes pull away from the pack. GuestFavorites puts the top 10% of Dallas listings at $63,323 a year, well above the median.

## What Dallas guests look for

### How they search

- By neighborhood: Uptown, Deep Ellum, Bishop Arts, Lower Greenville, near Love Field or near the Medical District.

- By trip length. Weekly and monthly discounts show up in search results, and Dallas stays run almost six nights.

- By workspace and wifi, for the work trip.

- By parking. Street parking in older neighborhoods worries guests, so a driveway or garage belongs in the first photos.

### What moves the rate

- A washer: $26,080 a year on average with one, $8,708 without. Nine in ten listings have one, so missing it hurts.

- A full kitchen: $25,089 with, $6,307 without. Long stays cook.

- Rare extras line up with top earners: kids' bikes ($81,317 a year with, in 0.4% of listings) and a kayak ($65,225 with, 0.3%).

- Pet friendly with a fenced yard, for relocations and long stays.

AirROI compares listings with and without each feature, August 2025 to July 2026. It shows correlation, not a promise.

## Full service management, from our Fort Worth base

Dallas is inside our full service area. That means we handle the whole operation, and you approve the big decisions.

### Full service management

Listing and photo direction, daily pricing, every guest message, cleaning with a vetted local team, maintenance coordination, reviews and a monthly statement with every booking and cost.

### Co hosting

Already hosting and want to keep your listing? You keep the listing, the reviews and the payouts. We run pricing, guest messages and the cleaning schedule as your co host.

### Launch package

For a home that is not listed yet: a setup list, smart lock and guest guide, photo direction, listing copy for Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com, and pricing rules, so you go live fast.

### How our pricing engine works

- A rate for every night, a year out, with a floor you approve. No price we set goes under it.

- Event nights priced on their own, set before the crowd books.

- Minimum stays by season, lowered for short gaps between stays so those nights can still sell.

- A fill ladder: unsold nights step down on a set schedule as the date gets close, never past the floor.

- Every change logged and read back from the channel, so what you see is what guests see.

### What it costs

Full service is one flat 20% of booking revenue. What it covers is in our [pricing section](https://listandhost.com/pricing/). Co hosting, the launch package and remote work are quoted in writing after a [free look](https://listandhost.com/services/#free-look) at your home.

You can block dates for your own use any time. Repairs above an amount you set come to you with a quote first.

# Eureka Springs Airbnb Pricing and Co Hosting

Source: https://listandhost.com/eureka-springs/

Updated October 18, 2026

Almost half the rentals in Eureka Springs are one bedroom places: 46.5% in AirROI's data. It is a couples town. Weddings, anniversaries, walks downtown and a hot tub at night. We offer remote pricing and listing work to Eureka Springs owners, with the same system behind the Ozark cabin loft and glass house our team runs.

The average Eureka Springs, AR short term rental listed at $215 a night, booked 34% of its nights and took in about $23,139 in yearly revenue (AirROI public market data, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026, read October 16, 2026). A market average is not a promise of what your home will earn. We do not run full service here yet. Co hosting or remote pricing does. ## A small market that lives on October

AirROI estimates, August 2025 to July 2026.

| Measure | Eureka Springs |
| - | - |
| Average nightly rate | $215 |
| Occupancy | 33.6% |
| Yearly revenue, average | $23,139 |
| Listings | 835 |
| Revenue in a year | down 0.3% |
| Average stay | 2.7 nights |
| Booked ahead | 47 days on average |

| Season | Months | Average nightly rate | Occupancy |
| - | - | - | - |
| Peak | May, June, October | $227 | 42.3% |
| October alone | October | $239 | 50.3% |
| Low | December, January, February | $197 | 29.5% |

October is the month. Half of all nights sell, at the best rate of the year, and October stays are booked 73 days ahead on average. If your October rates are still flat in August, the best nights are already gone at the wrong price.

Stays are short: 2.7 nights on average and 2.3 in October. Weekend minimums that fit how couples book, plus one night gap fills midweek, keep the calendar tight.

Market figures are third party estimates for the period shown. They are not a promise of income. Your estimate is built from your home and its own comparable listings.

## What brings people to Eureka Springs

| When | What fills Eureka Springs homes |
| - | - |

| May | May Festival of the Arts, all month. May is in the peak group. |
| June and July | Thursday evening concerts in Basin Park, and summer lake trips to Beaver Lake. |
| Late August | Volkswagen and Ozark Euro Festival (August 28 to 30 in 2026). |
| September | The Original Ozark Folk Festival, Jeep Jam (September 10 to 12 in 2026) and Bikes, Blues and BBQ weekend in Fayetteville, about an hour away. |

| December to February | The low season. Couples getaways at lower rates. |
| All year | Weddings and elopements, the historic downtown, Turpentine Creek Wildlife Refuge and the Lake Leatherwood trails. |

## What wins a couples market

### How couples choose

- A hot tub, a view and a king bed in the first three photos.

- Honest walk times to downtown. The streets are steep, so say so.

- Parking at the door, with a photo of it.

- Privacy. No shared walls, no shared yard.

### What moves the rate

- Wifi. About one listing in ten still has none, and those averaged $10,096 a year against $24,676 with it.

- A pool table: $53,427 with, $22,089 without, in 3.4% of listings.

- Exercise equipment: $54,583 with, in 1.0% of listings.

- Wedding ready: room to get dressed, good light for photos and a clear house rule on guests.

AirROI compares listings with and without each feature, August 2025 to July 2026. It shows correlation, not a promise.

# Glen Rose and Granbury Airbnb Pricing

Source: https://listandhost.com/glen-rose-granbury/

Updated October 18, 2026

Two small towns southwest of Fort Worth, about an hour from our home base, with two different guests. Glen Rose sells dinosaur tracks, Fossil Rim and the Paluxy River to families. Granbury sells Lake Granbury and its historic square to groups and long weekends. We help owners in both price and list.

The average Glen Rose, TX short term rental listed at $234 a night, booked 34% of its nights and took in about $29,437 in yearly revenue (AirROI public market data, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026, read October 16, 2026). A market average is not a promise of what your home will earn. We do not run full service here yet. Co hosting or remote pricing does. ## Two towns, side by side

AirROI estimates, August 2025 to July 2026.

| Town | Average nightly rate | Occupancy | Yearly revenue, average | Listings | Revenue in a year |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Glen Rose | $234 | 34.1% | $29,437 | 98 | up 3.1% |
| Granbury | $298 | 34.1% | $28,733 | 425 | down 10.4% |

| Season | Glen Rose | Granbury |
| - | - | - |
| Peak months | March, May, October: $238 a night, 44.1% booked | May, June, October: $313 a night, 40.5% booked |
| Low months | January, February, September: $213, 28.5% | January, February, December: $274, 33.0% |
| Booked ahead | 46 days on average | 41 days on average |
| Average stay | 3.2 nights | 4.3 nights |

Glen Rose is small and growing fast: 98 listings, with supply up 21% in a year. New listings compete on price first, so a flat rate set last year now loses its weekends.

Granbury is bigger, and 61.4% of its listings have 3 or more bedrooms. Stays run longer, and revenue fell 10.4% in a year. In a softer market, homes priced every day keep their occupancy.

Market figures are third party estimates for the period shown. They are not a promise of income. Your estimate is built from your home and its own comparable listings.

| June to August | River days on the Paluxy and the Brazos | The Old Fashioned Fourth of July Festival on the square, and lake season |
| September to October | Paluxy River Jam (September 17 to 19 in 2026). October is in the peak group. | Harvest Moon Festival of the Arts. October is in the peak group. |
| November to December | Holiday family trips | December is in the low group, a good month for weekly stays |
| All year | Fossil Rim Wildlife Center, Dinosaur World, weddings, and contract crews during refueling outages at the Comanche Peak nuclear plant | Lake Granbury, the historic square and Granbury Opera House, weddings and family reunions |

| BNBCalc | 12 months to Sep 2026 | $286 | 32% | $40,589 average | 3,040 |

| Season (AirROI) | Months | Average nightly rate | Occupancy |
| - | - | - | - |
| Peak | June, March, May | $292 | 41.5% |
| Low | January, February, September | $239 | 29.3% |

The sources agree on rate: the mid to high $200s a night. They disagree on occupancy, from about a third of nights to nearly half. That gap is the difference between a listing that is priced and run every day and one that is not.

Stays are short, 3.3 nights on average, and booked 44 days ahead. July stays book 66 days out and January stays only 23, in AirROI's data. Summer prices have to be right by spring.

Market figures are third party estimates for the period shown. They are not a promise of income. Your estimate is built from your home and its own comparable listings.

## The Hot Springs year

| When | What fills Hot Springs homes |
| - | - |
| November 27, 2026 into spring | Oaklawn live racing. The 2026 to 2027 meet opens November 27, the earliest opening day in the track's history, with a holiday stretch through January 10. |
| Spring 2027 | The Arkansas Derby, now set three weeks before the Kentucky Derby. |
| Saturday before Thanksgiving to New Year's Eve | Holiday Lights at Garvan Woodland Gardens. |
| March | Spring break. Occupancy peaks in March. |

| September | In the low group, along with January and February. |

## Two kinds of Hot Springs guest

### Lake guests

- Waterfront, a dock and room to park a boat.

- Sleeps 8 or more for family weekends.

- Kayaks, a fire pit and a deck at sunset in the first photos.

### Town guests

- A walk to Bathhouse Row and Central Avenue.

- Minutes to Oaklawn on race days.

- Couples looking for a spa weekend, with easy parking.

### What moves the rate

- A hot tub: $52,713 a year on average with one, $21,316 without. Only 19.4% of listings have one.

- A sauna: $71,257 with, in 1.3% of listings.

- Life size games: $80,022 with, in 2.4% of listings.

Compare [Broken Bow](https://listandhost.com/broken-bow/), where 86% of cabins have a hot tub and it no longer sets a home apart. In Hot Springs it still does.

AirROI compares listings with and without each feature, August 2025 to July 2026. It shows correlation, not a promise.

# Wimberley and Fredericksburg Airbnb Pricing

Source: https://listandhost.com/texas-hill-country/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Remote Airbnb pricing and co hosting for Wimberley and Fredericksburg homes. Local demand calendar, rates and amenity data. Get a free estimate.

Updated October 18, 2026

Wimberley and Fredericksburg are about 75 miles apart and book for different reasons. Wimberley guests come for Blue Hole, Jacob's Well and the creeks. Fredericksburg guests come for wineries, Main Street and Enchanted Rock. Both are weekend markets with a lot of competition. We offer remote pricing and listing work to Hill Country owners.

The average Fredericksburg, TX short term rental listed at $338 a night, booked 33% of its nights and took in about $37,095 in yearly revenue (AirROI public market data, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026, read October 16, 2026). A market average is not a promise of what your home will earn. We do not run full service here yet. Co hosting or remote pricing does. Remote pricing means our engine sets the nightly rates and minimum stays for a home in any US market while the owner keeps local cleaning and upkeep.

## Wimberley and Fredericksburg, side by side

AirROI estimates, August 2025 to July 2026.

| Town | Average nightly rate | Occupancy | Yearly revenue, average | Listings | Revenue in a year |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Wimberley | $335 | 33.8% | $36,211 | 638 | up 4.4% |
| Fredericksburg | $338 | 32.6% | $37,095 | 2,213 | down 5.4% |

| Season | Wimberley | Fredericksburg |
| - | - | - |
| Peak months | March, May, June: $358 a night, 39.1% booked | March, December, November: $352 a night, 41.2% booked |
| Low months | January, February, September: $300, 30.2% | January, February, September: $321, 29.9% |
| Booked ahead | 54 days on average | 45 days on average |
| Average stay | 2.8 nights | 2.6 nights |

Two towns, two calendars. Wimberley peaks with swimming season. Fredericksburg peaks in spring and again in November and December, when holiday shoppers fill Main Street. Both slow down in January, February and September.

Fredericksburg is crowded: 2,213 listings, and 42% of them are one bedroom places. BNBCalc puts Wimberley at $338 a night and 28% occupancy for the 12 months to September 2026, close to AirROI on rate and lower on occupancy.

Market figures are third party estimates for the period shown. They are not a promise of income. Your estimate is built from your home and its own comparable listings.

## What fills each town

| When | Wimberley | Fredericksburg |
| - | - | - |

| First Saturday of most months | Wimberley Market Days at Lions Field, about a mile from the square. | Main Street shops and wineries busy every weekend. |
| October | Fall weddings in the valley. | Oktoberfest on the first weekend of October, then the Fredericksburg Food and Wine Fest late in the month. |

- A dishwasher: $52,091 a year with, $25,774 without. Only 43% of listings have one.

- A game console: $77,883 with, in 0.8% of listings. Rare extras stand out in a crowded search.

## What Hill Country owners ask us

**Wimberley or Fredericksburg: which earns more?**

About the same on average over the past year: $36,211 in Wimberley and $37,095 in Fredericksburg, by AirROI's estimates. Wimberley revenue rose 4.4% while Fredericksburg fell 5.4%, and Fredericksburg has more than three times as many listings.

**How do I fill weeknights in the Hill Country?**

Weekends sell themselves. Sunday to Thursday is where most homes lose money. We price weeknights apart from weekends, lower minimum stays midweek, let short gaps sell and step unsold nights down on a schedule, never under your floor.

**When should I set holiday prices in Fredericksburg?**

Early. November and December are peak months there, and guests book about 45 days ahead on average. Holiday nights should carry their own price and minimum stay by early fall.

**Do you work with my local cleaner?**

Yes. In the Hill Country we work remotely: pricing, the listing and, with co hosting, guest messages. Your cleaner keeps the turnovers and your payouts stay with you.
