# Why Is My Airbnb Not Getting Booked? A Page One Check

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/why-is-my-airbnb-not-getting-booked/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Why your Airbnb is not getting booked: nine checks led by price against page one, with our own October 2026 numbers. Get a free estimate.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

Most of the time, an Airbnb is not getting booked because its total price sits above the homes guests see on page one for the same dates and group size. Check that first, then minimum stays and how much of the market is still open, and only then photos, title, reviews, response time, calendar sync and amenities. Below are all nine checks, with numbers from a live search around the glass house our team runs in the [Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/), including a weekend we priced too high. We run the same checks in [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/).

## The short answer: price against page one, then everything else

Guests type a place, dates and a guest count, then compare the totals on the first page. Airbnb says its search weighs your total price against other listings in the area for those dates, and that homes priced below comparable listings tend to rank higher. In the United States, guests see a total that includes fees, before taxes. So what matters is not your nightly rate but the total for the stay, fees included, next to the homes around it. Price is not the only reason a home sits empty, but it is the fastest to check and fix.

## Check 1: where your total sits among page one homes

On October 13, 2026 we searched Airbnb for Jasper, Arkansas, for 8 adults, and recorded every comparable home on page one for 12 stays. Eight are below.

| Stay, 8 guests | Homes still open | Comparable homes on page one | Lowest to highest total | Median total | Our glass house |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Fri Oct 16 to Sun Oct 18 | 5 of 149 (3%) | 4 | $844 to $1,054 | $915 | Booked |
| Fri Oct 23 to Sun Oct 25 | 9 of 149 (6%) | 8 | $381 to $1,054 | $649.50 | Booked |
| Tue Oct 27 to Thu Oct 29 | 66 of 149 (44%) | 16 | $505 to $1,722 | $962.50 | Booked |
| Fri Oct 30 to Sun Nov 1, Halloween | 52 of 149 (35%) | 13 | $682 to $1,600 | $975 | Open at $1,863 |
| Fri Nov 20, one night (Saturday booked) | 9 of 149 (6%) | 4 | $251 to $331 | $299.50 | Open at $944 |
| Wed Nov 25 to Sat Nov 28, Thanksgiving | 30 of 149 (20%) | 13 | $581 to $2,318 | $1,189 | Booked |
| Thu Dec 24 to Sun Dec 27, Christmas | 85 of 149 (57%) | 15 | $670 to $2,614 | $1,133 | Booked |
| Wed Dec 30 to Fri Jan 1, New Year | 81 of 149 (54%) | 16 | $516 to $1,728 | $947 | Booked |

Basis: our live Airbnb search for Jasper, Arkansas, October 13, 2026, entire homes for 8 adults, first page only. Comparable means 3 to 5 bedrooms with reviews. Totals are the stay totals the search showed, fees in, taxes out: asking prices, not bookings. Homes still open is Airbnb's count for the dates out of 149 homes with no dates set. Our glass house sleeps 10; its totals include a $225 cleaning fee and $35 a night for each guest past 6. Status as of October 13. Four stays booked or partly booked at our home are left out for space.

### Our own over priced weekend

We had Halloween weekend, Friday October 30 to Sunday November 1, at $749 a night. For 8 guests that came to $1,863: $1,498 for two nights, the $225 cleaning fee and $140 for guests 7 and 8. Seventeen days out, our total was above every comparable home on page one and almost double the $975 median, with 52 of 149 homes still open.

Why: the weekend runs into peak fall color, which a public foliage forecast puts around November 4, and two October weekends here had sold at $749 a night. But those were booked in August and September. A price that sold two months ahead is no proof it will sell 17 days ahead.

On October 16 we lowered both nights to $649. With the same fees that is $1,663 before any last minute discount, still above the highest page one total from October 13. On the morning of October 18 both nights were still open. Count fees the way guests do: a $225 cleaning fee adds $112.50 a night to a two night stay.

## Check 2: orphan nights and minimum stays

An orphan night is an open night a booking has cut off from its neighbors. Minimum stays can make it impossible to book, and fees can make it impossible to sell.

Our example is Friday, November 20. On September 16 a guest booked four nights starting that Saturday. The Friday could now sell only as one night, or as the end of a stay starting earlier in the week, yet it kept our two night weekend minimum, so for 20 days no guest could arrive that Friday. On October 6 our engine's gap rule cut its minimum to one night.

That fixed the rule, not the price. In our search for that single night, only 9 of 149 homes showed up, against 63 for the full weekend, a sign that most homes nearby want two nights on a Friday. Four comparable homes asked $251 to $331. Ours asked $944: $649 for the night, the full $225 cleaning fee and $70 for guests 7 and 8. Even at this home's $349 floor it would be $644. On October 18 the night was still open at $649.

- **Set a one night minimum on every true gap.** Our [dynamic pricing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/) shows the rule we run.

- **Look at the cleaning fee on short stays.** Airbnb lets hosts set a lower cleaning fee for stays of 1 or 2 nights. On our lone Friday the full fee was about a quarter of the total.

- **Offer the night to the guests next to it.** In October one guest at this house added the gap night before their arrival. Our [glass house case study](https://listandhost.com/results/buffalo-river-glass-house/) has the details.

- **Do not cut a whole weekend to sell one stranded night.** A big home alone on one night competes with smaller homes, and some single nights stay empty.

## Check 3: how much of the market is still open

Airbnb shows how many homes match a search. Run it with your dates and without to see what share of the market is still for sale.

- **Under 10 percent open.** On the two regular October weekends, 5 and 9 of 149 homes were open. Sensibly priced homes are selling. If yours is empty, look for what hides it: a minimum no guest can meet, a blocked night, a guest count set too low or a calendar that did not sync.

- **A third or more open.** Halloween weekend had 35 percent open and October 27 to 29 had 44 percent. With that many choices, price decides.

- **Far out.** About ten weeks ahead, 57 percent of homes were open for Christmas and 54 percent for New Year; six weeks ahead, 20 percent for Thanksgiving. A high share that far out is no reason to cut. Watch how fast it falls week to week.

Open homes also show what a date is worth: in peak color they asked a median of $962.50 for October 27 to 29, midweek, nearly the $975 of Halloween weekend.

And make sure the home really is slow. In AirROI's public data, the average listing in each of the 12 markets our [estimator](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) covers was booked 33 to 41 percent of nights from August 2025 to July 2026, and 37.3 percent across 180 listings in the Buffalo River region (read October 16, 2026). Compare your month with your market's month, not with a full calendar. Our glass house booked 68 of 92 nights from August through October 2026 (October as booked on October 16; 53 nights booked before our pricing engine took over on September 21), as our [results page](https://listandhost.com/results/) shows.

## Checks 4 to 9: the listing itself

If your total is inside the page one band and your minimums can be met, look at the listing.

### Check 4: photos

The first photo wins the click and the first five keep a guest looking. Lead with what sets the home apart, in daylight. Every photo must match the stay: accuracy is one of the six ratings Airbnb collects, and ratings feed ranking. Our [guest ready checklist](https://listandhost.com/blog/getting-a-home-guest-ready-checklist/) covers what to finish first.

### Check 5: title and first lines

Name the main feature, the setting and who the home suits, not a pile of keywords. Do not expect too much from it: when we checked the glass house's ranking in September 2026, reviews, the Guest Favorite badge and a price inside the band of nearby homes mattered, and the title did not.

### Check 6: reviews

A home with few reviews has to win on price until it earns them. Guest Favorite needs at least 5 reviews in the past 4 years, 1 of them in the past 2 years, plus strong ratings and reliability. Fix what guests repeat and never offer anything for a review, which Airbnb's policy forbids. Our glass house had a 4.9 rating from 11 reviews on October 16, 2026. More in our [ranking and Guest Favorite guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-ranking-and-guest-favorite/).

### Check 7: response time

Airbnb's response rate is the share of new inquiries and requests you answered within 24 hours over the past 30 days. For homes without Instant Book, Airbnb says search weighs how fast you respond, and it says instantly bookable homes may rank higher. Turn on Instant Book and answer in minutes. In October 2026 the glass house listing showed a 100 percent response rate.

### Check 8: calendar sync

Airbnb says linked calendars update every 3 hours, so a night can sell twice inside that window, and a host cancellation counts against ranking and badges. Also look for nights blocked by an old import or a forgotten hold. Our [Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-vs-vrbo-vs-booking-com-for-owners/) covers running more than one site.

### Check 9: amenities guests filter for

Airbnb's filters include Instant Book, Self check in, Allows pets, Guest favorites and amenity groups from wifi to parking. A home that has not ticked an amenity drops out of every search filtered for it, even if it has one. Guest count works the same way: a home set to sleep 6 never appears in an 8 guest search. Hot tub owners can start with our [hot tub guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/hot-tub-rentals-upkeep-and-earnings/).

## A weekly ten minute routine

1. **Minutes 1 to 4.** In a private window, search your next open weekend and one open midweek stay two to five weeks out. Note the median page one total and where yours sits.

2. **Minutes 5 and 6.** Note how many homes are still open, against last week.

3. **Minute 7.** Find orphan nights in the next 60 days and check each minimum stay.

4. **Minute 8.** Compare calendars across every site.

5. **Minutes 9 and 10.** Read new reviews and questions, and fix one thing.

Then decide. Above three quarters of page one with a third of the market open: move the price, never below your floor. Inside the band with the market nearly sold out: find what hides the home. Log the totals weekly, so you act on a trend.

## When to ask for an audit

Ask for a second look when the home still sits for two weeks at a price inside the page one band, when reviews keep naming the same problem, or when you do not have the ten minutes. Our [free listing audit](https://listandhost.com/free-listing-audit/) checks 12 points, pricing first, against nearby homes on your dates, by email within two business days, from your public listing alone.

To hand the work over, see our [services](https://listandhost.com/services/): full service in Fort Worth, Arlington, Dallas and the Buffalo River region is 20% of booking revenue (October 2026), and co hosting or remote pricing anywhere in the US is quoted in writing, as our [pricing page](https://listandhost.com/pricing/) explains. To see what the home should earn at the right price, [get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/). It is an estimate, not a promise of income.

## Questions hosts ask

**Why is my Airbnb getting views but no bookings?**

Views mean the home shows up in search. No bookings usually means it loses the comparison with the homes beside it, most often on total price, then photos or reviews.

**How long should I wait before lowering my price?**

If a third or more of comparable homes are still open two to three weeks out and your total is above most of page one, move now. If under 10 percent are open, price is rarely the problem. Keep a floor either way. Those are our thresholds, drawn from the October 13, 2026 search above.

**Does a lower price help my Airbnb ranking?**

Airbnb says homes priced below comparable listings in the area for the same dates tend to rank higher. Price is one factor among several, with quality, availability, Instant Book and response speed.

**Should I drop my minimum stay?**

On true gap nights, yes, to one night. Elsewhere a two night weekend minimum keeps a single Saturday booking from stranding the Friday. Make sure no rule leaves a night that no stay can reach.

**Sources:** [Airbnb Help Center: how search results work](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/39) · [Airbnb Help Center: pricing display in the United States](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3610) · [Airbnb Help Center: cleaning fees and the short stay cleaning fee](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/58) · [Airbnb Help Center: sync your calendar to other websites](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/99) · [Airbnb Help Center: response rate and response time](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/430) · [Airbnb Help Center: search filters](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3740) · [Airbnb Help Center: Guest favorites](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3495) · [Airbnb Help Center: reviews policy](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2673) · [AirROI: Jasper, Arkansas Airbnb data, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026](https://www.airroi.com/airbnb-data/united-states/arkansas/jasper) · [More Than Just Parks: Buffalo National River fall color forecast](https://morethanjustparks.com/foliage-tracker/arkansas/buffalo-national-river) · [Glass house case study, a home our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/buffalo-river-glass-house/)


# What Is a Good Occupancy Rate for an Airbnb in 2026?

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/what-is-a-good-occupancy-rate-for-airbnb/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: What is a good Airbnb occupancy rate in 2026? Average and top quarter rates for 12 markets, the US top 100 and revenue per open night. Free estimate.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

A good occupancy rate for an Airbnb in 2026 is one that beats the typical listing in your own market, not a national number. Across the 12 markets we track, the average listing booked 32.6% to 41.0% of its open nights from August 2025 to July 2026, and the top quarter booked about 46% to 62% or more, according to AirROI. But a full calendar at a cheap price can earn less than a half full one priced right, so this guide also sets occupancy beside revenue per open night and what the homes our team runs booked.

**Short answer.** Find your market's middle listing and its top quarter, then aim for the top quarter on both occupancy and revenue per open night. In AirROI's August 2025 to July 2026 data, that means roughly 50% of nights or more in most getaway markets and about 60% or more in Fort Worth and Dallas. If you book far more than that at a nightly rate below the middle listing's, your price is probably too low.

## Occupancy in 12 markets

Every market our estimator covers, from one source over the same twelve months:

| Market | Active listings | Average occupancy | Middle listing | Top quarter books at least | Top 10% books at least |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Fort Worth, TX | 1,607 | 41.0% | 43% | 62% | 77% |
| Dallas, TX | 4,675 | 38.4% | 38% | 59% | 76% |
| Buffalo River region, AR | 180 | 37.3% | 37% | 56% | 72% |
| Broken Bow, OK | 3,170 | 35.4% | 34% | 50% | 67% |
| Arlington, TX | 896 | 34.8% | 33% | 52% | 70% |
| Granbury, TX | 425 | 34.1% | 32% | 52% | 71% |
| Glen Rose, TX | 98 | 34.1% | 32% | 49% | 65% |
| Branson, MO | 3,085 | 33.9% | 32% | 52% | 68% |
| Hot Springs, AR | 1,428 | 33.8% | 33% | 51% | 67% |
| Wimberley, TX | 638 | 33.8% | 32% | 48% | 66% |
| Eureka Springs, AR | 835 | 33.6% | 33% | 51% | 67% |
| Fredericksburg, TX | 2,213 | 32.6% | 32% | 46% | 63% |

Basis: AirROI public market pages, August 2025 to July 2026, active listings, as shown October 18, 2026 (marked updated September 12, 2026). Occupancy is the share of available nights booked; middle listing is AirROI's median tier. The Buffalo River region row is AirROI's Jasper market. Glen Rose has only 98 listings, so its tiers are less steady. The Fort Worth, Dallas and Arlington years include the World Cup matches at the Arlington stadium, June 14 to July 14, 2026.

The averages sit in a narrow band, 8.4 points from top to bottom. The spread inside each market is far wider: in Fort Worth the bottom quarter averages 23% booked while the top quarter books 62% or more. Where a home lands depends on its market: 45% of nights is mid pack in Dallas but just under the top quarter in Fredericksburg. Fort Worth and Dallas lead, which fits what we see at the [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/) home our team runs: work trips, medical stays and events fill city weeknights, while cabin and lake markets lean on weekends and seasons.

## The national picture

AirROI's table of the 100 largest US markets by listings, updated September 12, 2026, averages 39.7% of nights booked at $315 a night. From the same table, the middle market books 40.3% and the middle nightly rate is about $302; weighted by listings, 39.9% and $317.

- **The range.** From 27.6% in Big Bear Lake, California, to 52.0% in Honolulu.

- **Half booked is rare.** Honolulu is the only market of the 100 averaging 50% or more. Thirteen average 45% or more, and 19 are under 35%.

- **High rates, fewer nights.** Park City, Utah has the top average night at $642 and books 30.3% of nights.

- **Texas.** Austin averages 40.0%, San Antonio 38.5%, Dallas 38.4%, Houston 36.1% and Galveston 31.2%.

Rules of thumb call 50% healthy, and AirROI's own FAQ on that page says so (page updated September 12, 2026). Yet 99 of its 100 biggest markets average less. Read 50% as a top quarter result in most places, not a typical one. The middle of our 12 markets, 34.1%, sits below the national middle because nine are getaway markets where weekends and seasons carry the year.

## Occupancy against revenue per open night

Revenue per open night is what a listing earns divided by every night it was open to book, booked or not. Data services call it RevPAR. It is roughly the nightly rate times the share of nights booked, so it measures both halves of the job.

| Market | Average occupancy | Average night | Revenue per open night, average | Revenue per open night, top quarter from |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Broken Bow, OK | 35.4% | $458 | $170 | $212 |
| Fredericksburg, TX | 32.6% | $338 | $118 | $149 |
| Wimberley, TX | 33.8% | $335 | $117 | $144 |
| Granbury, TX | 34.1% | $298 | $103 | $129 |
| Dallas, TX | 38.4% | $256 | $94 | $121 |
| Arlington, TX | 34.8% | $278 | $93 | $118 |
| Hot Springs, AR | 33.8% | $265 | $93 | $111 |
| Glen Rose, TX | 34.1% | $234 | $92 | $121 |
| Fort Worth, TX | 41.0% | $225 | $91 | $119 |
| Branson, MO | 33.9% | $251 | $91 | $105 |
| Buffalo River region, AR | 37.3% | $232 | $88 | $116 |
| Eureka Springs, AR | 33.6% | $215 | $76 | $98 |

Basis: AirROI public market pages, August 2025 to July 2026, all home sizes mixed, as shown October 18, 2026, rounded to the dollar. Average night is the average rate on booked nights.

Broken Bow books fewer nights than Fort Worth, 35.4% against 41.0%, yet earns nearly twice as much per open night: $170 against $91. Fort Worth ranks first of the 12 on occupancy and ties for ninth on revenue per open night; Fredericksburg ranks last on occupancy and second on revenue. Big cabins do not need to book as many nights: AirROI's April 2026 cabin study put Broken Bow 4 bedroom cabins at $575 a night.

The same math works inside one home. In a made up example, a 3 bedroom could book 70% of nights at $150 or 50% at $230. The first earns $105 per open night, the second $115 with 73 fewer booked nights a year, so less wear and fewer cleanings. That is why our pricing aims at revenue per open night, as [dynamic pricing explained](https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/) shows.

## Why data services disagree on occupancy

The same market can look very different from one data site to the next.

| Market | Source | Period | Listings counted | Occupancy |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Fort Worth | AirROI | Aug 2025 to Jul 2026 | 1,607 | 41.0% average, about 43% middle listing |
| Fort Worth | Airbtics | Sep 2025 to Aug 2026 | 1,765 | 61% |
| Broken Bow | Rabbu | Twelve months to Apr 27, 2026 | 1,930, Airbnb only | 25% |
| Broken Bow | AirROI | Aug 2025 to Jul 2026 | 3,170 | 35.4% |
| Broken Bow | BNBCalc | Twelve months to Sep 2026 | 5,225, Airbnb and Vrbo | 34% in its summary, 36% in its overview |

Basis: each public page as shown October 18, 2026. Rabbu's figures come from its page summary, because the page blocked our direct read.

No service sees an owner's booking records. Each estimates from what listings show in public and makes different choices:

- **Blocked nights.** AirDNA's help center says it divides booked nights by nights not blocked, and counts a listing only with a reservation in the past 28 days. That pushes the rate up; counting every listed night pulls it down.

- **Which listings.** Airbnb alone or with Vrbo and Booking.com, 30 night only homes, part time listings.

- **Average or median.** AirROI's Fort Worth average is 41.0%; its middle listing books about 43%.

- **Which months.** A year ending July 2026 carries the World Cup summer in DFW. One ending April 2026 does not.

So compare your home with one service's numbers for the same period, never one site's average beside another's top quarter. For your own home, divide nights booked by nights you were open to book.

## When high occupancy means the price is too low

A calendar that fills fast can mean guests found a bargain. Three signs:

- **Your best nights sell weeks ahead** while similar homes stay open at higher prices.

- **The market sells out around you.** On October 13, 2026, our weekly comp check found only 7 of 214 similar homes near the Fort Worth home our team runs (3 bedrooms or more, sleeping 6) still open for the weekend of October 23, and 24 of 214 for November 13. Ours had sold both weekends weeks earlier, at about $209 and $248 a night. We raised 23 future weekend nights that day.

- **You book more than your market's top 10% at a rate below its middle listing's.** In Fort Worth, that is over 77% of nights at under about $165, AirROI's median rate for the same months.

Our estimator never assumes more than 85% of nights booked; its high cases run about 36% to 51% by market and size. Past 85% there is little room for repairs or owner stays, and the busiest nights are probably underpriced.

Some high occupancy at a low rate is on purpose. The cabin loft our team runs went live September 24, 2026 at $89 on weeknights and $149 on weekends until it has three reviews, and booked 16 of 31 October nights as of October 16. A 30 night stay at a lower rate can fill a slow January with one booking; see our [guide to 30 night stays](https://listandhost.com/blog/traveling-nurse-30-night-stays-fort-worth/).

Low occupancy can point the other way. At that cabin no weekend night sold at $169; on October 7 we cut October 23 and 24 to $149, and both booked within a week. The fix both ways is pricing by the night: event floors set early, weekends priced on their own, quiet weeknights stepping toward a floor. Our [DFW weekend and event pricing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-pricing-strategy-dfw-weekends-and-events/) walks through it.

## What the homes our team runs book

| Home and month | Nights booked | Share of nights | Average night | Revenue per open night |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Fort Worth 3 bedroom, August 2026 | 12 of 31 | 39% | $217 | $84 |
| Fort Worth 3 bedroom, September 2026 | 20 of 30 | 67% | $169 | $113 |
| Fort Worth 3 bedroom, October 2026, booked to date | 24 of 31 | 77% | $169 | $131 |
| Glass house, August 2026 | 16 of 31 | 52% | $455 | $235 |
| Glass house, September 2026 | 25 of 30 | 83% | $306 | $255 |
| Glass house, October 2026, booked to date | 27 of 31 | 87% | $502 | $437 |
| Cabin loft, October 2026, booked to date | 16 of 31 | 52% | $97 | $50 |

Basis: our booking records as of October 16, 2026. Average night is what guests paid per night after discounts, before cleaning fees, taxes and platform fees. Revenue per open night is average night times nights booked, divided by nights in the month. October figures are booked, not earned. The glass house's 2 blocked September nights count as unbooked. Our engine took over its prices September 21, 2026, after most of those nights were booked.

- **Fort Worth: more nights was the right trade.** Occupancy rose from 39% to 77% as the average night fell from $217 to $169, and revenue per open night still rose from $84 to $131, because quiet weeknights now sell near a $149 floor. Weekends were the exception, as the comp check showed.

- **Glass house: same occupancy, different months.** September and October booked 83% and 87%, yet October brought $437 per open night against $255, with peak fall color and higher rates.

From August through October the Fort Worth home booked 61% of nights, just under the 62% top quarter line for Fort Worth, and the glass house 74%, above the 72% top 10% line for the [Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/). Three fall months are not a year, so read this as a record, not a forecast. The method is on our [results page](https://listandhost.com/results/), with pages for the [Fort Worth home](https://listandhost.com/results/fort-worth-home/), the [glass house](https://listandhost.com/results/buffalo-river-glass-house/) and the [cabin loft](https://listandhost.com/results/ozark-cabin-loft/).

We run homes with full service in Fort Worth, [Arlington](https://listandhost.com/arlington/), [Dallas](https://listandhost.com/dallas/) and the Buffalo River region, and offer co hosting or remote pricing in places like [Broken Bow](https://listandhost.com/broken-bow/) and the [Texas Hill Country](https://listandhost.com/texas-hill-country/). See our [services](https://listandhost.com/services/) and [pricing](https://listandhost.com/pricing/).

## Questions owners ask

**What is a good occupancy rate for an Airbnb?**

One that beats the middle listing in your market on both occupancy and revenue per open night. In AirROI's August 2025 to July 2026 data, the top quarter booked at least 46% to 62% of nights across our 12 markets.

**What is the average Airbnb occupancy rate in the US?**

In AirROI's 100 largest US markets, the middle market books 40.3% of nights, and AirROI's own average is 39.7% (page updated September 12, 2026).

**Is 50% occupancy good for an Airbnb?**

In most of our markets, yes: it is at or within 2 points of the top quarter line in nine of the 12. Fort Worth (62%), Dallas (59%) and the Buffalo River region (56%) set the bar higher. AirROI data, August 2025 to July 2026.

**Can an Airbnb occupancy rate be too high?**

Yes. Booking more nights than your market's top 10% while charging less than its middle listing usually means guests are getting a bargain.

**Does occupancy count blocked nights?**

It depends on who is counting. AirDNA's help center says it leaves blocked nights out. For your own home, divide nights booked by nights you were open to book.

**Want to know what good looks like for your home?** [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/#estimator) with low, likely and high cases for nights booked, nightly rate and yearly bookings, and the basis for every number. It is an estimate, not a promise.

# Vacasa, Evolve or a Local Manager? Fees and Facts, 2026

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/vacasa-evolve-or-a-local-manager/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Vacasa and Evolve owner fees as each published them on October 18, 2026, what each fee is taken from, and who keeps your listing and reviews if you leave.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

Before you compare percentages, compare two other things: what each fee is taken from, and whose account holds your listing if you ever leave. As of October 18, 2026, Evolve publishes 10% or 15% of each stay’s rent plus cleaning and pet fees, Vacasa publishes no rate and quotes each home, and our full service fee is 20% of nightly rent plus extra guest fees, after the platform’s host fee and never on cleaning fees.

We are one of the choices in this guide, so we have a stake in your answer. Every figure about another company is its own published claim, read October 18, 2026 unless another date is given, and linked below. We cover fees, terms and listings only, not anyone’s service.

**Short answer.** Line up three things from every quote: the rate, the base and who holds the listing. On a 3 bedroom Fort Worth home in our estimator’s likely case, Evolve’s 15% plan and our 20% land $150 to $717 apart, and which costs less depends on how many cleaning fees the year holds. The bigger difference comes when you leave: a listing in your own account keeps its reviews.

## What changed at Vacasa in 2025

Casago, a vacation rental manager built on a franchise model, bought Vacasa. The purchase closed on April 30, 2025, at $5.30 a share, according to Vacasa’s SEC filing dated May 1, 2025 and Short Term Rentalz. The brand continues as Vacasa, a Casago company (VRMA Arrival, May 5, 2025). Two later facts matter more to an owner:

- **Your agreement.** Casago’s page for Vacasa owners says the merger closing does not change the management agreement, and homes stay on the same booking sites.

- **Who runs your market.** On August 21, 2026, Short Term Rentalz reported that Casago had sold all former Vacasa markets. They are now led by local franchise owners, destination based businesses or larger regional managers, with the last handovers due in September 2026.

If your home is with Vacasa today, ask who your agreement is with now, whose accounts hold your listings, and whether the fee or notice changed in the handover.

## What Vacasa publishes about owner fees

As of October 18, 2026, Vacasa does not publish a rate. Its fee page says its management fees are “tailored for each unique vacation rental property,” and its owner FAQ says the fee depends on the home’s location, number of bedrooms and guest amenities, with a quote from a local market expert.

- **The range on the page is the industry’s.** The fee page tells owners to expect 10% to 50% of revenue across vacation rental managers, not as Vacasa’s own rate.

- **Fee base.** Neither page says what the fee is taken from. Ask for it in one written sentence.

- **One owner fee, plus guest fees.** Vacasa describes one management fee for its core services. Guests pay a booking fee, a cleaning fee, pet and hot tub fees where they apply, and a damage waiver of up to $25 a night in most markets.

- **Notice.** The FAQ says you can cancel at any time with 90 days notice, and that stays already booked in that 90 day window are kept.

## What Evolve publishes, and what stays with the owner

Evolve publishes its plans, as read October 18, 2026: Core at 10%, Plus at 15% and Pro at a custom rate set by how many homes you have, with a one time onboarding fee of $250 plus $25 for each added property. Its FAQ says the fee is charged after guests check in, on each reservation’s base rate plus additional fees such as cleaning or pet fees, with taxes left out. Those pages do not mention platform fees, so ask whether the base is before or after them. What stays with you, by Evolve’s own description:

- **Cleaners.** Evolve connects you with local cleaning partners, or you use your own. You agree the price and pay them from the guest cleaning fee, and Evolve coordinates the schedule.

- **Help at the door.** During stays, on the ground support comes from a Guest Contact you choose.

- **Your old listings.** Evolve’s help center says listings you already had must be hidden or removed before your Evolve listing launches, as its agreement requires. It does not say whose account the new listing sits in.

Evolve says there are no long term contracts, and offers a refund of the first six months of management fees, requested between day 180 and day 210, with conditions. We found no notice period on the pages we read.

## The published numbers side by side

| Company | Published owner fee | What it is taken from, as published | Setup | Notice to leave |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Vacasa | Not published. Quoted per home | Not stated | Not stated | 90 days. Stays booked in that window are kept |
| Evolve | Core 10%, Plus 15%, Pro custom | Base rate plus additional fees such as cleaning or pet fees. Taxes left out | $250, plus $25 per added property | No long term contract. No notice period found |
| Awning | Essential 10% to 15%, Full Service 18% to 25% | Revenue, not defined further on its city pages | No setup fees | 90 days |
| List & Host | 20%, full service | Nightly rent plus extra guest fees, after the platform’s host fee. Never cleaning fees or taxes | None | quoted in writing after a free look |

Basis: each company’s own pages, read October 18, 2026, except Awning’s plan ranges, which come from its fee guide updated October 1, 2026. Ours are on our [pricing page](https://listandhost.com/pricing/).

## Tech led local models, Awning style

Some newer managers sell city by city from one national platform, with plan tiers and a low starting rate. Awning is one. Its Fort Worth and Dallas pages carry “From 10%” in the title, and their FAQ says full service starts at 10% of monthly revenue, depending on property type, location and services. Another line on the same pages says 15%, and a comparison table shows 5%. The FAQ lists no setup fees and 90 days notice to cancel. Its fee guide, updated October 1, 2026, lists Essential at 10% to 15% and Full Service at 18% to 25%.

A starting rate belongs to the smallest plan, so ask which plan covers cleaning, repairs and restocking, and how the agreement defines revenue. Awning’s own guide shows why: on $60,000 a year at 20%, taking the fee before or after Airbnb’s 15.5% host fee moves the cost by $1,860. Would rather keep the hands on work? Compare [a co host and a property manager](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-co-host-vs-property-manager/).

## What one home pays under each published base

Here are the published rates on their own bases, run on one home: our estimator’s likely case for a 3 bedroom in Fort Worth. That is $250 a night with 42.4% of nights booked, about 155 nights and $38,750 in nightly rent a year, plus a $170 cleaning fee per stay (AirROI market data, August 2025 to July 2026, read October 16, 2026). Stay length sets how many cleaning fees the year holds, so we show 6.8 nights, the Fort Worth average in AirROI’s data for those months, and 2.7 nights, the average at the Fort Worth home our team runs near Dickies Arena (every stay booked through June 2027, as of October 16, 2026). Event runs bring short stays, such as the NCHA Futurity, November 16 to December 12, 2026, and the 2027 Stock Show, January 15 to February 6.

| Rate and base, as published | 6.8 night stays: 23 stays, $3,910 in cleaning fees | 2.7 night stays: 57 stays, $9,690 in cleaning fees |
| - | - | - |
| Evolve Core: 10% of rent plus cleaning fees | $4,266 | $4,844 |
| Evolve Plus: 15% of rent plus cleaning fees | $6,399 | $7,266 |
| Awning Full Service: 18% to 25%, base not defined, shown on rent before platform fees | $6,975 to $9,688 | $6,975 to $9,688 |
| List & Host: 20% of rent after Airbnb’s 15.5% host fee | $6,549 | $6,549 |

Basis: each company’s published rate and base, read October 18, 2026, as if every stay came through Airbnb, whose single fee is 15.5% for most hosts (Airbnb Help Center, read October 18, 2026). An illustration, not a forecast for any home. The rows do not buy the same work: Evolve’s plans leave hiring and paying cleaners with you, Awning lists two plans at different rates, and our fee is full service.

## What a local team does differently

Hold us to the same facts. Our proof is the homes our team runs, and every number on our [results page](https://listandhost.com/results/) says how it was counted.

- **Your listing stays in your account.** We join it as your host team, so the reviews and booking history stay yours. The platforms pay you directly, and your statement arrives by the 10th.

- **One base, written down.** 20% of nightly rent plus extra guest fees, after the platform’s host fee. No setup fee, and repairs and supplies at cost with receipts.

- **Prices checked every day.** Our own engine reviews the next 12 months each morning, inside a floor you approve. From September 21 to October 16, 2026, it logged 133 nightly price changes and 52 minimum stay changes across the homes our team runs. On October 13, 2026, a check of nearby homes found three open stays at our Fort Worth home 11% to 25% under the comparable median, and we raised them that day.

- **Full service only where we have people.** Full service in Fort Worth, the rest of Dallas Fort Worth and the Buffalo River region of Arkansas. Co hosting or remote pricing anywhere else in the United States. See [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/), [Arlington](https://listandhost.com/arlington/), [Dallas](https://listandhost.com/dallas/) and the [Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/), and every option on our [services page](https://listandhost.com/services/).

We are a small team with a short record. If you own homes in several states and want one company for all of them, a national manager may suit you better. Our page on [a local team vs national managers](https://listandhost.com/compare/national-managers/) shows who fits each.

## Leaving any manager: listing, reviews, future bookings

The exit is harder to compare than the fee, and it decides what you keep. Airbnb’s help center says there is no way to transfer an account to a different host, and reservations cannot be moved to a new host or account. So the account that holds your listing keeps its reviews and future bookings. Vacasa’s own guide for owners who sell says neither Airbnb nor Vrbo lets a host transfer a listing, though you can ask to have reviews moved, and guests asked to rebook on a new listing may not.

Notice, as published: Vacasa 90 days, with stays booked in that window kept; Awning 90 days; Evolve none found. Ours is quoted in writing after a free look, and stays already booked past the end date are honored.

Before you sign with anyone, get in writing:

1. Whose account holds the listing on Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com and any direct booking site.

2. What happens to the reviews when you leave, platform by platform.

3. Who hosts, and who is paid for, stays booked past the end date.

4. The notice in days, how it must be sent, and any fee to leave early.

5. Whether your current listing must come down first, and what happens to its bookings.

Our [15 questions to ask an Airbnb manager](https://listandhost.com/blog/questions-to-ask-an-airbnb-manager/) cover the rest, and our [guide to management fees](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-management-fees/) compares two full quotes line by line.

## Questions owners ask

**Does Vacasa publish its management fee?**

No. As of October 18, 2026, Vacasa quotes each home, with a fee based on location, bedrooms and guest amenities. The 10% to 50% range on its fee page describes vacation rental managers in general, not its own rate.

**What does Evolve charge owners in 2026?**

As published on October 18, 2026: Core at 10%, Plus at 15% and Pro at a custom rate, plus a one time $250 onboarding fee and $25 for each added property. The fee is taken from the base rate plus fees such as cleaning or pet fees, with taxes left out.

**Is Vacasa still Vacasa after the Casago deal?**

The brand continues as a Casago company. The purchase closed on April 30, 2025, and on August 21, 2026 Short Term Rentalz reported that Casago had sold all former Vacasa markets to local franchise owners and other operators.

**Do I keep my reviews if I leave a manager?**

Only if the listing sits in your own account. Airbnb says accounts cannot be transferred to a different host and reservations cannot move to a new account. If the manager's account holds the listing, plan on starting a new one.

**Is a lower percentage always cheaper?**

No. The base matters as much as the rate. On our Fort Worth example, 15% of rent plus cleaning fees cost $150 less than 20% of rent after Airbnb's host fee when stays averaged 6.8 nights, and $717 more when they averaged 2.7 nights (published rates read October 18, 2026).

**Start with your own number.** [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) for your home, with the basis for every figure. Then run each quote’s rate on its own base, the way the table above does. It is an estimate, not a promise of income.

# Short Term Rental Management in Dallas and Arlington, 2026

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/dallas-arlington-short-term-rental-management/
Updated: 2026-10-19
Summary: Dallas and Arlington short term rental management: stadium and long stay demand, neighborhoods, dated revenue ranges, costs and how we run it.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026 · Updated October 19, 2026

Short term rental management in Dallas and Arlington means a local team runs the pricing, guest messages, cleaning and repairs for your home in exchange for a share of booking revenue; our full service fee is 20%, with no setup fee. Three data services put the average or median listing in the two cities at about $24,000 to $41,000 a year in booking revenue, for periods between August 2025 and September 2026, with Arlington's best nights tied to AT&T Stadium and Globe Life Field and Dallas filled by longer work, medical and family stays.

Every figure below says where it came from and when. The service pages are [Airbnb property management in Dallas](https://listandhost.com/dallas/) and [Airbnb management in Arlington](https://listandhost.com/arlington/). For Arlington income by bedroom count, see [how much an Airbnb makes in Arlington](https://listandhost.com/blog/how-much-does-an-airbnb-make-in-arlington-tx/); for Fort Worth, our [Fort Worth Airbnb management guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-airbnb-management-owner-guide/).

**Short answer.** The gap inside each city is far bigger than the gap between them. In AirROI's data for August 2025 to July 2026, the top quarter of listings booked about $4,200 a month in both cities, against about $2,300 for the median listing. Pricing, photos, reviews and fast answers make most of that difference, and those are the parts a manager runs.

## Dallas and Arlington by the numbers

Each service counts listings, blocked nights and revenue its own way, so read these as a range, not one true number.

| City | Source | Period | Listings | Occupancy | Nightly rate | Yearly revenue |
| - | - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Dallas | AirROI | Aug 2025 to Jul 2026 | 4,675 | 38.4% | $256 average | $24,382 average |
| Dallas | Airbtics | Sep 2025 to Aug 2026 | 4,702 | 59% | $182 | about $41,000 |
| Dallas | GuestFavorites | Jan to Sep 2026 | 4,549 | 54% | $200 | $39,712 |
| Arlington | AirROI | Aug 2025 to Jul 2026 | 896 | 34.8% | $278 average | $25,379 average |
| Arlington | GuestFavorites | Jan to Sep 2026, updated Oct 16 | 1,005 | 45% | $234 | $38,533 |

AirROI averages every listing, including homes that sit empty most of the year; the other two lean toward the typical listing. GuestFavorites also prints a lower typical figure in its own text, $24,183 for Dallas and $23,073 for Arlington, so treat the top of the range with care. We read every page on October 17, 2026.

Supply is growing fast. AirROI counts 37.7% more Dallas listings and 47.1% more Arlington listings than a year earlier (August 2025 to July 2026), and Airbtics counts 76% more in Dallas (September 2025 to August 2026). More homes are chasing the same guests, and the homes priced and presented well take a bigger share.

## The spread inside each city

| AirROI tier | Dallas per month | Dallas occupancy | Dallas nightly rate | Arlington per month | Arlington occupancy | Arlington nightly rate |
| - | - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Bottom quarter | $1,088 | 20% | $120 | $1,113 | 18% | $109 |
| Median | $2,309 | 38% | $187 | $2,291 | 33% | $196 |
| Top quarter | $4,209 | 59% | $302 | $4,218 | 52% | $337 |
| Top 10% | $6,957 and up | 76% and up | $466 and up | $7,108 and up | 70% and up | $529 and up |

Basis: AirROI revenue per listing per month, August 2025 to July 2026. A top quarter Dallas listing booked close to double the median by selling more nights at a higher price, and Arlington looks almost the same. Same stadiums, same airports: what separates those rows is mostly operation.

## What drives demand in Arlington

Arlington books on the event calendar. AT&T Stadium, Globe Life Field, Texas Live! and Six Flags Over Texas sit within a few miles of each other, and the city counts 16.5 million visitors a year (City of Arlington, July 28, 2026). The stadium sits between downtown Dallas and downtown Fort Worth, so a big game fills homes across the area.

- **AT&T Stadium.** Eight Cowboys regular season home games in 2026, plus the Big 12 Championship and the Cotton Bowl Classic. In June and July 2026 it hosted nine World Cup matches, 631,843 fans in all, per the city.

- **Globe Life Field.** The Rangers play 81 home games in 2027, opening at home on Thursday, April 1, per the schedule released July 16, 2026. Baseball's labor agreement expires December 1, 2026, and CBS Sports reported on October 8 that a work stoppage is widely expected, so treat 2027 dates as provisional.

- **Six Flags Over Texas and UT Arlington.** Summer family trips, and graduation weekends in May and December.

June 2026 set the city's hotel record, $31 million in room revenue, against the old mark of $23.6 million from November 2024, a football month (same city release). In AirROI's data for August 2025 to July 2026, the peak months were June, July and November, at $408 a night on average, and the low months January, February and April, at $195. Guests booked 41 days ahead on average. June stays averaged 3.4 nights, against 5.3 in March: event crowds book short stays. Plan 2027 on a normal football and baseball year.

| Date | Event | Venue |
| - | - | - |
| Sun Nov 1, 2026 | Cowboys vs Cardinals | AT&T Stadium |
| Sun Nov 15 | Cowboys vs 49ers | AT&T Stadium |
| Sun Nov 22 | Cowboys vs Titans | AT&T Stadium |
| Thu Nov 26 | Thanksgiving, Cowboys vs Eagles | AT&T Stadium |
| Fri Dec 4 | Big 12 Championship | AT&T Stadium |
| Sun Dec 27 | Cowboys vs Jaguars, night game | AT&T Stadium |
| Fri Jan 1, 2027 | Cotton Bowl Classic, a playoff quarterfinal | AT&T Stadium |
| Sun Jan 3, 2027 | Cowboys vs Giants | AT&T Stadium |
| Apr 1 to 8, 2027 | Rangers home opener vs Athletics, then Tampa Bay | Globe Life Field |

Read from the official schedules on October 17, 2026. Check each date again before you price it.

## What drives demand in Dallas

Dallas books on long stays, with big weekends on top. Visit Dallas counted more than 27.7 million visitors in 2024.

- **Work, moves and medical stays.** The average stay was 5.9 nights, booked 30 days ahead (AirROI, August 2025 to July 2026). Relocations, project work, the Southwestern Medical District, Love Field and DFW Airport fill weeknights all year.

- **The State Fair of Texas.** 2,020,064 visitors in 2025. The busiest day was Saturday, October 11, Texas vs OU weekend, with 193,960, per the fair's own count.

- **Arena nights.** Mavericks and Stars games and concerts at American Airlines Center, fall through spring.

- **Seasons.** AirROI's peak months were June, March and December, at $295 a night on average, and the low months January, February and September, at $206.

Dallas is the bigger pond, with about five times Arlington's listings in AirROI's count for August 2025 to July 2026. But only 29.3% of them have 3 or more bedrooms, against 40.1% in Arlington, so a family sized Dallas home faces a smaller slice of that supply.

## Neighborhoods guests search for

These areas show up in guest searches and in the data services. They describe demand, not a promise for any street.

- **Uptown, Deep Ellum and Bishop Arts, Dallas.** AirROI names them the top Dallas neighborhoods. Restaurants and nightlife draw couples and friend trips, mostly on weekends.

- **Lower Greenville, the Medical District and near Love Field, Dallas.** Week long work and medical stays, where a desk, fast wifi and a washer matter more than a pool.

- **The Entertainment District, Arlington.** On October 17, 2026, Google suggested "near AT&T Stadium", "near Six Flags" and "near Globe Life Field" for Arlington Airbnb searches, so the title, the first photo and the drive time to the gate carry the listing.

- **Around UT Arlington.** Graduations and campus visits, close to the stadiums without game day traffic at the door.

Google also suggested "with pool" for both cities that day.

## What a nearby home our team runs shows

To be plain: our team does not run a home in Dallas or Arlington yet. The nearest is a 3 bedroom in west Fort Worth that sleeps 8, live since July 2026, so these results are labeled Fort Worth.

- **Weekends and weeknights are two businesses.** From August through October 2026, Friday and Saturday nights averaged $236 and weeknights $139, after discounts, before cleaning and platform fees. Weekend stays were booked a median of 44 days ahead; weeknight only stays, 1 day ahead.

- **A game day across town is not a game day next door.** On Thursday, October 8, 2026, the Cowboys played a night game at AT&T Stadium. We priced that night at $449. Unsold five days out, it stepped to $249, then $199, and sold the day before. A home near the stadium can hold a price longer; a home across the metro should not count on it.

- **Steady months build.** It booked 12 of 31 nights in August, 20 of 30 in September and 24 of 31 in October, with payouts of $3,124, $3,840 and $4,742 after platform fees, cleaning fee included. October is booked, not earned, as of October 16, 2026.

It is rated 4.9 on Airbnb from 14 reviews, and another home our team runs, a glass house in the Buffalo River region, is a Guest Favorite rated 4.9, both read October 16, 2026. See the [Fort Worth home results](https://listandhost.com/results/fort-worth-home/) and all [results from homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/). Past results are not a promise of what your home will earn.

## How we run a Dallas or Arlington home

Full service in Fort Worth, the rest of Dallas Fort Worth and the Buffalo River region of Arkansas. Co hosting or remote pricing anywhere else in the United States. In Dallas and Arlington we take a home wherever we can staff a vetted local cleaning team.

1. **Estimate, then a [free look](https://listandhost.com/services/#free-look).** We price your home against the listings it competes with on the same dates, then send the fee, term and setup list in writing before you sign.

2. **Launch.** A listing written for how guests search, a photo shoot we direct, a smart lock, and the home live on Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com on one calendar. Setup items are billed at cost after you approve the list.

3. **Pricing every day.** A rate for every night a year out, inside a floor you approve. Games, the fair and big concerts get their own prices and minimum stays once confirmed. Open nights step down on a schedule as the date nears, never under the floor, and every change is read back from the channel. Why event nights so often sell too cheap is in our [DFW weekend and event pricing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-pricing-strategy-dfw-weekends-and-events/).

4. **Guests.** Every message, check in steps, house rules and quiet hours that keep neighbors on your side.

5. **Cleaning and repairs.** Local cleaners with a checklist and photos. Repairs over your limit come to you with a quote first.

6. **Reporting.** A monthly statement for your home by the 10th, with payouts, costs and every stay by check in date. An [online view](https://listandhost.com/owner-dashboard/) with nights booked ahead, upcoming stays and open nights is being built. Block dates for yourself at any time.

Keeping your listing and cleaner? See co hosting on our [services page](https://listandhost.com/services/), and how our engine sets a price in the [dynamic pricing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/).

## What the top quarter does differently

1. **Event nights priced early.** Two night minimums on big weekends and floors that automatic discounts cannot slide. Our [event weekend playbook](https://listandhost.com/blog/stock-show-and-dickies-arena-weekends-for-hosts/) shows how we do it in Fort Worth.

2. **A home built for its guest.** Arlington groups want a bed for everyone and parking for several cars; the average Arlington listing sleeps 5.3 (AirROI, August 2025 to July 2026). Dallas work guests want a desk, a washer and a full kitchen.

3. **Reviews near perfect.** The average Arlington listing is rated 4.76, and 36.8% carry Guest Favorite (AirROI, August 2025 to July 2026). See [how Guest Favorite works](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-ranking-and-guest-favorite/).

4. **Long stays on purpose.** Many Arlington hosts have already gone monthly: 41.9% of listings in AirROI's data accept only stays of 30 nights or longer. That thins the field on game weekends and crowds the long stay market. Our [guide to 30 night stays](https://listandhost.com/blog/traveling-nurse-30-night-stays-fort-worth/) covers pricing them.

5. **Fast answers on every channel.** Weeknight guests book late, and Vrbo and Booking.com reach guests Airbnb does not ([which booking sites fit your home](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-vs-vrbo-vs-booking-com-for-owners/)).

## Hire a manager or run it yourself?

If you live close and enjoy guests, running it yourself keeps the fee; if not, the fee buys back the hours and the pricing work. Our [side by side comparison](https://listandhost.com/compare/self-managing/) lays out both. Ask any manager who sets prices, whether the fee touches cleaning fees, whether payouts come to you, and who keeps the listing if you part ways; our [15 questions to ask an Airbnb manager](https://listandhost.com/blog/questions-to-ask-an-airbnb-manager/) go further. Our [guide to Airbnb management fees](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-management-fees/) shows what is normal in 2026.

## Questions owners ask

**What does short term rental management cost in Dallas and Arlington?**

Our full service fee is 20% of booking revenue, with no setup fee. Booking revenue is the nightly rent plus any extra guest fees, after the platform's host fee. Taxes and cleaning fees are not part of it. Repairs and supplies are billed at cost with receipts.

**How much does an Airbnb make in Dallas or Arlington?**

Data services put the average or median Dallas listing at $24,382 to about $41,000 a year and Arlington at $25,379 to $38,533, for periods between August 2025 and September 2026 (AirROI, Airbtics, GuestFavorites). Arlington's figures include the 2026 World Cup summer, so a normal year may land lower.

**Is Dallas or Arlington better for a short term rental?**

They are different businesses. Dallas runs on steady work and medical stays booked about 30 days ahead; Arlington runs on the stadium calendar, booked about 41 days ahead (AirROI, August 2025 to July 2026). A big home with parking near the stadiums fits Arlington; a well equipped home near Uptown or the Medical District fits Dallas.

**Will a home near AT&T Stadium book every game?**

No. Each game is its own market. On October 8, 2026, a Cowboys home game night, our Fort Worth home started at $449 and sold the day before at $199. We set a price and minimum stay for each date, then step unsold nights down, never under your floor.

**Do you already run homes in Dallas or Arlington?**

We offer full service in both from our Fort Worth base. Today the homes our team runs are in Fort Worth and the Buffalo River region of Arkansas, and we publish their results rather than claim Dallas or Arlington ones we do not have.

# Ozark Cabin Rental Management: The Buffalo River Guide

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/ozark-cabin-rental-management-buffalo-river/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: How to run a cabin rental in the Buffalo River region and the Ozarks: seasons, what guests book, remote upkeep and dated numbers. Get a free estimate.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

Running a cabin rental in the Buffalo River region comes down to three jobs: price a short peak season well, sell what guests can count on every day, and keep a dependable local team on call for a home you may live hours away from. October, May and June carry the year here, and hot tubs, trails, dark skies and elk sell a cabin far more reliably than the river does. Here is how it works, with market data and dated numbers from the two homes our team runs in the region. For our own service there, see [Buffalo River cabin management](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/).

**Short answer.** In AirROI's data for the Jasper area, the average short term rental earned $26,695 from August 2025 to July 2026, with 37.3% of nights booked at an average of $232. The top quarter of listings brought in $3,767 a month, against $2,153 for the middle listing. Much of that gap comes down to the home and how it is run: a hot tub, strong reviews, prices set every day, and a local cleaner who never misses a turnover.

## The Ozark market in numbers

The Buffalo River region is small next to the better known Ozark towns, but its average listing earns as much or more.

| Market | Active listings | Average night | Nights booked | Average listing, a year |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Buffalo River region, AR (Jasper area) | 180 | $232 | 37.3% | $26,695 |
| Eureka Springs, AR | 835 | $215 | 33.6% | $23,139 |
| Branson, MO | 3,085 | $251 | 33.9% | $25,747 |

Basis: AirROI public market data, August 2025 to July 2026, read October 17, 2026. Averages across all home sizes, and many listings are not open every night. A market average is not a promise of what any home will earn.

Three more figures from AirROI's Jasper area data, same period:

- **The spread is wide.** The top quarter of listings earned $3,767 a month and the top tenth at least $5,916, against $2,153 for the middle listing.

- **Great reviews are the norm.** The average rating is 4.92, and 77.2% of listings carry Airbnb's Guest Favorite badge. The glass house our team runs is rated 4.9 from 11 reviews and is a Guest Favorite, read October 16, 2026. Here that is the market average, not a standout. Our [Guest Favorite guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-ranking-and-guest-favorite/) covers what drives it.

- **Revenue was soft.** Average revenue fell 3.7% from the year before.

Park traffic also cooled after a record. The National Park Service counted 1,686,348 visits to the Buffalo National River in 2024, the most on record, and 1,393,246 in 2025, 17% fewer.

## When guests come: the cabin season

River crowds and cabin bookings do not peak together. In the park's 2025 count, May through July brought 49% of the year's visits and September through November only 18%. Yet October is the most booked month for rentals in AirROI's data. Cabin guests are not mainly coming to float. They come for fall color, elk, hiking weather and a hot tub on a cool night.

| Season | What the market does | What fills cabins | What to do |
| - | - | - | - |
| Spring, March to May | May is in the peak group with June and October: 48.9% of nights booked at $244. | Waterfalls after rain, green trails | Price spring weekends early. |
| Summer, June to August | June brings the most revenue and the highest nightly rates. | Families and groups. 51.7% of listings sleep 6 or more. | Sell the deck, the hot tub and the air conditioning. Never promise floating. |
| Fall, September to November | September is in the low group, which averages 29.0% of nights booked. October has the highest occupancy. | The elk rut, fall color, hiking weather | Set October and early November prices by midsummer. Fall stays book 54 days ahead on average. |
| Winter, December to February | January has the lowest occupancy and February the lowest revenue. | Holidays, stargazing, hot tub weekends | Holiday floors and minimum stays, plus plain notes on ice and gravel. Winter stays book 24 days ahead. |

Basis: AirROI Jasper area data, August 2025 to July 2026. Park visits from NPS Visitor Use Statistics, read October 17, 2026.

**Summer and the river.** The Buffalo River Chamber says floating on the upper river is mostly limited to spring and early summer, and to fall only in a wet year. A park spokesperson told KY3 in July 2022 that the upper river around Ponca tends to dry up in peak summer. A listing that sells floating in August earns disappointed guests. The check in notes at the homes our team runs say plainly where the river is and that it can run low or dry.

**Fall runs late.** The elk rut runs through September and October, according to Arkansas Tourism, but fall color can come later. A public foliage model forecast on October 17, 2026 put this year's peak at the Buffalo National River around November 4. As of October 16, 2026, our glass house had 14 November nights booked at an average of $547, Thanksgiving included.

**Winter is real.** In January 2025, Harrison averaged an overnight low of 24.3 degrees, and a January 9 to 10 storm brought widespread snow to the northern half of Arkansas, according to the National Weather Service in Little Rock. Holidays still sell. Our guide to [Buffalo River cabin income by season](https://listandhost.com/blog/buffalo-river-cabin-income-by-season/) walks through each month with real numbers.

## What guests book in the Ozarks

Guests here book a getaway, not a bed. In AirROI's Jasper area data for August 2025 to July 2026, 56.1% of listings fall in its outdoor and unique group, against 32.2% standard houses. The average listing sleeps 5.4 guests, the average stay is 3.1 nights, and guests book 46 days ahead on average. At our glass house, stays that include a weekend night were booked a median of 45 days ahead, against 5 days for weekday only stays, counting every stay booked as of October 16, 2026.

What sells a cabin here:

- **A hot tub.** 27.8% of Jasper area listings have one, and they averaged $43,474 a year against $20,242 without (AirROI, same period). Homes with tubs tend to be bigger, so the tub is not the whole gap. Airbnb ranks the hot tub sixth among the amenities guests searched for most worldwide in 2025. Our [hot tub guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/hot-tub-rentals-upkeep-and-earnings/) covers costs and upkeep.

- **Dark skies.** The Buffalo National River was named an International Dark Sky Park in June 2019, the first in Arkansas, according to the National Park Service. A deck, good chairs and outdoor lights that point down make it a reason to book.

- **Elk.** Arkansas Tourism says the herd grew from 112 elk released between 1981 and 1985 to about 500 (read October 17, 2026), and that dawn and dusk are the best viewing times. Put a short viewing note in the guest guide.

- **Trails and waterfalls.** Hikes to bluffs, caves and waterfalls work in every season and are best after rain. List the nearest trailheads and drive times.

- **Wifi that works.** 96.1% of Jasper area listings have wifi (AirROI, August 2025 to July 2026). In our experience cell signal is weak at many homes in the region, so guests lean on it.

Leave the river out of the promise and treat good water as a bonus.

## How remote owners run a cabin well

Most owners here live hours from the home. Pricing, messages, calendars and statements can run from anywhere. The rest needs hands at the home.

| Job | From anywhere? | Who does it |
| - | - | - |
| Prices and minimum stays | Yes | You, pricing software or a manager, every day |
| Guest messages and reviews | Yes | Someone who answers within the hour, nights and weekends included |
| Calendars on Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com | Yes | One shared calendar, so a night sold on one closes on the others |
| Cleaning, restocking and hot tub care | No | A local cleaner, plus a backup |
| Repairs, storms, ice and lockouts | No | A local handyman who answers the phone |
| Well and septic | No | Local service companies, on a schedule |

Basis: how the work splits at the two homes our team runs in the region.

Ten habits that work here:

1. **Two cleaners, not one.** Every turnover needs a backup for illness, holidays and same day flips. Ask for photos of every room, the hot tub and the deck before the next guest arrives.

2. **An arrival guide for rural roads.** Gravel drives and weak signal cause more stress than anything inside the home. Our check in details go out on their own before arrival and cover the gravel drive in, and the cabin loft's include a photo of where to park. Tell guests to download directions before they lose signal.

3. **Keyless entry.** A keypad or smart lock, ideally with a new code for each stay, means no key handoffs and no midnight lockouts. 83.9% of Jasper area listings offer self check in (AirROI, August 2025 to July 2026).

4. **A freeze plan.** The American Red Cross advises leaving the heat set no lower than 55 degrees when you are away in cold weather. Insulate exposed pipes, add a temperature alert you can check from your phone, and know who can reach the home on an icy morning.

5. **Septic and well on a calendar.** The EPA says a household septic system should be inspected at least every three years and that tanks are typically pumped every three to five, more often with heavier use. A rental with a new group every few days is heavy use. The EPA also advises testing a private well every year for total coliform bacteria, nitrates, total dissolved solids and pH.

6. **A price floor.** In September 2026, before a hard floor, our glass house sold 11 nights under $200. On September 28 we set a floor of $349 a night and capped last minute discounts at 10%. Every night booked since has sold at $314 or more, as of October 16, 2026. Our [dynamic pricing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/) explains floors, gap nights and minimum stays.

7. **A launch plan built for reviews.** Our cabin loft went live on September 24, 2026 with no reviews, priced at $89 on weeknights and $149 on weekends until its first three reviews, with Instant Book on. Only 12.2% of Jasper area listings use Instant Book (AirROI, August 2025 to July 2026). The cabin took its first booking three days after going live and had 16 of 31 October nights booked as of October 16, 2026. See the [cabin loft launch results](https://listandhost.com/results/ozark-cabin-loft/).

8. **More than one booking site.** Of the 35 stays booked at our glass house as of October 16, 2026, 7 came from Vrbo, Booking.com or our direct site. Each site also keeps a different share: across the three homes our team runs, as of October 16, 2026, host fees plus any discounts or refunds came to 19.9% of what guests were charged at list price on Airbnb (64 stays) and 8.0% on Vrbo (9 stays), or 11.2% after the payment cut we see on Vrbo deposits. Our [booking site comparison](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-vs-vrbo-vs-booking-com-for-owners/) has the details.

9. **Devices guests are told about.** Airbnb does not allow security cameras that monitor any part of a home's interior, and outdoor cameras must be disclosed in the listing. Noise monitors that only measure sound levels are allowed if disclosed, but not in bedrooms, bathrooms or sleeping areas.

10. **The truth, up front.** Tell guests about the gravel, the winter roads, the weak signal and the river level before they book, so normal Ozark conditions never become a refund request or a poor review.

Setting up a cabin for its first guest is its own job. Our [guest ready checklist](https://listandhost.com/blog/getting-a-home-guest-ready-checklist/) covers it.

## Run it yourself or hire help

Self managing works when you live close, have a cleaner you trust and can answer guests fast at any hour. From hours away, the hard part is being reachable when an ice storm hits or a cleaner calls in sick. Our [self managing comparison](https://listandhost.com/compare/self-managing/) puts the hours, dollars and risks side by side.

Full service in Fort Worth, the rest of Dallas Fort Worth and the Buffalo River region of Arkansas. Co hosting or remote pricing anywhere else in the United States. Full service is 20% of booking revenue. Booking revenue is the nightly rent plus any extra guest fees, after the platform's host fee. Taxes and cleaning fees are not part of it. There is no setup fee, guests pay the cleaning fee, repairs and supplies are billed at cost with receipts, and there is no fee on nights you block for yourself. On a cabin with $30,000 a year in booking revenue, the fee would be $6,000, an illustration and not a forecast. Every line is on our [pricing page](https://listandhost.com/pricing/).

If you already have a local cleaner and want to keep your listing and reviews, co hosting or remote pricing may fit better; compare all four options on the [services page](https://listandhost.com/services/), and see what each model covers in our [co host vs property manager guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-co-host-vs-property-manager/). Elsewhere in the Ozarks, we offer remote pricing and co hosting in [Eureka Springs](https://listandhost.com/eureka-springs/) and [Branson](https://listandhost.com/branson/), where the owner's local team keeps the hands on work. Every number from our own homes is on the [results page](https://listandhost.com/results/), with its period and basis.

## Questions owners ask

**How much does a cabin rental make near the Buffalo River?**

In AirROI's Jasper area data for August 2025 to July 2026, the average listing earned $26,695 a year, the middle listing $2,153 a month and the top quarter $3,767 a month. A market average is not a promise for any home.

**When is the busy season for Buffalo River cabins?**

In AirROI's Jasper area data for August 2025 to July 2026, October has the highest occupancy and June the most revenue, with May also in the peak group. January and February are the slowest months, though holidays sell well.

**Can I run a Buffalo River cabin from out of state?**

Yes, if the hands on work is covered. Pricing, messages and calendars can run from anywhere. Cleaning, hot tub care, repairs, ice and septic need a local cleaner with a backup and a handyman who answers the phone, or a full service manager.

**Should my listing advertise the river?**

Mention it as nearby, but do not sell it. A park spokesperson said in 2022 that the upper river around Ponca tends to dry up in peak summer. Sell the hot tub, the deck, the trails, the elk and the stars.

**What does cabin management cost in the Buffalo River region?**

Full service with List & Host is 20% of booking revenue, meaning the nightly rent plus any extra guest fees after the platform's host fee. Cleaning fees are not part of it. There is no setup fee, and repairs and supplies are billed at cost with receipts.

**Own a cabin in the Buffalo River region?** [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/?m=buffalo-river#estimator) built from your home and live booking data for the region, with the basis for every number. It is an estimate, not a promise of income.
