# How to Choose an Airbnb Manager: 15 Questions to Ask

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/questions-to-ask-an-airbnb-manager/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: The 15 questions to ask before you hire an Airbnb or short term rental manager, what a good answer sounds like and the red flags. Then get a free estimate.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

To choose a short term rental manager, interview at least three on the same 15 questions, get every answer in writing, and check their proof yourself before you sign. Walk away from any manager who promises a set income, will not write down what the fee is taken from, or wants your listing and reviews in their own account.

We are a management company, so we have a stake in your answer. This is the list we would want an owner to bring to us. The choice matters: hosts in a PriceLabs survey of more than 1,400 spent an average of 8.3 hours a week on their listings (reported November 20, 2025). Still deciding whether to hire anyone? Start with [self managing vs hiring a manager](https://listandhost.com/blog/self-managing-vs-hiring-an-airbnb-manager/).

## How to run the search

1. **Shortlist three,** including one local team and one larger company. Our comparison of [a local team and national managers](https://listandhost.com/compare/national-managers/) explains the difference.

2. **Send the same questions by email.** Written answers are easier to compare, and they show how clearly each manager writes, which is what your guests will see.

3. **Ask for three things on paper:** a sample agreement, a real owner statement with names removed, and links to three listings they run today.

4. **Check the proof yourself** with the table below, then score the answers and compare total cost on the same year of bookings.

## Fees and money

### 1. What exactly is your fee taken from?

A percentage means nothing without its base. Fees can come from everything guests pay, from nightly rent only, or from rent after the platform fee, and some agreements count cleaning fees (Awning, updated October 1, 2026). Awning’s own example puts the gap at $1,860 a year on $60,000 of revenue at the same 20% rate, only from taking the fee before or after Airbnb’s 15.5% host fee.

**Good answer:** one written sentence saying whether platform fees, cleaning fees, taxes and extra guest fees are in or out. **Red flag:** a rate with no base, or a base that changes between the call and the agreement.

### 2. What is billed on top, and do you mark anything up?

Setup, linens, supplies, photography, hot tub care and repairs can all be extra. Repairs are usually billed at the vendor’s cost, sometimes plus a coordination markup that varies by company (Awning, October 2026). Our [guide to management fees](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-management-fees/) compares two full quotes, extras included.

**Good answer:** a written list of every possible charge, each marked at cost or with its markup. **Red flag:** markups that never appear on the statement.

### 3. Where does guest money go, and what does the statement show?

Some managers let the platforms pay you directly and invoice their fee. Others collect payouts first and pay you the rest. Either can work if the statement ties every payout to a booking, with nights, channel, fees and costs on separate lines.

**Good answer:** last month’s statement with names removed, and the day of the month it arrives. **Red flag:** totals only, or “we send a report when you ask.”

## Pricing and earnings

### 4. Who sets my nightly prices, and how often do they change?

Pricing is where a manager earns the fee or wastes it. Rates and minimum stays should move with seasons, weekends, events and how close the date is. Ask who or what sets them, how often your nights are reviewed, and who approves the lowest price your home can take. Our guide to [dynamic pricing for owners](https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/) explains floors and event weeks.

**Good answer:** a daily review, a floor you approve, event dates priced months ahead and a change log you can see. **Red flag:** prices set once a season, or “the software handles it” with nobody watching.

### 5. What do you do when a weekend is still open ten days out?

This shows whether there is a plan or a panic button. A good manager steps open nights down slowly toward a floor and holds event nights firm. A weak one cuts until something books.

**Good answer:** a specific sequence with a floor, in plain words. **Red flag:** “we drop it until it books.”

### 6. What will my home earn, and how did you get that number?

An honest estimate is a range built from homes like yours on real dates, with its basis written down. Nobody can promise what guests will book, and a manager who quotes high to win you still charges the same fee when the year comes in lower.

**Good answer:** a low to high range, the comparable homes behind it and the date it was pulled. **Red flag:** a guaranteed income, or one number with nothing behind it.

## Guests and reviews

### 7. Who answers my guests at 2 AM, on holidays and when you are sick?

Airbnb counts response rate as the share of new inquiries and booking requests answered within 24 hours over the past 30 days, and its Superhost program asks for 90% or better plus a 4.8 overall rating (Airbnb Help Center, read October 17, 2026). Treat those as the floor. A guest locked out at night needs an answer in minutes.

**Good answer:** who covers which hours, who backs them up, and the response rate on a listing they run. **Red flag:** one person with no backup.

### 8. Can I see three listings you run right now?

Testimonials on a manager’s own site are easy to write. Live listings are not. In October 2024 Airbnb reported that co hosts in its Co-Host Network averaged 4.9 stars, against 4.62 for large managers with more than 30 active listings, both as of September 30, 2024. Those are group averages, so judge the listings in front of you. Our guide to [Airbnb ranking and Guest Favorite](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-ranking-and-guest-favorite/) explains the badges.

**Good answer:** links you can open today. **Red flag:** screenshots only, or “our owners prefer privacy” for every home.

### 9. How do you handle reviews, and what will you never do for one?

Every good guest should get a review, and every public review a calm reply. Nobody should buy them. Airbnb’s policy says reviews may not be provided or withheld in exchange for something of value, and on August 14, 2024 the Federal Trade Commission announced a rule that bans paying for reviews that express a set opinion.

**Good answer:** a written review routine, with no discounts or gifts tied to ratings. **Red flag:** “we give guests a discount for five stars.”

## Cleaning, repairs and damage

### 10. Who cleans, who checks the clean, and who covers when a cleaner cancels?

At the homes our team runs, checkout is 11 AM and check in is 4 PM, so every turn fits in five hours. A missed clean means a bad review and sometimes a refund.

**Good answer:** a written checklist, photos after every turn and a backup cleaner by name. **Red flag:** “we will find someone.”

### 11. What is my repair limit, and who goes to the home in an emergency?

A repair limit is what a manager may spend without asking you. Too low and every small fix waits on your phone. Too high and you learn about big bills from the statement. Also ask how far the nearest team member lives from your home.

**Good answer:** a written dollar limit, a quote before anything above it, and someone who can reach the home the same day. **Red flag:** no limit in the agreement, or nobody local for a full service price.

### 12. How do you document damage and file claims?

Timing decides most claims. On Airbnb, a host asks for damage reimbursement in the Resolution Center within 14 days of the responsible guest’s checkout, with photos and estimates or receipts (Airbnb Help Center, read October 17, 2026). Vrbo and Booking.com have their own processes.

**Good answer:** photos before cleaning starts, claims filed inside the window, outcomes on your statement. **Red flag:** no record of what was damaged or lost.

## Control and leaving

### 13. Whose account holds the listing, and what happens to my reviews if I leave?

If the listing lives in your own Airbnb account and the manager joins as a co host, the reviews stay with you, and only you as the listing owner can set up or change a co host’s payouts (Airbnb Help Center, read October 17, 2026). A Vacasa owner guide (read October 17, 2026) says hosts cannot transfer listings on Airbnb or Vrbo, so a listing in the manager’s account stays there and reviews can be moved only by request. Ask the same for Vrbo and Booking.com. Our [co host vs property manager guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-co-host-vs-property-manager/) shows how each model handles the listing.

**Good answer:** “Your account, your listing. We join as your co host.” **Red flag:** a new listing built in their account.

### 14. How long is the term, how much notice ends it, and what does leaving cost?

Terms reported in Awning’s fee guide (updated October 1, 2026) run from no long term contract to 1 to 3 years, with 90 days notice to cancel at one large company. As an illustration only: on $40,000 a year in nightly rent, 90 days of notice at a 20% fee is about $2,000 in fees after you decide to go. Ask who hosts stays booked before the end date.

**Good answer:** term, notice and any exit fee in one short paragraph, and booked stays honored. **Red flag:** a long first term with an exit fee and automatic renewal.

### 15. What do I still control?

You own the home. Ask how you block dates for yourself, whether any fee applies to nights you use, who approves the floor price, and what you can see on your own any day.

**Good answer:** owner stays with simple notice and no fee, and a dashboard you can open any time. **Red flag:** limits on your own use of the home.

## Check the proof yourself

Every manager says they price well, answer fast and keep owners happy. Here is how to check each claim before you sign.

| What they say | Ask for | How to check it |
| - | - | - |
| “We answer fast” | Listings they host | The Airbnb host profile shows response rate and usual response time |
| “Our pricing earns more” | Last month’s price log for one home | Click through two months of a listing’s dates. Weekends and events should cost more than weeknights |
| “Guests love our homes” | Three live listings | Read the last ten reviews and the host’s replies |
| “Our statements are clear” | A real statement, names removed | Each payout ties to a booking, each cost has a line |
| “Owners stay with us” | Two owners you can call | Ask what went wrong once and how it was fixed |

## Red flags that should end the search

- A guaranteed income, or a number with no comparable homes behind it.

- A fee with no written base, or charges that show up after you sign.

- Your listing moved into their account.

- No live listings you can open and read.

- Discounts or gifts offered to guests for reviews.

- No named backup for cleaning or guest messages.

- Pressure to sign on the first call, or no sample agreement to take home.

- A long first term with an early exit fee and automatic renewal.

## Score three managers side by side

Give each answer 2 points if it is specific and in writing, 1 if vague but reasonable, and 0 if missing or a red flag, for 30 points in all. Do not let a point of fee decide it alone. As an illustration: on $40,000 in nightly rent, one point of fee is $400, while 5% more nightly rent from better pricing is $2,000.

| Area | Questions | Get in writing |
| - | - | - |
| Fees and money | 1 to 3 | Fee base, extra charges, a sample statement |
| Pricing and earnings | 4 to 6 | Who prices, the floor rule, an estimate with its basis |
| Guests and reviews | 7 to 9 | Coverage hours, live listings, the review routine |
| Cleaning and repairs | 10 to 12 | Cleaner backup, repair limit, claims routine |
| Control and leaving | 13 to 15 | Listing ownership, term and notice, owner use |

## How we answer these 15 questions

Score us the same way. Full service is 20% of booking revenue. Booking revenue is the nightly rent plus any extra guest fees, after the platform's host fee. Taxes and cleaning fees are not part of it. There is no setup fee for full service, repairs and supplies are billed at cost with receipts, the platforms pay you directly, and your statement arrives by the 10th of each month. Your Airbnb listing stays in your own account. Anything above the repair limit you set comes to you with a quote first. The term and the notice to leave are quoted in writing after a [free look](https://listandhost.com/services/#free-look), before you sign anything.

Each morning our pricing engine reviews every night for the next 12 months, inside a floor you approve. In its first 26 days live, September 21 to October 16, 2026, it logged 133 nightly price changes and 52 minimum stay changes across the homes our team runs (basis: the engine’s own change log). One of those homes is a Guest Favorite rated 4.9, read from its public Airbnb listing on October 16, 2026. See how we count on our [results page](https://listandhost.com/results/), or read our [owner FAQ](https://listandhost.com/faq/).

Full service in Fort Worth, the rest of Dallas Fort Worth and the Buffalo River region of Arkansas. Co hosting or remote pricing anywhere else in the United States. See [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/), [Dallas](https://listandhost.com/dallas/), [Arlington](https://listandhost.com/arlington/) and the [Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/), every option on our [services page](https://listandhost.com/services/) and every fee on our [pricing page](https://listandhost.com/pricing/).

**Put us through the same 15 questions.** Start with a [free earnings estimate for your home](https://listandhost.com/estimate/): a low to high range built from homes like yours, with the basis for every number. It is an estimate, not a promise of income.

## Questions owners ask

**What questions should I ask before hiring an Airbnb manager?**

Ask what the fee is taken from, what is billed on top, who sets prices, who answers guests at night, whose account holds the listing, and how long the term and notice are.

**What are the red flags when choosing a short term rental manager?**

A guaranteed income, a fee with no written base, your listing moved into their account, no live listings you can check, discounts for reviews, and a long first term with an exit fee.

**How much does a short term rental manager charge?**

Full service commonly runs 18% to 25% of revenue, and limited plans about 10% to 15%, according to an Awning fee guide updated October 1, 2026. Always ask what the percentage is taken from.

**Should my listing be in my account or the manager's?**

Your own account, so the reviews and booking history stay with you if you change managers. On Airbnb, only the listing owner can set up or change a co host's payouts.

# How Much Does an Airbnb Make in Arlington, TX, by Bedroom?

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/how-much-does-an-airbnb-make-in-arlington-tx/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Arlington TX Airbnb income by bedroom count, with dated sources, the World Cup effect, real costs and a home we run nearby. Get a free estimate.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

In a normal year, our estimator puts an Arlington, Texas Airbnb that is available every night at roughly $19,500 in bookings as a 1 bedroom, $25,300 as a 2 bedroom, $34,100 as a 3 bedroom and $44,600 as a 4 bedroom, counting nightly revenue before cleaning fees and platform fees. Those are its middle cases, built on AirROI's Arlington data for August 2025 to July 2026 with the World Cup summer taken out; across all sizes, AirROI's average Arlington listing took in $25,379 in that same window. We read every source below on October 17, 2026. For how we run homes there, see our [Airbnb management in Arlington](https://listandhost.com/arlington/) page.

**Short answer.** Bedroom count sets the ceiling, but how a home is run decides where it lands. AirROI's top quarter of Arlington listings earns about three times what its bottom quarter earns per open night ($118 against $40). Bigger homes earn more per night; they do not book more nights.

## Arlington Airbnb income by bedroom count

No public source we found publishes a dated, Arlington only table of yearly revenue by bedroom count. So here are the two best references side by side: our estimator for Arlington, and the closest published bedroom table, which BnBCalc labels as the broader Dallas market.

| Bedrooms | Low | Likely | High | Nights booked, likely | BnBCalc typical listing, wider Dallas market |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| 1 | $14,400 | $19,500 | $24,900 | 135 (37%) | $21,900 at 46% booked |
| 2 | $18,700 | $25,300 | $32,300 | 130 (36%) | $33,100 at 46% |
| 3 | $25,200 | $34,100 | $43,600 | 129 (35%) | $44,000 at 43% |
| 4 | $32,900 | $44,600 | $56,900 | 126 (34%) | $61,100 at 41% (4 or more) |
| 5 | $43,100 | $58,200 | $74,400 | 124 (34%) | counted in 4 or more |
| 6 or more | $58,100 | $78,300 | $100,000 | 120 (33%) | counted in 4 or more |

Basis: low, likely and high are our estimator's yearly gross bookings (nightly rate times nights booked) for a home available all 365 nights, cleaning and platform fees not counted. They start from AirROI's public Arlington data for August 2025 to July 2026 (896 active listings), replace June and July 2026 with the average of May and August because of the World Cup, and spread the market across sizes using Arlington's own bedroom mix. Low and high move the nightly rate 10% down or up and use the revenue per open night of AirROI's median and top quarter listings. The bedroom split is our model, not a count of Arlington homes by size. BnBCalc's column is its "typical" tier, which it says covers the broader Dallas market; data updated September 2026.

Each added bedroom adds more than the one before it: about $5,800 a year from 1 to 2 bedrooms in our middle case, and about $13,600 from 4 to 5. And the share of nights booked slips as homes get bigger, because fewer groups need five or six bedrooms on any given night. Bigger homes win on price, not on occupancy.

## Nightly rates by bedroom count

| Bedrooms | RedAwning, Arlington | BnBCalc typical, wider Dallas market | Our estimate for Arlington, likely (low to high) |
| - | - | - | - |
| 1 | $109 | $122 | $145 ($130 to $160) |
| 2 | $140 | $173 | $195 ($175 to $215) |
| 3 | $203 | $245 | $265 ($240 to $290) |
| 4 | $289 | $346 (4 or more) | $355 ($320 to $390) |
| 5 | not published | counted in 4 or more | $470 ($425 to $520) |
| 6 or more | not published | counted in 4 or more | $650 ($585 to $710) |

Basis: nightly rates before cleaning fees, estimates rather than quotes. RedAwning's Arlington page shows its averages without a date; a 2026 note on the page says they start from 2024 data raised 3 to 5% for 2025 and 2026. BnBCalc's are rounded from its September 2026 table.

The references differ by $30 to $70 a night for the same size. RedAwning starts from older data. AirROI's average Arlington night ($278) sits far above its median ($196), because a few large, pricey homes pull the average up. If your home is ordinary for its size, plan near the low end of our range.

## What the market data says

| Measure | AirROI | GuestFavorites |
| - | - | - |
| Period | Aug 2025 to Jul 2026 | Jan to Sep 2026 |
| Active listings | 896 | 1,005 |
| Nightly rate | $278 average, $196 median | $234 average, $171 median |
| Share of nights booked | 34.8% average, about 33% median | 45% headline, 39% median |
| Yearly revenue per listing | $25,379 average | $38,533 median |
| Top of the market | Top 10% earn $195 per open night | Top 10% near $62,576 a year, 85% booked |
| Bottom of the market | Bottom quarter earns $40 per open night | Bottom quarter near $6,367 a year, 11% booked |

Basis: both public pages, read October 17, 2026; GuestFavorites says its page was updated October 16, 2026. Revenue per open night is AirROI's RevPAR: revenue divided by every available night, booked or not.

Why so far apart? GuestFavorites covers nine months and does not say how it turns them into a year, and its headline median of $38,533 sits just under its own top quarter figure of $39,920, so we read it as the generous end. AirROI covers a full year and counts many listings that are not open every night, which pulls its average down. Both include the World Cup summer, and both show a very wide gap between the best run homes and the rest.

## Why 2026 numbers overstate a normal Arlington year

- **Nine World Cup matches.** AT&T Stadium hosted nine matches from June 14 to July 14, 2026, including a semifinal. The city counted 631,843 fans across them.

- **A hotel record.** Arlington hotels took in a record $31 million in room revenue in June 2026, more than 30% above the previous monthly record of $23.6 million, set in November 2024, per the City of Arlington's July 28, 2026 release.

- **A spike in the data.** AirROI names June as Arlington's peak revenue month, with monthly revenue up to $7,340 and nightly rates peaking at $560. Its weakest month, January, dips to about $1,909.

Any trailing twelve month figure read in late 2026 or early 2027 carries that summer. Our estimator replaces June and July 2026 with the average of May and August, which lowers Arlington's yearly figures by 13%, the biggest cut of the three Dallas Fort Worth cities we cover (Dallas 8%, Fort Worth 4%). If someone shows you an Arlington projection built on 2026 data, ask whether the World Cup is in it.

## When Arlington books

| December | 10.3% | $3,500 |
| March | 9.5% | $3,200 |
| April | 7.4% | $2,500 |
| February | 6.0% | $2,100 |
| January | 5.6% | $1,900 |

Basis: AirROI's monthly pattern for Arlington, August 2025 to July 2026, with June and July replaced as above, applied to the likely 3 bedroom year of $34,100. The other six months each carry 8.2% to 8.8%. The dates behind that shape, read from the official pages on October 17, 2026:

- **Cowboys home games at AT&T Stadium.** November 1, 15 and 22, Thanksgiving Day on November 26, December 27, and January 3, 2027.

- **Big 12 Championship.** Friday, December 4, 2026, at AT&T Stadium.

- **Cotton Bowl Classic.** Friday, January 1, 2027, a College Football Playoff quarterfinal, at AT&T Stadium.

- **Grand Prix of Arlington.** IndyCar returns to the streets around AT&T Stadium, Globe Life Field and Texas Live! on March 19 to 21, 2027, after a race day grandstand sellout in 2026.

- **Texas Rangers.** 81 home games at Globe Life Field in 2027, starting with the home opener on Thursday, April 1. Baseball's labor agreement expires December 1, 2026, so treat those dates as provisional.

- **Six Flags Over Texas, Hurricane Harbor and UT Arlington.** Summer family trips, the park's holiday season and graduation weekends fill the gaps between games.

Our [Fort Worth event calendar for hosts](https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-event-calendar-for-hosts-2026-2027/) covers the arena, rodeo and college dates next door through 2027, and our [Fort Worth market report](https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-short-term-rental-market-report-october-2026/) lists the stadium and arena dates across the area through March 2027.

## Who you compete with

AirROI's Arlington data for August 2025 to July 2026 describes the field:

- Supply grew 47.1% in a year, while AirROI's revenue figure rose 7.3%. More homes are chasing the same guests.

- 41.9% of listings take only stays of 30 nights or more, so fewer homes compete for game weekends than the headline count suggests.

- 87.3% are entire homes, 40.1% have 3 or more bedrooms, and 56.6% sleep 6 or more.

- The average stay is 6.2 nights, and guests book an average of 41 days ahead.

- 50.8% of hosts are Superhosts and 36.8% of listings carry Airbnb's Guest Favorite label. A strong rating is the entry ticket.

| Feature | Share of Arlington listings | Average yearly revenue with it | Without it |
| - | - | - | - |
| Hot tub | 6.3% | $64,427 | $22,776 |
| Outdoor kitchen | 2.6% | $67,858 | $24,260 |

Basis: AirROI's Arlington market report, same period, read October 17, 2026. These gaps are correlation, not cause: homes with a hot tub or an outdoor kitchen also tend to be bigger and better run. Our estimator adds only 4% to the nightly rate for a hot tub in a city market, our own assumption. See our guide to [hot tub rentals](https://listandhost.com/blog/hot-tub-rentals-upkeep-and-earnings/) for the upkeep side.

On October 17, 2026, Google's suggestions for Arlington Airbnb searches included "near AT&T Stadium", "near Six Flags", "Globe Life Field", "with pool" and "pet friendly". Your title, first photo and map pin should answer those.

## A reality check from a home our team runs

The closest home our team runs with a booking record sits in west Fort Worth: 3 bedrooms, sleeps 8, taking guests since July 2026. It is not in Arlington, so treat it as a nearby check.

- **Nights and rate.** From August through October 2026 (October as booked on October 16), it was booked 56 of 92 nights, or 61%, at an average of $179 a night after discounts, before cleaning and platform fees.

- **Per open night.** That is about $109 for every night on the calendar, booked or not, between the likely ($94) and high ($119) cases our estimator gives a 3 bedroom in Arlington.

- **Two kinds of nights.** A Friday or Saturday night brought $236 on average against $139 for the rest of the week. Weekend stays were booked about six weeks out (a median of 44 days), while weeknight only stays came in a median of 1 day ahead.

Three fall months is a short record, so we do not turn it into a yearly figure. The lesson carries over: price event weekends early, and answer weeknight requests fast. The method is on the [results page for that home](https://listandhost.com/results/fort-worth-home/), and our [Fort Worth Airbnb income guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/how-much-can-an-airbnb-make-in-fort-worth/) has its monthly numbers. You can also [see results from all the homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/), one of them a Guest Favorite rated 4.9 on Airbnb (read October 16, 2026).

## The costs that come out before you keep anything

| Cost | What to expect | Basis |
| - | - | - |
| Platform fees and discounts | About 18.7% of what guests pay for the nights | Measured on 75 accepted stays at the homes our team runs, as booked October 16, 2026. Airbnb kept 19.9% across 64 stays, discounts included; its help page, read October 17, 2026, puts the host fee at 15.5% for most hosts |
| Cleaning | Usually paid by guests through a cleaning fee | AirROI: 90% of Arlington listings charge one, median $130. Our Fort Worth 3 bedroom pays its cleaner $90 a turn and charges guests $110 (October 2026) |
| Electricity | About $200 to $230 a month | Bills at our Fort Worth 3 bedroom, 2026 |
| Water, gas, internet, supplies | Varies by home and grows with bookings | Budget it monthly |
| Repairs and insurance | Small fixes every month, and a policy that covers short term guests | Set money aside from every payout; ask your agent about cover |
| Getting guest ready | Beds for the whole group, linens, a smart lock | One time. See our guest ready checklist |
| Management | Only if you hire it | Our full service fee is 20% of booking revenue; what it covers is on our pricing page |

## A worked 3 bedroom example

| Case | Nightly rate | Nights booked | Gross bookings | After 18.7% platform fees and discounts |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Low | $240 | 105 | $25,200 | $20,500 |
| Likely | $265 | 129 | $34,100 | $27,700 |
| High | $290 | 150 | $43,600 | $35,400 |

Basis: the 3 bedroom rows of our estimator, for a home that sleeps 8 with 2 baths and no hot tub, available all year. Cleaning fees are left out on both sides, since they mostly pay the cleaner. From the last column you still pay utilities, supplies, repairs, insurance, any mortgage and, if you hire one, a manager. These are examples, not promises. Weighing this against a sale? See [how to test a house that is not selling as a short term rental](https://listandhost.com/blog/house-not-selling-short-term-rental/).

## What moves an Arlington home toward the top quarter

1. **Price event dates early and protect them.** Load each game, race and holiday when the date is confirmed, with a floor and a two night minimum on big weekends. Our guide to [dynamic pricing](https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/) explains floors and fill plans, and our [DFW weekend and event pricing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-pricing-strategy-dfw-weekends-and-events/) shows what happens when event nights are left unprotected.

2. **Sell to the whole group.** More than half of Arlington listings sleep 6 or more. Beds for everyone and a driveway that fits several cars belong in the first photos.

3. **Fill January and February with longer stays.** They are the weakest months, and the average stay is already 6.2 nights. Our [guide to 30 night stays](https://listandhost.com/blog/traveling-nurse-30-night-stays-fort-worth/) shows how to reach work and medical stays.

4. **Earn the rating.** With 36.8% of listings already Guest Favorites, photos, reviews and reply speed decide who gets booked. See [how Airbnb ranks listings](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-ranking-and-guest-favorite/).

5. **List on more than one channel.** Vrbo and Booking.com reach guests Airbnb does not. See [Airbnb vs Vrbo vs Booking.com](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-vs-vrbo-vs-booking-com-for-owners/).

This is the daily work our [full service management](https://listandhost.com/services/) covers in Arlington, from our Fort Worth base. How we run a home there, step by step, is in our [Dallas and Arlington management guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/dallas-arlington-short-term-rental-management/).

## Questions owners ask

**How much does a 3 bedroom Airbnb make in Arlington, TX?**

Our estimator puts a normal year at $25,200 to $43,600 in nightly revenue, $34,100 likely, for a home that sleeps 8 and is available all year. BnBCalc's typical 3 bedroom in the wider Dallas market books $44,000. Both are before cleaning and platform fees, read October 17, 2026.

**What occupancy does an Airbnb in Arlington get?**

AirROI puts the average at 34.8% of nights for August 2025 to July 2026, about 33% at the median. GuestFavorites shows 45% for January to September 2026. Our estimator uses 33% to 37% as the likely case, depending on size.

**Why do Arlington Airbnb income numbers disagree so much?**

Each service picks its own listings, period and method, and some report averages while others report medians. Windows that include June and July 2026 also carry the nine World Cup matches at AT&T Stadium, which set a city hotel record.

**What are the best months for an Airbnb in Arlington?**

With the World Cup summer taken out, AirROI's pattern makes November, December and March the strongest months and January and February the weakest. Football, the holidays, spring break and the Grand Prix drive the strong months.

**Does a bigger home make more in Arlington?**

Per night, yes. But bigger homes do not book more nights: in our estimate the likely share of nights booked slips from 37% for a 1 bedroom to 33% for 6 bedrooms, and BnBCalc's wider Dallas table slides from 46% to 41%.

# How Much Can an Airbnb Make in Dallas? By Bedroom, 2026

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/how-much-can-an-airbnb-make-in-dallas/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Dallas Airbnb income by bedroom for 2026: low, likely and high yearly bookings from AirROI data, the World Cup effect and a worked 3 bedroom net.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

A 3 bedroom Airbnb in Dallas that is open every night books about $40,100 a year in a normal year, the likely case in our estimator, with a range of $31,000 to $51,200. That is nightly revenue before cleaning fees and platform fees, built on AirROI's public Dallas data for August 2025 to July 2026 (4,675 active listings) with the World Cup summer taken out. We read AirROI on October 16, 2026 and checked it again, with every other source below, on October 18, 2026. For how we run homes there, see our [Airbnb property management in Dallas](https://listandhost.com/dallas/) page.

**Short answer.** Size sets the nightly rate, and how a home is run sets how many nights it sells. In AirROI's Dallas data, a listing in the top quarter earns about 65% more per open night than the middle listing ($110.70 against $67.00, World Cup months replaced). Bigger homes earn more per night; they do not book more nights.

## Dallas Airbnb income by bedroom count

Each bedroom adds more than the one before it: about $6,700 a year from 1 to 2 bedrooms in the likely case, $10,400 from 2 to 3, and $23,700 from 5 to 6. AirROI's average Dallas listing of any size took in $24,382 over the same months, but many listings are not open every night.

And the share of nights booked slips from 39.3% for a 1 bedroom to 35.8% for 6 bedrooms, because fewer groups need that much room on any given night.

## Why 2026 overstates a normal Dallas year

AT&T Stadium in nearby Arlington hosted nine World Cup matches from June 14 to July 14, 2026, a semifinal among them. AirROI names June as the Dallas peak revenue month, and June stays were booked 56 days ahead on average, against 30 for the year. Any trailing twelve month figure read in late 2026 or early 2027 carries that summer.

Our estimator replaces June and July 2026 with the average of May and August, which lowers the Dallas year by 8%. Left in, the likely 3 bedroom would read about $43,700 instead of $40,100. If someone shows you a Dallas projection built on 2026 data, ask whether the World Cup is in it.

| Month | Share of a normal year | A likely 3 bedroom month |
| - | - | - |
| March | 9.6% | $3,900 |
| October | 9.2% | $3,700 |
| November | 9.1% | $3,700 |
| April | 8.0% | $3,200 |
| January | 7.0% | $2,800 |
| February | 6.0% | $2,400 |

Basis: AirROI's monthly pattern for Dallas, August 2025 to July 2026, with June and July replaced as above, applied to the likely 3 bedroom year of $40,100. December carries about 9.4%, and May through September about 8% to 9% each. In a normal year Dallas has no single giant month. March, AirROI's month with the highest share of nights booked, brings spring break; the State Fair of Texas, which ran September 25 to October 18, 2026, fills October; the Big 12 Championship on December 4, 2026 and the Cotton Bowl playoff game on January 1, 2027, both in Arlington, lift the holidays. Work trips, moves and medical stays fill the rest. Our [DFW weekend and event pricing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-pricing-strategy-dfw-weekends-and-events/) shows how to price those dates.

## Is an Airbnb profitable in Dallas? A worked 3 bedroom net

****************

| Line | Low | Likely | High |
| - | - | - | - |
| Nightly rate | $260 | $290 | $315 |
| Nights booked | 119 | 138 | 162 |
| Gross bookings | $31,000 | $40,100 | $51,200 |
| Platform fees and discounts, 18.7% | minus $5,800 | minus $7,500 | minus $9,600 |
| After platform fees | $25,200 | $32,600 | $41,600 |
| Cleaning: about 20, 23 or 27 turns at $155, paid by guests, paid to the cleaner | passes through | passes through | passes through |
| Our full service fee, 20% of the line after platform fees | minus $5,000 | minus $6,500 | minus $8,300 |
| Left before your own costs | $20,200 | $26,100 | $33,300 |

Basis: the 3 bedroom rows of our estimator, for a home that sleeps 8 with 2 baths and no hot tub, open all year. The 18.7% is what platform fees and discounts took on 75 accepted stays at the homes our team runs, as booked October 16, 2026; Airbnb alone kept 19.9% across 64 of them, discounts included, while its help page puts the host fee at 15.5% for most hosts. Turns assume AirROI's Dallas average stay of 5.9 nights. Platforms take their cut of the cleaning fee too, so set it a little above what the cleaner costs; our Fort Worth 3 bedroom charges guests $110 and pays $90 a turn (October 2026). Our fee is worked out after platform fees and never charged on cleaning fees; the details are on our [pricing page](https://listandhost.com/pricing/).

So is it profitable? The likely case leaves about $26,100 a year, or $2,170 a month. Out of that come your mortgage, utilities (electricity at our Fort Worth 3 bedroom ran about $200 to $230 a month in 2026), internet, supplies, repairs and a policy that covers short term guests. If those come to less than the line above, the home makes money; if not, it does not. These are examples, not promises. Setting up from scratch? Our [guest ready checklist](https://listandhost.com/blog/getting-a-home-guest-ready-checklist/) covers the one time costs.

## What separates the middle listing from the top quarter

| Dallas listing | Revenue per open night, World Cup months replaced | Over 365 nights |
| - | - | - |
| Middle (50th percentile) | $67.00 | $24,500 |
| Average | $86.80 | $31,700 |
| Top quarter (75th percentile) | $110.70 | $40,400 |

Basis: AirROI's revenue per available night (revenue divided by every open night, booked or not) for Dallas, August 2025 to July 2026, all sizes mixed, adjusted for the World Cup as above. Unadjusted, AirROI shows $41 at the 25th percentile, $73 at the median, $121 at the 75th and $185 at the 90th.

For a home open every night, that gap is about $16,000 a year. AirROI's unadjusted tiers show where it comes from: the top quarter of Dallas listings books 59% of nights or more against 20% or less for the bottom quarter, and charges $302 a night or more against $187 at the median. What the top quarter does differently, in our experience and in AirROI's report:

1. **Prices every night on its own.** Event weekends get a floor early; quiet nights step down before they go empty. Dallas guests book 30 days ahead on average, and February stays only 19, so a price set once in spring goes stale. See [dynamic pricing explained](https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/).

2. **Sells longer stays on purpose.** The average Dallas stay is 5.9 nights, and 36.4% of listings take only stays of 30 nights or more. Weekly and monthly discounts fill January and February. Our [guide to 30 night stays](https://listandhost.com/blog/traveling-nurse-30-night-stays-fort-worth/) shows how.

3. **Has the basics long stays need.** AirROI counts $26,080 a year on average for Dallas listings with a washer against $8,708 without, and $25,089 with a kitchen against $6,307 without. That is correlation, not cause, but at least nine in ten listings have each, so a home without them starts behind.

4. **Earns the rating.** 50.2% of Dallas hosts are Superhosts and 29.0% of listings carry Airbnb's Guest Favorite label. See [how Airbnb ranks listings](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-ranking-and-guest-favorite/).

5. **Stands out in a growing field.** AirROI counts 37.7% more Dallas listings than a year earlier, while its revenue figure fell 6.8%.

That daily work is what our [full service management](https://listandhost.com/services/) covers in Dallas, from our Fort Worth base. How we run a Dallas or Arlington home step by step is in our [Dallas and Arlington management guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/dallas-arlington-short-term-rental-management/).

## A check from a home our team runs nearby

We do not have a Dallas booking record to show you. The closest home our team runs with one sits in west Fort Worth: 3 bedrooms, sleeps 8, taking guests since July 2026. It is not in Dallas, so treat it as a nearby check.

- **Nights and rate.** From August through October 2026 (October as booked on October 16), it was booked 56 of 92 nights, or 61%, at an average of $179 a night after discounts, before cleaning and platform fees.

- **Per open night.** That is about $109 for every night on the calendar, booked or not, almost exactly the likely case our estimator gives a Dallas 3 bedroom ($110), and between its low ($85) and high ($140).

- **A different mix.** It got there with a lower rate than our Dallas likely night of $290 and far more nights booked than the Dallas likely share of 37.9%. Weekend nights brought $236 on average against $139 on weeknights.

Three fall months is a short record, so we do not turn it into a yearly figure. The method is on the [results page for that home](https://listandhost.com/results/fort-worth-home/), and our [Fort Worth Airbnb income guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/how-much-can-an-airbnb-make-in-fort-worth/) has its monthly numbers. You can also [see results from all the homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/). For the city next door, see [how much an Airbnb makes in Arlington, by bedroom](https://listandhost.com/blog/how-much-does-an-airbnb-make-in-arlington-tx/).

## Questions owners ask

**How much does a 3 bedroom Airbnb make in Dallas?**

Our estimator puts a normal year at $31,000 to $51,200 in nightly bookings, $40,100 likely, for a home open all 365 nights, before cleaning and platform fees. BnBCalc's typical 3 bedroom in the broader Dallas market books $44,000 (September 2026 data).

**Is an Airbnb profitable in Dallas?**

It can be, but the market alone does not decide it. In our likely 3 bedroom case about $26,100 a year is left after platform fees, discounts and a 20% management fee, before your mortgage, utilities, insurance, repairs and supplies. Whether that is a profit depends on those costs. It is an estimate, not a promise.

**What is the Airbnb occupancy rate in Dallas?**

AirROI puts the average at 38.4% of nights for August 2025 to July 2026, about 38% at the median. Our estimator's likely case slips from 39.3% for a 1 bedroom to 35.8% for 6 bedrooms, with the World Cup summer taken out.

**Do 2026 Dallas numbers include the World Cup?**

Most do. Nine matches at AT&T Stadium in Arlington from June 14 to July 14, 2026 lifted June and July. Replacing those months with the average of May and August lowers the Dallas year by 8% in our estimator.

**How much is a cleaning fee for a Dallas Airbnb?**

Our estimator uses $75 for a 1 bedroom up to $335 for 6 bedrooms, scaled from AirROI's Dallas median of $115. BnBCalc's Dallas page shows $73 to $225 for 1 to 4 or more bedrooms (October 2026). Guests usually pay it, and our fee is never charged on it.

# How Much Can I Make on Airbnb per Month? 12 Markets

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/how-much-can-i-make-on-airbnb-per-month/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: A 3 bedroom Airbnb month by month in 12 markets, AirROI data Aug 2025 to Jul 2026: best months, slow months and the cash to hold back. Get a free estimate.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

A 3 bedroom home that is open every night books about $2,800 to $4,900 in an average month across the 12 markets in our estimator, before platform fees, cleaning fees and your own costs. The month matters as much as the market: the same likely case runs about $1,300 in a Branson January and about $4,600 in a Branson June. Both come from our estimator's likely case, built on AirROI market data for August 2025 to July 2026 (read October 16, 2026) and split by each market's monthly pattern.

**Short answer.** Ask for a monthly range, not one number. Fort Worth, the flattest of the 12 markets, swings from about $2,700 in February to about $3,800 in May for a likely 3 bedroom. Branson, the steepest, swings from about $1,300 in January to about $4,600 in June. January, February and September fall below an average month in all 12 markets. City markets spread the year; getaway markets bunch it.

Each year is split by the market's monthly revenue pattern in AirROI's data for August 2025 to July 2026, read October 16, 2026. Each month is rounded to $100 on its own. An estimate, not a promise.

The market sets the level: Broken Bow's likely 3 bedroom year, $58,900, is the highest of the 12, and Arlington's, $34,100, the lowest. The guests set the shape, and the shape decides your cash from month to month.

## City markets vs getaway markets

City guests come for work, family, games, concerts and events all year. Getaway guests come when the weather and the school calendar allow.

| Group | Best three months, share of the year | Slowest three months, share of the year | Best month against slowest |
| - | - | - | - |
| City markets: Fort Worth, Arlington, Dallas | 28.8% | 20.5% | 1.6 times |
| Getaway markets: the other nine | 31.7% | 17.5% | 2.2 times |

Basis: averages of each market's shares from the first table (AirROI monthly patterns, August 2025 to July 2026). An even year puts 25% into any three months.

Getaway markets win June (10.4% of the year on average, against 8.3% in the cities after the World Cup adjustment), March and October. The cities hold up better from December through February and in September.

The groups overlap. Arlington swings from 5.6% of its year in January to 10.6% in November, wider than Fredericksburg or Wimberley in the [Texas Hill Country](https://listandhost.com/texas-hill-country/). Fort Worth is the flattest of all 12, between 7.0% and 9.9% every month. Its winter holds up best, and the Fort Worth Stock Show runs through those weeks (January 15 to February 6 in 2027).

Among the getaways, the [Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/) peaks in June (11.4%) with October close behind (11.3%); Arkansas Tourism lists September and October as the elk rut in Boxley Valley. [Eureka Springs](https://listandhost.com/eureka-springs/) is the only market that peaks in October, at 11.9%. [Branson](https://listandhost.com/branson/) has the deepest winter: January and February together bring 7.6% of its year.

## Planning cash for the slow months

A yearly estimate divided by 12 is the wrong number for a budget. The mortgage, insurance and internet cost the same in January as in June; bookings do not. Compare January and February with two average months.

| Market | January and February, share of the year | January and February, likely 3 bedroom | Short of two average months |
| - | - | - | - |
| Branson | 7.6% | $2,700 | $3,300 |
| Broken Bow | 11.3% | $6,700 | $3,100 |
| Buffalo River region | 9.6% | $3,600 | $2,700 |
| Eureka Springs | 10.6% | $4,200 | $2,500 |
| Hot Springs | 10.2% | $3,800 | $2,400 |
| Wimberley | 11.9% | $5,800 | $2,400 |
| Glen Rose | 11.9% | $4,900 | $2,000 |
| Fredericksburg | 13.1% | $6,900 | $1,900 |
| Granbury | 11.7% | $4,400 | $1,900 |
| Arlington | 11.7% | $4,000 | $1,700 |
| Dallas | 13.0% | $5,200 | $1,500 |
| Fort Worth | 14.4% | $5,600 | $900 |

Basis: the first table (AirROI, August 2025 to July 2026). An average month is the year divided by 12, so two average months are 16.7% of the year. Each figure is rounded to $100 on its own.

Those are gross bookings. Across 75 accepted stays at the homes our team runs, as booked on October 16, 2026, platform fees and discounts took 18.7% of what guests were charged, so a $1,300 Branson January leaves about $1,060 before cleaning, utilities and the mortgage. With full service, our fee is 20% of booking revenue after platform fees, so it shrinks in a slow month too; your fixed bills do not. Every fee is on our [pricing page](https://listandhost.com/pricing/).

- **Hold back from the strong months.** In Branson, January and February fall about $3,300 short of two average months; set that aside from summer and the holidays.

- **Plan for September too.** It sits below an average month in all 12 markets, lowest in Broken Bow (5.5%) and Glen Rose (6.0%).

- **Budget winter from the low case.** Our estimator's low case sets the rate 10% under the market average and uses the middle listing's revenue per open night. Use it until your own record says otherwise.

## What moves a home up within its month

Inside any month, the home and its pricing decide where it lands against the market line.

1. **Weekends and weeknights are two markets.** Our October 13, 2026 comp check covered 214 entire homes with 3 or more bedrooms, searched for six adults in west Fort Worth. For Friday October 16 to Sunday October 18, 20 were still open, and the 10 comparable homes on page one asked a median of $1,028 for the two nights, before taxes. For Tuesday October 20 to Thursday October 22, 102 were open, at a median of $463. Homes left open late lean pricier, so the gap is overstated; still, price weekends early. See our [DFW weekend and event pricing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-pricing-strategy-dfw-weekends-and-events/).

2. **Event dates.** In Fort Worth, the NCHA Futurity is scheduled for November 16 to December 12, 2026, and the Stock Show for January 15 to February 6, 2027. Price those nights on their own, with minimum stays; see our [Fort Worth event calendar for hosts](https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-event-calendar-for-hosts-2026-2027/).

3. **Longer stays for winter.** Work and medical stays can fill city winters; see [30 night stays for traveling nurses](https://listandhost.com/blog/traveling-nurse-30-night-stays-fort-worth/).

4. **A hot tub in getaway markets.** AirROI's April 2026 cabin study measured a 7.9% lift in Broken Bow, 8.3% in Blue Ridge and 10.8% in Gatlinburg; our estimator adds 8% to the nightly rate. Our [hot tub guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/hot-tub-rentals-upkeep-and-earnings/) covers the running costs.

5. **Floors before the slow month.** Set your lowest price ahead of time, so automatic discounts cannot sell a night for less than it costs; see [dynamic pricing for owners](https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/).

Our [services page](https://listandhost.com/services/) lists what each service covers. Here is how two homes our team runs did against their line this fall.

| Home | August 2026 | September 2026 | October 2026, booked to date |
| - | - | - | - |
| Fort Worth line: likely 3 bedroom | $2,900 | $2,800 | $3,300 |
| The 3 bedroom Fort Worth home our team runs, sleeps 8 | about $2,600 (12 nights at $217) | about $3,400 (20 nights at $169) | about $4,100 (24 nights at $169) |
| Buffalo River region line: likely 3 bedroom | $3,000 | $2,400 | $4,200 |
| The glass house our team runs, 3 bedrooms plus a loft, sleeps 10, hot tub | about $7,300 (16 nights at $455) | about $7,700 (25 nights at $306) | about $13,600 (27 nights at $502) |

Basis: the line is the likely 3 bedroom month from the first table, a normal year's shape, not a forecast. The homes show nights booked times the average night guests paid, after discounts, before cleaning fees, taxes and platform fees, from our booking records as of October 16, 2026; October is booked, not yet earned. The glass house sleeps 10 and has a hot tub, so it is not a like for like match. Two homes over three months is a short record, not a forecast for yours. ## Questions owners ask

**How much does an Airbnb make per month on average?**

For a 3 bedroom home open every night, our estimator's likely case averages about $2,800 a month in Arlington to about $4,900 in Broken Bow, before platform fees, cleaning fees and costs. AirROI's average listing of any size earns about $1,900 to $4,300 a month in these markets ($23,139 to $51,710 a year, August 2025 to July 2026), since many listings are smaller or not open every night.

**What is the slowest month for an Airbnb?**

January or February, in every one of the 12 markets. September is a second dip: it falls below an average month in all 12, lowest in Broken Bow at 5.5% of the year.

**Which month earns the most on Airbnb?**

It depends on the market. March leads in five of the 12 (Dallas, Glen Rose, Broken Bow, Wimberley and Fredericksburg), June in three (the Buffalo River region, Hot Springs and Branson), May in two (Fort Worth and Granbury), November in Arlington and October in Eureka Springs.

**Can I budget with the yearly estimate divided by 12?**

Not safely. In Branson, January and February together bring about $2,700 on a likely 3 bedroom year, about $3,300 short of two average months. Budget from the monthly split and set money aside from the strong months.

**Why were June and July changed for Fort Worth, Arlington and Dallas?**

The nine World Cup matches at the Arlington stadium, June 14 to July 14, 2026, pushed those months far above a normal year. We replaced them with the average of May and August, which lowers the yearly figures by 4% in Fort Worth, 8% in Dallas and 13% in Arlington.

**Sources:** [AirROI: Fort Worth, TX Airbnb data, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026](https://www.airroi.com/airbnb-data/united-states/texas/fort-worth) · [AirROI: Arlington, TX Airbnb data, Aug 2025 to Jul
