# How Does a Co Host Get Paid on Airbnb? Splits and Fees

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/how-does-a-co-host-get-paid-on-airbnb/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: How Airbnb co host payouts work: percentage, fixed amount or cleaning fee splits, when they pay, a worked split on a real stay, and how Vrbo differs.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

A co host gets paid on Airbnb when the listing owner turns on payout sharing: Airbnb then pays the co host a cut of every booking, set as a percentage, a fixed amount, the cleaning fee, or the cleaning fee plus a percentage, worked out from the host's earnings after Airbnb's host service fee. For most stays the money reaches the co host's own payout method by the end of the business day after check in, and only the owner can set or change it.

Below: Airbnb's rules (Help Center, read October 18, 2026), a worked split on one real payout from a home our team runs, what co hosts charge, and Vrbo. We offer co hosting, so we have a stake in the answer.

**Short answer.** The owner sets the split, the co host confirms it, and Airbnb pays co hosts first and the owner what is left. A percentage comes off earnings after Airbnb's fee, so a co host quoted 20% of gross needs a bigger split setting or an invoice. Vrbo has no split: the owner pays a Vrbo helper directly.

## Short answer: how the money moves

1. **The guest pays Airbnb** one price for the nights and the cleaning fee, plus taxes, under Airbnb's single fee, which hosts who use property management software must use.

2. **Airbnb takes its host service fee:** 15.5% for most hosts, typically 14% to 16% for the rest, on the nightly price and fees such as cleaning. The rest is the host's potential earnings.

3. **Co hosts are paid first** from those earnings, in a set order. The owner gets what remains.

4. **Airbnb releases the money** by the end of the business day after check in. Hosts without two completed stays (unless their listing is verified) and listings with ongoing issues wait until after checkout. Stays of 28 nights or more pay monthly.

Basis: Airbnb Help Center articles on co host payouts, service fees and payout methods, read October 18, 2026.

## What Airbnb's payout split allows

The owner picks one option per co host, in the listing editor under Your space, Co hosts, then Payouts.

| Option | What the co host gets | The cleaning fee |
| - | - | - |
| Cleaning fee | The cleaning fee set in your listing | All of it |
| Cleaning fee plus percentage | The cleaning fee, plus a percentage of the rest | Paid in full, outside the percentage |
| Percentage | A share of each booking's potential earnings | In or out, your choice |
| Fixed amount | A set dollar amount per booking | Not involved |

Basis: Airbnb Help Center, how co host payouts work, read October 18, 2026.

- **Only the owner sets it.** A co host cannot edit a payout, even with full access. They have 14 days to confirm, and a change applies only to bookings that start after they confirm it.

- **Only Airbnb stays are shared.** Damage reimbursements and Resolution Center payouts stay with the owner. Two resolution payments, $120 and $50, that reached the Fort Worth home our team runs with one September 2026 stay, one of them for extra pets, would not be split (our booking records).

- **Several co hosts are paid in order**, cleaning fee splits first and fixed amounts last. If the earnings run out, the owner is last in line: in Airbnb's own example, four co hosts take $275 of $500 and the owner keeps $225.

- **The co host needs their own payout method**, such as a bank account or PayPal, and a verified identity where Airbnb asks.

## Co host permission levels and what each can do

Permissions and pay are separate settings. A co host at any level can be paid.

| Level | Can | Cannot |
| - | - | - |
| Full access | Message guests, change the calendar, prices and listing, manage reservations, handle damage claims, see earnings, add or remove co hosts | Set up or edit co host payouts |
| Calendar and messaging | Message guests, view the calendar | Change anything, see earnings, write guest reviews |
| Calendar | View the calendar | Everything else |

Basis: Airbnb Help Center, what co hosts can do, read October 18, 2026. A listing can have up to 10 co hosts.

A full access co host can remove other co hosts, which ends their payouts. Give full access to the person who runs the listing, and a lighter level to a cleaner who only needs the calendar.

## A worked split on one real stay

One Airbnb payout from the [glass house our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/buffalo-river-glass-house/) in the [Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/): a four night weekday stay in mid October 2026 for a group of more than 4, no discount.

| Line on the reservation | Amount |
| - | - |
| Nights at $399, $399, $399 and $449 | $1,646.00 |
| Cleaning fee | $225.00 |
| Guest price before taxes | $1,871.00 |
| Airbnb host service fee, 15.5% | −$290.01 |
| Host potential earnings, paid the day after check in | $1,580.99 |

Basis: our Airbnb reservation record for this stay, read October 18, 2026.

Four ways to split that $1,580.99. Where the cleaning fee is left out, Airbnb's own examples take the full fee off first, leaving $1,355.99.

| Split the owner sets | Co host gets | Owner's payout | Owner after a $200 clean |
| - | - | - | - |
| 20%, cleaning fee included | $316.20 | $1,264.79 | $1,064.79 |
| 20%, cleaning fee left out | $271.20 | $1,309.79 | $1,109.79 |
| Cleaning fee plus 15% | $428.40 | $1,152.59 | $1,152.59 (co host pays the cleaner) |
| $150 fixed per booking | $150.00 | $1,430.99 | $1,230.99 |

Basis: Airbnb's published payout method applied to the stay above. $200 is our cleaner's rate at this home for more than 4 guests (October 2026). An illustration of the method, not what this home pays anyone; Airbnb's rounding can differ by a cent.

Putting the cleaning fee inside a 20% split moves $45 to the co host on this one stay. A co host quoted 20% of the $1,646 nightly rent before Airbnb's fee expects $329.20, which no 20% setting pays: it would take about 24.3% with the cleaning fee left out, and the matching number shifts from stay to stay, so many owners pay a gross based fee by invoice instead.

This stay is the clean case. Across 64 Airbnb stays at the three homes our team runs (check ins July 2026 to June 2027, as booked October 16, 2026), Airbnb's fee plus discounts and refunds took 19.9% of what guests were charged at list price. Discounts come out of the earnings a percentage is taken from: an $89.40 last minute discount on a four night Fort Worth stay in October 2026 cut a 20% co host's share by about $15. A fixed amount would not have moved.

## What co hosts typically charge, and on what base

No platform sets co host fees. Three 2026 guides, all from companies that sell management or software, publish these ranges.

| Source | Date | Co host or partial help | Base |
| - | - | - | - |
| Awning | Updated October 1, 2026 | 10% to 15% for half service; full service 18% to 25% | Gross or net, per the contract |
| TIDY | 2026 | 10% to 25% for co hosts | Gross bookings |
| Hostfully | May 25, 2026 | 10% to 25%, or $500 to $800 a month per property | Gross booking revenue |

The base matters as much as the rate. AirROI puts the average Fort Worth listing at $24,276 a year in revenue (August 2025 to July 2026). At 20% of that, a co host earns $4,855; at 20% after a 15.5% host fee, $4,103, about $750 less. Settle in writing whether the percentage comes before or after the platform's fee, whether cleaning and pet fees count, and what a refund does to it.

Basis: AirROI's public Fort Worth data, read October 16, 2026, with Airbnb's 15.5% fee applied to all of it as an illustration, not a forecast for any home.

**Event weekends.** A percentage rises with the price; a fixed amount does not. In our Airbnb search on October 13, 2026, 3 and 4 bedroom homes for 6 guests in central and west [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/) had a median two night total of $738 for the Stock Show opening weekend, January 15 to 17, 2027 (14 homes), against $463 for Tuesday to Thursday, October 20 to 22, 2026 (11 homes), before taxes. On a percentage, the event weekend pays the co host about 1.6 times as much. On a [30 night traveling nurse stay](https://listandhost.com/blog/traveling-nurse-30-night-stays-fort-worth/), owner and co host are paid monthly.

**Our model.** Full service with List & Host is 20% of booking revenue: the nightly rent plus any extra guest fees, after the platform's host fee, with cleaning fees and taxes left out. It is not taken through Airbnb's split. The platforms pay you directly, and our fee comes on one invoice with your monthly statement. [Co hosting](https://listandhost.com/services/#cohost) is priced in writing after a [free look](https://listandhost.com/services/#free-look). See our [pricing page](https://listandhost.com/pricing/) and our [co host vs property manager guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-co-host-vs-property-manager/).

## Vrbo: users and payouts on a partner account

Vrbo has no co host role and no payout split. Our guide to [Airbnb vs Vrbo vs Booking.com](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-vs-vrbo-vs-booking-com-for-owners/) compares the three.

- **Access.** The owner invites a helper by email from the account settings, with one level of access covering messages, calendar, rates, listing and reservations, while financial settings stay with the owner, per Hostfully (May 25, 2026). Vrbo's own help pages on users did not load for us on October 18, 2026, so check the labels in your dashboard.

- **Payouts.** Vrbo pays the payout account set for each listing under Payments, then Payout accounts. It says listings cannot be transferred to another party, and a bank change made because of a new manager may be revoked (Vrbo Help Center, read October 18, 2026).

- **Paying the helper.** By invoice, on the base you agreed. At the homes our team runs, Vrbo kept 8.0% of list price across 9 stays, or 11.2% counting the 3.5% payment cut on Vrbo deposits (as booked October 16, 2026), so agree whether the helper's percentage comes before or after that.

## Airbnb's Co-Host Network and its bar

Airbnb's directory of co hosts for hire, the Co-Host Network, launched October 16, 2024 with more than 10,000 co hosts in 10 countries, the United States among them. In our search check on October 17, 2026, its Fort Worth page showed three co hosts with ratings and years hosting, but no fees. To join, Airbnb's Help Center (read October 18, 2026) asks for:

- An active listing as a host, a full access co host or a calendar and messaging co host.

- In the past 12 months, 10 or more stays, or 3 or more stays totaling 100 or more nights.

- An average rating of 4.8 or higher over the past 12 months, across every listing they support.

- Cancellations under 3%, a verified identity, and in the US a personal display name, not a business.

A co host rated below 4.7 may be hidden from the network's search, and below 4.5 Airbnb may end its network agreement. The bar shows a track record. It does not show the fee, the base or who covers a lockout at night, so ask. Our [15 questions to ask an Airbnb manager](https://listandhost.com/blog/questions-to-ask-an-airbnb-manager/) work for a co host too.

## You keep the listing, reviews and payouts

A co host joins your listing; they do not take it. The listing, its reviews and its payout account stay in your name, and removing a co host stops their payouts. Ask anyone you hire whether your home stays on your account. The glass house above is an Airbnb Guest Favorite rated 4.9 from 11 reviews (October 16, 2026), and that rating belongs to the listing, not to whoever runs it. With our co hosting you keep your listing, reviews, cleaner and payouts, and with full service the platforms pay you, never us. See our [services](https://listandhost.com/services/) and the records behind our numbers on our [results page](https://listandhost.com/results/).

## Questions owners ask

**How does a co host get paid on Airbnb?**

The listing owner sets a payout split in the listing editor: the cleaning fee, the cleaning fee plus a percentage, a percentage, or a fixed amount per booking. Once the co host confirms, Airbnb pays their share from the host's earnings after Airbnb's host service fee.

**Can I share the cleaning fee with my co host?**

Yes. You can give a co host the full cleaning fee, the cleaning fee plus a percentage of the rest, or a percentage with the cleaning fee in or out. On one $1,580.99 payout at a home our team runs (October 2026), including it in a 20% split moved $45 to the co host.

**When does an Airbnb co host get paid?**

For most stays, by the end of the business day after check in, alongside the host. Newer hosts and listings with ongoing issues are paid after checkout, and stays of 28 nights or more pay monthly.

**What percentage does an Airbnb co host take?**

Owner and co host agree on it. 2026 guides from Awning, TIDY and Hostfully put co hosts at about 10% to 25%, usually of gross bookings, while Airbnb's split is taken after its host fee.

**Does Vrbo split payouts with a co host?**

No. The owner gives a helper access to the account and pays them directly, while Vrbo pays the owner.

**Weighing a co host or full service?** [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) built from your address, your home and live booking data for your market, with the basis for every number. Then run the split table above on your own figures. It is an estimate, not a promise of income.

**Sources:** [Airbnb Help: how co host payouts work, read October 18, 2026](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3389) · [Airbnb Help: what co hosts can do, read October 18, 2026](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1534) · [Airbnb Help: requirements to join and stay on the Co-Host Network, read October 18, 2026](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3727) · [Airbnb Help: Airbnb service fees, read October 18, 2026](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1857) · [Airbnb Help: add a payout method, read October 18, 2026](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/54) · [Airbnb Newsroom: Co-Host Network launch, October 16, 2024](https://news.airbnb.com/en-uk/airbnb-2024-winter-release-introducing-co-host-network-the-best-local-hosts-to-manage-your-airbnb) · [Airbnb: Fort Worth co hosts page](https://www.airbnb.com/host/fort-worth-tx/co-hosts) · [Vrbo Help: update your bank account information, read October 18, 2026](https://help.vrbo.com/articles/How-do-I-update-my-bank-account-information) · [Hostfully: Vrbo co host, May 25, 2026](https://www.hostfully.com/blog/vrbo-co-host/) · [Awning: Airbnb management fees, updated October 1, 2026](https://awning.com/post/airbnb-management-fees) · [TIDY: Airbnb management fees, 2026](https://www.tidy.com/airbnb-management-fees) · [AirROI: Fort Worth, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026](https://www.airroi.com/report/world/united-states/texas/fort-worth) · [Fort Worth Stock Show and Rodeo: visitor questions](https://www.fwssr.com/p/plan-a-visit/frequently-asked-questions)


# House Not Selling? How to Test It as a Short Term Rental

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/house-not-selling-short-term-rental/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: House not selling? When a short term rental can carry it: the numbers to check, a worked example, the real risks and a 90 day test plan. Free estimate.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

If your house is not selling, a short term rental makes sense only when what it leaves after platform fees, cleaning, utilities and setup beats what the empty house costs you each month, and beats the price cut or lease you would otherwise accept. The way to find out is not a projection but a short, capped test on real bookings: set a budget, list with a short booking window, and judge it on payouts after about 90 days.

Below: the numbers to check before you spend anything, a worked example with the basis for every figure, the risks we see at the homes our team runs in [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/) and the [Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/) of Arkansas, and a 90 day test plan.

## Why so many sellers are asking

Homes are taking longer to sell. Realtor.com's September 2026 housing report put the national median time on market at 61 days, with 20.8% of active listings carrying a price cut. In the Dallas, Fort Worth and Arlington metro, 27.5% of listings had a price cut that month. Redfin data reported by Stacker put Fort Worth's median time on market at an average of 57.7 days for January to June 2026.

Many owners turn to renting. Zillow found that 2.3% of homes listed for rent on its site in October 2025 had recently been listed for sale and not sold, matching its October 2022 level, and its March 2026 list put Dallas at 3.4%. Most of those are long term leases. A short term rental is a different business: more money per night, more work, more cost and more ways to be wrong.

## Your three options, side by side

| Option | Money | Work | Cash up front | Selling soon |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Cut the price | Holding costs end at closing; you take less at the sale | Least | None | That is the point |
| Lease it long term | Monthly rent, usually on a one year lease | Low once a tenant moves in | Little; the house can stay empty of furniture | Harder while a tenant lives there |
| Run it short term | Nightly bookings that swing with the season | Most: guests, cleaning and pricing every day | Furniture, linens and supplies | Possible, if the booking window stays short |

Basis: how each option generally works, not a forecast for any house.

## The numbers to check before you spend anything

### 1. What the empty house costs you each month

This is the bar a rental has to clear. Add your loan payment if there is one, your insurance, the yearly bills that come with owning the house spread over twelve months, basic utilities, lawn care and small repairs. You pay this every month the house sits, whether anyone stays or not.

### 2. What homes like yours actually book

Start with market data that carries a date, and expect the sources to disagree. For Fort Worth, AirROI puts the average listing at $24,276 a year in bookings (August 2025 to July 2026), while Airbtics puts the median at about $43,000 (September 2025 to August 2026). For the Jasper area of the Buffalo River region, AirROI shows an average of $26,695 a year with 37.3% of nights booked over August 2025 to July 2026. Many listings in those figures are not open every night, and a home can land well above or below them.

Then look at the season. At the 3 bedroom Fort Worth home our team runs, 39% of nights sold in August 2026 and 77% in October, counting October as booked on October 16. AirROI names January, February and September as the weak months in both Fort Worth and the Jasper area. A test that only runs through a strong fall will flatter the numbers. Our [Fort Worth income guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/how-much-can-an-airbnb-make-in-fort-worth/) and our [Buffalo River season guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/buffalo-river-cabin-income-by-season/) go month by month, and our [Ozark cabin rental guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/ozark-cabin-rental-management-buffalo-river/) covers running a cabin from out of town.

### 3. What comes off the top

- **Platform fees and discounts.** Airbnb's single host fee is 15.5% for most hosts (Airbnb Help Center, read October 17, 2026). Across 75 stays at the three homes our team runs, with check ins from July 2026 to June 2027 as booked on October 16, 2026, platform fees and discounts took 18.7% of what guests were charged. On Airbnb alone it was 19.9% over 64 stays.

- **Cleaning.** Guests pay a cleaning fee, and it pays the cleaner. At our Fort Worth home guests pay $110 and the cleaner earns $90 a turn (October 2026). Stays there average 2.7 nights (stays booked as of October 16, 2026), so turns add up fast.

- **Utilities.** Guests use the house fully. Electricity at our Fort Worth home has run about $200 to $230 a month in 2026. Add internet and streaming.

- **Supplies, repairs and wear.** Paper goods and coffee every month, plus what guests break or wear out.

- **Management, if you hire it.** Our full service fee is 20% of booking revenue, worked out after platform fees and never charged on cleaning fees or taxes. Our [pricing page](https://listandhost.com/pricing/) shows what is billed at cost.

### 4. What it costs to get guest ready

Awning puts furnishing a typical short term rental at roughly $10,000 to $30,000 (June 2026). RedAwning puts a 3 bedroom house at $15,000 to $35,000, plus $1,000 to $10,000 for linens, toiletries and other guest supplies (updated May 2026). Both sell services to owners, so treat those as vendor ranges. A house that still has your furniture, or is staged, can start for far less: good beds, two sets of linens per bed, towels, kitchen basics and a smart lock. Our [guest ready checklist](https://listandhost.com/blog/getting-a-home-guest-ready-checklist/) lists what guests expect.

### 5. How long the first bookings take

A new listing starts with no reviews, and Airbnb shows a star rating only after three. Airbnb lets a new listing offer 20% off its first 3 bookings (Airbnb Help Center, read October 17, 2026). Our cabin loft in the Buffalo River region went live on September 24, 2026, priced at $89 weeknights and $149 weekends until it had three reviews. Its first booking came 3 days later, and it had 6 stays booked by October 14. That was one cabin in one fall. Plan for your first month to be the weakest, not the average.

## A worked example

This is an example to show the method, not a forecast for any home. A 3 bedroom Fort Worth house has sat unsold, and holding it costs the owner $2,000 a month (example: loan payment, insurance, yearly ownership bills, basic utilities and lawn). The bookings line uses the likely case from our free estimator for a 3 bedroom Fort Worth home, read October 17, 2026: $38,700 a year, about $250 a night with 42% of nights booked, built on AirROI data for August 2025 to July 2026.

******** ********

| Line | Average month | Basis |
| - | - | - |
| Bookings for the nights | $3,225 | $38,700 a year divided by 12. The estimator's months run from $2,700 (February) to $3,800 (May) |
| Platform fees and discounts | −$603 | 18.7%, measured on our own 75 stays |
| Cleaning | $0 | The guest cleaning fee pays the cleaner |
| Utilities, internet and streaming above the empty house | −$250 | Example; use your own bills |
| Supplies | −$97 | 3% of bookings, example |
| Repairs and wear reserve | −$161 | 5% of bookings, example |
| Left if you run it yourself | $2,114 | Before your own hours |
| Management at 20% | −$524 | 20% of $2,622, the bookings after platform fees |
| Left with full service | $1,590 |  |
| Setup, paid once | $20,000 | Example, inside Awning's $10,000 to $30,000 range |

Read the table three ways.

- **Against the holding cost.** With full service, an average month leaves $1,590, about 80% of the $2,000 it costs to hold the house. Run yourself, $2,114 covers all of it, before your hours. A February that books $2,700 leaves about $1,290 with full service, and the owner pays the rest.

- **Against the setup.** $20,000 takes about 13 months to earn back at $1,590 a month, or about 9 and a half months at $2,114. If you expect to sell within six months, buying all new furniture rarely pays back. A test that uses the furniture already in the house can: $6,000 for beds, linens and supplies earns back in about 4 months at the same pace.

- **Against your other options.** Compare what is left, and your hours, with your best written lease quote (no furniture needed) and with what a price cut would cost you.

## The risks, plainly

- **Setup money that does not come back.** The payback math above is the biggest risk for an owner who still plans to sell soon.

- **A slow first season.** New listings start with no reviews, and the weak months in AirROI's data (January, February and September) are weak.

- **More competition every year.** AirROI counted 29% more active Fort Worth listings over one year, while its revenue figure rose 2.3% (August 2025 to July 2026). More homes are chasing the same guests.

- **Wear and damage.** Hundreds of guest nights a year wear floors, walls and furniture. At our Fort Worth home a $100 damage payment in July 2026 and a $120 damage charge in September 2026 were collected through the platforms. Not every loss comes back.

- **Insurance gaps.** The Insurance Information Institute said in March 2026 that standard homeowner policies generally do not cover commercial activity such as short term renting, and that owners who do not tell their insurer risk denied claims. Tell your agent, and get a written quote for a policy that covers paying guests before the first stay.

- **Guests on the books when a buyer appears.** If a host cancels a confirmed Airbnb stay, the fee is 10% of the reservation amount more than 30 days before check in, 25% from 48 hours to 30 days, and 50% inside 48 hours, with a $50 minimum, and Airbnb may block those dates (Help Center, read October 17, 2026). A short booking window keeps that risk small.

- **Your time.** Hosts in a 2025 PriceLabs survey reported 8.3 hours a week on their listings. Our guide to [self managing versus hiring a manager](https://listandhost.com/blog/self-managing-vs-hiring-an-airbnb-manager/) breaks the hours down.

## How to test it in 90 days

1. **Write down your bar.** Your monthly holding cost, your best written lease quote and the lowest sale price you would take. Decide now what result keeps the test going.

2. **Get a range for the house.** Low, likely and high, with the slow months, from a source that shows its basis.

3. **Cap the setup.** Use what is already in the house, buy for sleep and photos first, and set a hard budget before the first purchase.

4. **Keep the booking window short.** Airbnb lets you open your calendar 3, 6, 9, 12 or 24 months ahead (Help Center, read October 17, 2026). Three months keeps future bookings few if a buyer comes along.

5. **Price for the first three reviews.** Start under the market, use the new listing discount, and raise prices as reviews land. Our [cabin loft launch](https://listandhost.com/results/ozark-cabin-loft/) shows every price move we made.

6. **Track four numbers every week.** Nights booked, average night, payouts after platform fees and costs paid. Our guide to [dynamic pricing](https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/) explains how nightly prices should move.

7. **Decide on day 90** with the scorecard below.

| Check at day 90 | Keep going if | Rethink if |
| - | - | - |
| Payouts after costs, last 30 days | They cover the holding cost | They cover less than half of it |
| Nights booked | Rising month over month at steady prices | Flat, even after price cuts |
| Reviews | Three or more, all four or five stars | A low score on cleanliness or accuracy |
| Setup payback | Inside the months you plan to keep the house | Longer than you plan to own it |
| Your hours | They fit your week, or you have help | More than you can give |

Basis: our own rule of thumb from running three homes, not a promise of any result.

If you sell later, the test is not wasted. Payout reports and reviews give a buyer real numbers instead of a projection, which is what our [guide for buyers](https://listandhost.com/blog/buying-a-short-term-rental-numbers-to-check/) tells them to ask for. Ninety days is a short record, so expect buyers to weigh it lightly.

Full service covers Fort Worth, [Arlington](https://listandhost.com/arlington/), [Dallas](https://listandhost.com/dallas/) and the Buffalo River region of Arkansas for 20% of booking revenue, with the launch included and no setup fee. Elsewhere in the United States we offer co hosting, a launch package or remote pricing, each quoted in writing and explained on our [services page](https://listandhost.com/services/). Our proof is the homes our team runs, one of them a Guest Favorite rated 4.9 on Airbnb as of October 16, 2026, and every figure with how we counted it is on our [results page](https://listandhost.com/results/).

## Quick answers

**Should I rent my house instead of selling it?**

It comes down to three numbers: what the empty house costs you each month, what renting would leave after fees and costs, and what a price cut would cost you. Setup costs and slow months can make a short term rental lose money, so run a short, capped test before you commit.

**How much does it cost to turn a house into a short term rental?**

Awning puts furnishing a typical short term rental at roughly $10,000 to $30,000 (June 2026). RedAwning puts a 3 bedroom house at $15,000 to $35,000 (updated May 2026). A house that still has its furniture can start for far less.

**How fast does a new short term rental get its first booking?**

It depends on the market and the price. Our cabin loft in the Buffalo River region got its first booking 3 days after going live on September 24, 2026, priced under the market until its first reviews. Plan for the first month to be the slowest.

**Can I keep the house listed for sale while it takes guests?**

It can be done, but showings and stays compete for the same days. Block showing times on the calendar and keep the booking window short, because cancelling a confirmed Airbnb stay costs the host 10% to 50% of the reservation amount, with a $50 minimum, per Airbnb's Help Center on October 17, 2026.

**Is a long term lease better than a short term rental for a house that will not sell?**

A lease brings steadier money with less work and no furniture, but a tenant living there makes a quick sale harder. A short term rental can bring more in a good month, with more work, cost and swing by season. Compare both against what the empty house costs you.

# Harrison, AR Short Term Rentals: What Homes Earn

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/harrison-ar-short-term-rental-income/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Harrison, AR short term rental income from AirROI data read Oct 18, 2026: $151 a night, 37.5% booked, longer stays than cabin towns. Get a free estimate.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

A short term rental in Harrison, Arkansas earns less per night than a cabin near Jasper or Ponca, but its bookings are spread more evenly through the year and its guests stay longer. AirROI's Harrison data for August 2025 to July 2026, read October 18, 2026, shows 97 active listings averaging $151 a night, with 37.5% of nights booked and $16,516 a year per listing. For how we run homes here, see our page on [property management in Harrison and the Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/).

**Short answer.** Harrison is a steadier, lower rate town than the cabin areas. It books the same share of nights as the Jasper area, 37.5% against 37.3%, at about two thirds of the rate. Its slowest month brought in 55% of its best month's revenue, against 40% around Jasper, and stays average 5.1 nights against 3.1. Work, medical and family guests sit beside weekend visitors to the Buffalo region, so 30 night stays deserve a real price here.

## Harrison by the numbers: AirROI data read October 18, 2026

| AirROI, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026 | Harrison | Jasper area | Ponca |
| - | - | - | - |
| Active listings | 97 | 180 | 37 |
| Average night | $151 | $232 | $364 |
| Share of nights booked | 37.5% | 37.3% | 28.5% |
| Average listing, yearly revenue | $16,516 | $26,695 | $31,038 |
| Average stay | 5.1 nights | 3.1 nights | 2.6 nights |
| Booked ahead, average | 32 days | 46 days | 66 days |
| Busiest and slowest month, nights booked | 49.9% Oct, 29.9% Jul | 54.3% Oct, 23.6% Jan | 44.7% Oct, 17.7% Jan |
| Slowest month's revenue as a share of the best | 55% | 40% | 38% |

Basis: AirROI's public pages for Harrison, Jasper and Ponca, trailing twelve months to July 2026 (pages updated September 12, 2026), read October 18, 2026. The last row is our division of AirROI's lowest monthly average revenue by its highest. Yearly averages include listings open only part of the year.

Harrison's year swings less: its busiest month books 49.9% of nights and its slowest 29.9%, a gap of 20 points, against 31 around Jasper and 27 at Ponca. Guests also stay longer and book closer to the date, which reads like travel for work and family as much as for vacations.

| Harrison listings | Bottom quarter | Middle | Top quarter | Top 10% |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Nightly rate | $106 | $140 | $182 | $232 or more |
| Share of nights booked | 19% | 35% | 55% | 76% or more |
| Revenue per open night | $35 | $52 | $74 | $102 |
| Monthly revenue | $795 | $1,515 | $2,413 | $3,551 or more |

Basis: AirROI's Harrison page, same period, read October 18, 2026. Each row ranks listings on its own measure, so a column is not one home.

Open every night, the middle listing's $52 per open night works out to about $19,000 a year in nightly revenue and the top quarter's $74 to about $27,000, before cleaning and platform fees. The six top earners on AirROI's page took in $37,121 to $57,589 over the same year; four are 2 or 3 bedroom homes, and three name a hot tub in the title. Most of the market is small: of the 93 listings AirROI sorts by size, 57 have 1 or 2 bedrooms.

Peak months are October, May and June, at 44.7% booked, $161 a night and $2,187 a month on average. The low months, January, February and April, run 31.7%, $151 and $1,369. Low season earns 63% of peak here, against 48% around Jasper in our [Buffalo River season guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/buffalo-river-cabin-income-by-season/). October is the best single month at 49.9% booked. It lines up with fall color: a foliage forecast issued October 18, 2026 puts peak color on the Buffalo National River around November 4, and our event calendar for the homes our team runs in the region tags October 15 to November 10, 2026 as the color season.

## Who stays in Harrison

- **Medical and work stays.** North Arkansas Regional Medical Center, on N. Main Street, offers emergency care, surgery, imaging, women's health, pediatrics, cardiology and orthopedics. As of October 17, 2026, AMN Healthcare's job page for Harrison listed a 13 week travel nurse contract in labor and delivery, starting October 31, 2026. A 13 week contract means about three months of housing near the hospital.

- **North Arkansas College.** The two year public college had 2,089 students in federal College Navigator data read October 18, 2026. Campus visits, graduations and new staff looking for housing can bring short and monthly stays.

- **Families and team weekends.** Arkansas Tourism says the city hosts more than 75 sports tournaments a year, from volleyball, softball and baseball to 7 on 7 football and basketball, plus summer concerts and hot air balloons each fall. Homes that sleep 6 or more, 48.5% of Harrison listings per AirROI, suit those weekends.

- **Travelers on US 65.** Harrison sits on US 65 about an hour south of Branson, per Arkansas Tourism. AirROI's top guest home cities are Springfield, Dallas, Little Rock, Harrison and Fayetteville, and no city dominates: Springfield sends 2.6% of guests. Branson itself is a pricier market; the same AirROI page lists nearby Branson West at $268 a night. See our [Branson page](https://listandhost.com/branson/).

- **Buffalo region visitors.** The park headquarters for the Buffalo National River is in Harrison, and the park's directions start from Harrison, south on Highway 7, Highway 43 or US 65. Arkansas Tourism puts the Buffalo River Trail at Pruitt 12 miles from downtown, with the elk herd and waterfalls like Hemmed In Hollow nearby. Sell the trails, waterfalls, elk and scenic drives, never the river: the upper river often runs too low to float in summer and fall.

## Nightly stays vs 30 night stays

Harrison already leans long. Stays average 5.1 nights, from 5.2 in September down to 3.4 in October, when fall color brings leisure guests. Of the 97 listings, 22 (22.7%) set a minimum stay of 30 nights or more, against 19.4% around Jasper. Airbnb counts 28 nights or more as a monthly stay: hosts can set a monthly discount at 28 nights, and Airbnb collects and pays out monthly. For budgets, the GSA lodging rate for Harrison is the standard $113 a night for October 2026 to September 2027, a ceiling for federal travelers, not a price to charge.

Whether a monthly guest pays off depends on how your home books now. Here is what a 30 night stay must bring in to match a month of nightly guests.

| Your home books like | Nights booked in 30 | Nightly revenue for the month | Stays to clean | A 30 night stay matches it at |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| The middle listing | 10 to 11 (35%) | $1,515 | About 2 | About $51 a night |
| The top quarter | 16 to 17 (55%) | $2,413 | About 3 | About $80 a night |
| The top 10% | 23 or more (76%) | $3,551 or more | 4 to 5 | About $118 a night or more |

Basis: AirROI's Harrison monthly revenue and occupancy tiers, read October 18, 2026. Stays to clean is nights divided by the 5.1 night average stay; the last column is monthly revenue divided by 30, our math. Revenue as AirROI reports it, before platform fees.

A home that books like the middle listing comes out ahead with any monthly guest paying more than about $1,500, and cleans once instead of twice. A top quarter home needs about $2,400, before the saved cleans and the utilities a monthly guest uses. Test it against your own last twelve months, and price long stays that run through October with the peak in mind. Our [guide to 30 night stays for traveling nurses](https://listandhost.com/blog/traveling-nurse-30-night-stays-fort-worth/) covers setup and screening; it is written for Fort Worth, but the steps carry over.

## What guests here filter for

AirROI's Harrison amenity data (August 2025 to July 2026, read October 18, 2026) shows correlation, not cause: homes with more amenities also tend to be larger.

- **WiFi and a kitchen.** Listings without WiFi averaged $9,162 a year, against $17,001 with it; without a kitchen, $9,506 against $16,897. Work and monthly guests treat both as basics.

- **A hot tub.** Only 16.5% of Harrison listings have one, against 27.8% around Jasper. Those averaged $25,728 a year, against $14,696 without, so a tub stands out here. Our [hot tub guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/hot-tub-rentals-upkeep-and-earnings/) covers the upkeep.

- **Family gear.** The 11.3% of listings with a high chair averaged $25,484, against $15,369.

- **Work and medical basics.** Blackout curtains, a washer and dryer, a desk, parking near the door, and drive times to the hospital and the college in the listing. See our [guest ready checklist](https://listandhost.com/blog/getting-a-home-guest-ready-checklist/).

The review bar is high in AirROI's Harrison data, read October 18, 2026: a 4.92 average rating, 80.4% Superhosts and 76.3% of listings marked Guest Favorite. Only 13.4% allow Instant Book, and winter stays book 23 days ahead against 35 in summer, so a home that books on the spot catches short notice trips. See [how Airbnb ranks listings](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-ranking-and-guest-favorite/).

# Fort Worth Event Calendar for Hosts: 2026 and 2027

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-event-calendar-for-hosts-2026-2027/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Fort Worth event dates hosts should price for in 2026 and 2027: Stock Show, Dickies Arena, TCU, Cowtown and NCAA, and how far prices move. Free estimate.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

The Fort Worth dates that move short term rental prices between now and the end of 2027 are the Fort Worth Stock Show and Rodeo (January 15 to February 6, 2027), the NCHA Futurity (November 16 to December 12, 2026), the Cowtown Marathon weekend (February 27 and 28, 2027), the NCAA men's basketball rounds at Dickies Arena (March 18 and 20, 2027), TCU home football Saturdays and a full year of Dickies Arena shows. Price those dates early and above a normal weekend: in our October 13, 2026 scan of 3 and 4 bedroom homes near the venues, a two night event weekend asked about 1.5 to 1.7 times a two night midweek stay, and weekends that were nearly sold out asked 2 to 3.5 times.

Below is the calendar we price around, read from official pages on October 17, 2026, and how prices should move for each kind of event. It is the planning sheet behind our [Fort Worth Airbnb management](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/); costs, income by bedroom and how to choose a manager are in our [Fort Worth owner guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-airbnb-management-owner-guide/).

## How far event dates move prices

Three sets of numbers, each with its own basis:

- **Live asking prices near the venues.** On October 13, 2026 we checked Airbnb for 3 and 4 bedroom homes for 6 guests near the Cultural District, TCU and the Stockyards. Two night midweek stays had median totals of $463 and $468, cleaning included. Event weekends with about a third of homes still open asked $704 to $800. The TCU homecoming weekend, 97% gone ten days out, asked a median of $1,618 for the homes left, and the Monster Trucks weekend, 89% gone a month out, asked $1,010. The Stock Show opening weekend asked $738 with 46% of homes still open, 94 days out.

- **What guests paid at the home our team runs.** From August through October 2026, its Friday and Saturday nights averaged $236 and other nights $139, after discounts and before cleaning, about 1.7 times.

- **How early guests book.** AirROI puts the Fort Worth average at 38 days between booking and arrival (August 2025 to July 2026). At the home our team runs, guests booked weekend stays a median of 44 days out and weeknight only stays a median of 1 day out.

Cheaper homes sell first, so a high leftover median shows demand, not a price every home will get. Every date we checked is in our [Fort Worth market report for October 2026](https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-short-term-rental-market-report-october-2026/).

## How pricing should move, by type of event

We sort each date into one of four types before we set a price, a floor and a minimum stay. A floor is the lowest price a night may ever sell for; automatic tools may go above it, never below. The full method is in [dynamic pricing explained for owners](https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/).

| Type | Examples | How the price moves | Minimum stay |
| - | - | - | - |
| Citywide, weeks long | Stock Show, NCHA shows | Weeknights rise too, not only weekends. Keep weekly discounts small | 2 nights; welcome weekly stays |
| One big weekend, known months ahead | TCU homecoming, Cowtown, Colonial, two arena shows in one weekend | Set it 60 or more days out. Hold or raise when fewer than 1 in 4 similar homes are open | 2 nights; 3 for the biggest |
| Late reveal | NCAA basketball and gymnastics | The crowd is known only days before. Hold the price; no last minute discounts | 2 nights, any arrival day |
| One show night | A Monday or midweek concert | A modest lift on that night only | 1 night |

### Stock Show: price 23 nights, not 6

The 2026 show counted 1,012,925 visitors, down 250,995 from about 1.26 million in 2025, in a year with five days of sleet and freezing rain, as reported by Carnival Warehouse on April 17, 2026. What follows for hosts:

1. **The opening weekend is a long weekend.** Martin Luther King Jr. Day is Monday, January 18, 2027, and the arena lists the Cowboys of Color Rodeo that day. Price Sunday night, January 17, as an event night.

2. **Weeknights are event nights.** At the home our team runs, Stock Show weeknights ask $299 and weekends $379, against $149 to $199 on ordinary weeknights. Asking prices as of October 17, 2026, not results.

3. **Guests plan in the fall.** Rodeo tickets for 2027 went on sale September 14, 2026, per the arena's event page. Have prices loaded by then, and load the 2028 dates the day the show posts them.

4. **Plan for weather.** Keep ice melt on hand and line up a backup cleaner.

Minimum stays, discounts and the mistakes we made are in our [Stock Show and Dickies Arena host playbook](https://listandhost.com/blog/stock-show-and-dickies-arena-weekends-for-hosts/).

### Dickies Arena: count the shows per weekend

The arena seats up to 14,000 for a concert, per its own page, and on October 17, 2026 its list already ran to November 6, 2027. Our rule: one Saturday show makes a strong weekend; two shows in one weekend, or one act playing two nights, makes a big one. March 2027 stacks up early: Don Omar on Saturday the 6th, The Love of Soul Tour on Saturday the 13th, Greta Van Fleet on Monday the 15th, the NCAA rounds that week and Hans Zimmer on Monday the 22nd. A single Monday show lifts that one night only.

### TCU football: Saturdays, homecoming and graduation

Home games fill Friday and Saturday nights together. The three 2026 home games played so far drew 37,600 to 46,139 fans each, per the season page read October 17, 2026. In our October 13 scan, homecoming weekend had only 7 of 214 homes still open ten days out. For 2027, TCU hosts Alcorn State on September 4, Labor Day weekend, and North Texas on September 11, per FBSchedules on April 17, 2026. Its Big 12 home games against Arizona State, Baylor, Houston and Texas Tech had no dates there; add each one the day it is set. Mark commencement too: TCU planned to confer degrees on more than 2,800 candidates over May 8 and 9, 2026.

### Cowtown: a runners' weekend

The Cowtown starts and finishes at the Will Rogers Memorial Center. NBC 5 reported that the 2026 race expected about 28,000 runners from all 50 states. Runners book Friday and Saturday nights, so set a 2 night minimum, and offer a later Sunday checkout if your cleaner can manage it: a marathoner who finishes late on Sunday morning wants a shower before the drive home. Jo Koy plays Dickies Arena the same Saturday. The home our team runs asked $319 a night for that Friday and Saturday on October 17, 2026.

### NCAA weekends: price for the bracket

When Fort Worth last hosted the men's first and second rounds, in 2022, the arena says they sold out with more than 13,000 fans, $11.5 million in direct spending and 14,000 room nights. The catch is timing: the NCAA names the teams on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027, four days before the first game.

- Hold your price for Wednesday through Saturday night until Selection Sunday. Keep fill rules and last minute discounts off those nights.

- Allow Wednesday arrivals and keep the minimum at 2 nights. A team that loses Thursday goes home Friday.

- Once the bracket is out, check similar homes every day. Those four days are the booking window for most fans.

The women's gymnastics championships, April 15 and 17, 2027, are in their ninth straight year in Fort Worth; the arena credits the last edition with more than 8,500 visitors and an estimated 12,000 room nights. Teams qualify at regional meets in the weeks before, so price it the same way.

### Horse shows: long stays, not weekends

The NCHA Futurity, Super Stakes and Summer Spectacular bring riders, owners and families who stay for days or weeks. They reward a weekly price that beats a hotel, fast replies to multi night inquiries and a clear answer on where a truck and trailer can park. For stays of a month or more, see our guide to [30 night stays in Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/blog/traveling-nurse-30-night-stays-fort-worth/).

### Arlington and Dallas dates spill over

Big games at AT&T Stadium fill homes across the area: the Big 12 Championship on Friday, December 4, 2026, the Cotton Bowl quarterfinal on January 1, 2027 and a Cotton Bowl semifinal on Friday, January 14, 2028. Dallas weekends reach Fort Worth too: over the Texas and OU weekend in October 2026, the home our team runs sold one three night stay at $254 a night after discounts, against $169 across the month. Closer to those venues? See [Airbnb management in Arlington](https://listandhost.com/arlington/) and [Airbnb management in Dallas](https://listandhost.com/dallas/).

## A pricing timeline for any event

1. **Six months out: load the calendar.** Give every date above a floor and a minimum stay.

2. **Three months out: first comparison.** Check what similar homes ask and how many are still open. On October 13, 2026, 94 days before the Stock Show, 46% of homes near the venues were open.

3. **Six to eight weeks out: hold.** Weekend guests book now, a median of 44 days ahead at the home our team runs. When fewer than one in four similar homes are left, hold or raise.

4. **Three weeks out: check the price guests see.** Discounts stack after your price, and a last minute discount can carry an event night well under the number you set; our [guide to DFW weekend and event pricing](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-pricing-strategy-dfw-weekends-and-events/) shows one at our own home. Keep event nights out of automatic cuts.

5. **The final week: fill the gaps.** Open any one night gap beside a booking to one night stays.

6. **After the event: write down what sold.** The price, the booking date and the share of homes still open set next year's floor.

Doing this by hand for dozens of dates a year is real work. It is the core of our [full service management and remote pricing](https://listandhost.com/services/); what each costs is on our [pricing page](https://listandhost.com/pricing/). You can also [see results from homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/), including the [Fort Worth home near Dickies Arena](https://listandhost.com/results/fort-worth-home/).

## Questions owners ask

**When is the 2027 Fort Worth Stock Show?**

January 15 to February 6, 2027, 23 days, at the Will Rogers Memorial Center and Dickies Arena. The opening weekend runs into Martin Luther King Jr. Day on Monday, January 18.

**When is the 2027 Cowtown Marathon?**

The race's registration page lists the 5K and 10K on Saturday, February 27, 2027 and the half marathon, marathon and ultra on Sunday, February 28. Confirm on the race's own site before you price.

**Which NCAA events are at Dickies Arena in 2027?**

The men's basketball first and second rounds on March 18 and 20, and the women's gymnastics championships on April 15 and 17. Men's teams are named on Selection Sunday, March 14.

**How much more should a Fort Worth home charge on an event weekend?**

It depends on how full the weekend already is. In our October 13, 2026 scan, event weekends with about a third of homes still open asked 1.5 to 1.7 times a midweek stay, and nearly sold out weekends asked 2 to 3.5 times for the homes left. Size, look and reviews decide where your home lands.

**How far ahead should I set event prices?**

As soon as the dates are posted. AirROI puts the Fort Worth average at 38 days between booking and arrival (August 2025 to July 2026). Late reveal events like the NCAA rounds are the exception: hold the price until the teams are known.

# Fort Worth Airbnb Management: The Complete Owner Guide

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-airbnb-management-owner-guide/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: What a Fort Worth Airbnb manager does and costs, income by bedroom count and neighborhood with sources, the key event dates and how to choose one.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

A Fort Worth Airbnb manager runs your listing, daily pricing, guest messages, cleaning and repairs, and full service commonly costs about 18% to 25% of booking revenue, according to Awning's 2026 fee guide (updated October 1, 2026). Public data puts the typical Fort Worth listing at about $24,000 to $43,000 a year in bookings, and our estimator puts a 3 bedroom home at about $31,100 to $50,400 a year before platform fees and costs, built on AirROI market data for August 2025 to July 2026.

Below: what a manager does here, what you pay on top of the fee, income by bedroom count and neighborhood, the event calendar and how to choose. We are a management company with a stake in the answer, and our team runs a 3 bedroom home in west Fort Worth, so we show its records where they help. Estimates are not promises. For our own service details, see [Airbnb management in Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/).

## What an Airbnb manager does in Fort Worth

Full service means the manager takes the whole job: listing and photos, daily prices, every guest message, cleaners around every stay, repairs, reviews and a monthly statement. Our [A to Z checklist of what a management company does](https://listandhost.com/blog/what-does-an-airbnb-management-company-do/) covers each piece. Three parts matter more in Fort Worth than in most cities.

- **Event weekends sell early.** At the 3 bedroom home our team runs, stays with a Friday or Saturday night were booked a median of 44 days ahead (August to October 2026). Dickies Arena shows, TCU games and the Stock Show need prices and floors set months out.

- **Weeknights sell at the last minute.** At the same home, weeknight only stays were booked a median of 1 day ahead. They go to whoever replies first with a clean home ready.

- **Long stays fill the gaps.** AirROI puts the average Fort Worth stay at 6.8 nights, and 32.9% of listings take only stays of 30 nights or more (August 2025 to July 2026). See [30 night stays for traveling nurses](https://listandhost.com/blog/traveling-nurse-30-night-stays-fort-worth/).

| You decide | The manager runs |
| - | - |
| Your floor price and repair limit | Daily prices, minimum stays and discounts inside that floor |
| Nights you block for yourself | Guest messages, check in steps and reviews |
| Any repair or purchase over your limit | Cleaners, turnovers, restocking and small fixes |
| Whether to keep the agreement | Statements, payout records and damage claims |

## What short term rental management costs in Fort Worth

| Type of management | Typical fee | Who does the hands on work |
| - | - | - |
| Marketing and pricing only | About 10% to 15% | You or your own cleaner |
| Full service with a local team | About 18% to 25% | The manager |
| Luxury, resort or master lease | About 25% to 40% | The manager |

Basis: Awning, Airbnb management fees 2026, updated October 1, 2026. RedAwning's Fort Worth page lists 22% to 30% for full service and 15% to 20% for co hosting (no date shown, read October 17, 2026).

The percentage is only half the quote. In the example year from our [guide to management fees](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-management-fees/), $40,000 of nightly rent plus $6,000 of cleaning fees, the same 20% comes to $9,200, $8,000 or $6,760, depending on whether it is taken from everything guests paid, the rent before platform fees, or the rent after them. Here is a likely year for a 3 bedroom Fort Worth home.

********

| Likely year, 3 bedroom Fort Worth home | Amount |
| - | - |
| Gross bookings for the nights | $38,700 |
| Platform fees and discounts, about 18.7% | −$7,237 |
| After platform fees and discounts | $31,463 |
| Management fee at 20% | −$6,293 |
| Left before your own costs | $25,170 |

Basis: our estimator's likely case, $250 a night with 42% of nights booked (AirROI, August 2025 to July 2026, sized to 3 bedrooms). The 18.7% is what platforms kept, fees and discounts together, across 75 accepted stays at the homes our team runs, as booked October 16, 2026. The fee is our own 20%, taken after the platform's host fee. Cleaning fees pay the cleaner and are left out. An illustration, not a forecast.

With any manager, you still pay utilities, internet, supplies, repairs and insurance. Cleaning is usually covered by the guest cleaning fee: AirROI reports 87.4% of Fort Worth listings charge one, with a median of $126 (August 2025 to July 2026). Some managers add setup fees or markups on repairs and supplies, so get each in writing. Our [pricing page](https://listandhost.com/pricing/) shows how we handle every cost.

The fee buys back time. PriceLabs' survey of more than 1,400 hosts found an average of 8.3 hours a week, about 430 hours a year (Global Host Report 2025, reported November 20, 2025). On the example above, the $6,293 fee is about $15 for each of those hours. Our guide to [self managing vs hiring a manager](https://listandhost.com/blog/self-managing-vs-hiring-an-airbnb-manager/) runs the break even math.

## What a Fort Worth Airbnb can earn by bedroom count

Three data services count the market differently. AirROI: $24,276 average year, $225 a night, 41% of nights booked, 1,607 listings (August 2025 to July 2026). Airbtics: $43,000 median year, $184 a night, 61% booked, 1,765 listings (September 2025 to August 2026). GuestFavorites: $39,299 a year, $200 a night, 54% booked, 1,362 listings (January to September 2026). Listings vary even more: per AirROI for the same period, a bottom quarter listing earns about $1,132 a month, the median $2,379, the top quarter $4,160 and the top tenth $6,438 or more.

Size explains much of that. These are the Fort Worth ranges our [estimator](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) uses.

| Bedrooms | Nightly rate | Share of nights booked | Yearly gross bookings, low to high | Likely |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| 1 | $125 to $155 | 39% to 51% | $17,800 to $28,900 | $22,200 |
| 2 | $165 to $205 | 38% to 50% | $23,100 to $37,300 | $28,700 |
| 3 | $225 to $275 | 38% to 50% | $31,100 to $50,400 | $38,700 |
| 4 | $300 to $365 | 37% to 50% | $40,700 to $65,900 | $50,600 |
| 5 | $400 to $490 | 36% to 48% | $53,100 to $86,000 | $66,100 |
| 6 or more | $550 to $675 | 36% to 47% | $71,700 to $115,800 | $89,100 |

Basis: AirROI public market data for Fort Worth, August 2025 to July 2026, spread across sizes with the market's own bedroom mix, with June and July 2026 replaced by the average of May and August because the World Cup matches at the Arlington stadium (June 14 to July 14, 2026) lifted them. Gross bookings are nightly rate times nights booked over 365 nights, before platform fees, cleaning, any management fee and your costs. Cross check: RedAwning shows $153, $197, $285 and $405 a night for 1 to 4 bedrooms (no date shown, read October 17, 2026).

Our own record: from August through October 2026, the 3 bedroom home our team runs was booked 56 of 92 nights (61%) at a $179 average night, with $11,706 in payouts (as of October 16, 2026, October as booked). That is more nights than the high case at a lower rate, because quiet weeknights sell near a $149 floor. Weekends averaged $236 and weeknights $139. Three months is a short record. See the [Fort Worth results page](https://listandhost.com/results/fort-worth-home/) and our guide to [how much an Airbnb can make in Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/blog/how-much-can-an-airbnb-make-in-fort-worth/).

## Income by Fort Worth neighborhood

We found no public source with dated yearly income by Fort Worth neighborhood, and the undated figures disagree. Here they are side by side.

| Area | What brings guests | Average nightly rate, Airbtics (listings) | Yearly revenue published elsewhere, no date shown |
| - | - | - | - |
| Stockyards | The Historic Stockyards, weekend rodeos, live music | $274 (30) | $33,215 (BnBCalc) |
| Cultural District | Dickies Arena, Will Rogers Memorial Center, museums | $192 (14) | About $5,000 a month (RedAwning); $28,470 (BnBCalc) |
| University Area | TCU games, graduations, family visits | $193 (5) | None found |
| Near Southside | Restaurants, the medical district | $130 (19) | $23,800 (BnBCalc) |
| Downtown | Sundance Square, the convention center | Not shown | $72,011 (RedAwning); $33,660 (BnBCalc) |
| Arlington Heights and Sunset Heights | Near the Cultural District and West 7th | Not shown | $73,881 and $77,842 (RedAwning) |
| Fairmount | Historic homes south of downtown | Not shown | $52,679 (RedAwning); $21,900 (BnBCalc) |

Basis: Airbtics' Fort Worth page, updated October 16, 2026, shows no period for its neighborhood rates. RedAwning and BnBCalc show no date for theirs; BnBCalc credits Mashvisor and Wheelhouse. All read October 17, 2026.

Read these as hints. Downtown is $72,011 in one source and $33,660 in another, and a Stockyards night is $130 or $274 depending on who counts. What moves a home more is its size and sleeping count, its drive to Dickies Arena, TCU and the Stockyards, parking for a group, and the listing itself. Live prices help more than averages: on October 13, 2026, our scan of 3 and 4 bedroom homes for 6 guests near the venues found two night weekend stays asking a median of $754, against $463 and $468 midweek, cleaning included. The full scan is in our [October 2026 Fort Worth market report](https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-short-term-rental-market-report-october-2026/).

## The Fort Worth event calendar owners price around

Visit Fort Worth counted 11.5 million visitors in 2024. For an owner, a handful of dates set the year: the NCHA Futurity at the Will Rogers Memorial Center (November 16 to December 12, 2026), the Cotton Bowl Classic at AT&T Stadium in Arlington (January 1, 2027), the Fort Worth Stock Show and Rodeo (January 15 to February 6, 2027, 23 days), the NCAA men's basketball rounds at Dickies Arena (March 18 and 20, 2027), the MAIN ST. Fort Worth Arts Festival downtown (April 15 to 18, 2027) and the Charles Schwab Challenge at Colonial Country Club (May 27 to 30, 2027), plus Dickies Arena shows, TCU home football each fall and Cowboys games in Arlington. Dates were read from the official pages on October 17, 2026; schedules change, so check before you price. Even the biggest dates are not sold out months ahead: on October 13, 2026, 46% of homes in our scan area were still open for the Stock Show opening weekend. Every date through December 2027, with the price move and minimum stay each kind of event earns, is in our [Fort Worth event calendar for hosts](https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-event-calendar-for-hosts-2026-2027/).

The data services disagree on the best season. AirROI names June, May and March as strongest and January, February and September as weakest, but its year includes the World Cup summer. Airbtics says demand peaks in October and November and is weakest in August. Do not price summer 2027 off summer 2026. Our [Stock Show and Dickies Arena playbook](https://listandhost.com/blog/stock-show-and-dickies-arena-weekends-for-hosts/) covers floors and minimum stays.

## How to choose an Airbnb manager in Fort Worth

A manager makes the most sense if you live far from the home, work full time, own two or more homes, or do not want to be on call for last minute guests. Our [15 questions to ask an Airbnb manager](https://listandhost.com/blog/questions-to-ask-an-airbnb-manager/) cover fees, statements, reviews and contracts in any market. In Fort Worth, add four that test local know how, and get every answer in writing.

1. **Show me last year's Stock Show prices.** Ask for the opening weekend rate and minimum stay at a home they ran. A manager with no event prices sells those nights at the weekday rate.

2. **How do you price a Futurity weeknight?** The horse shows fill weeknights for weeks at a time and reward a weekly price, not a weekend one.

3. **Who turns the home on the Saturday after a Dickies Arena show?** Event weekends stack checkouts and check ins on the same day, so ask for the backup cleaner by name.

4. **Who answers a weeknight request at 9 PM?** As the booking lead times above show, weeknight guests here often book the day before, and the first clear reply wins them.

Red flags: a promised income figure, results you cannot trace to a real home, prices that never change, and a fee with no written base; in the fee example above, the same 20% landed anywhere from $6,760 to $9,200 a year. Ask for a sample statement too, like our [example owner dashboard](https://listandhost.com/owner-dashboard/). Weighing a big company? See [local team vs national managers](https://listandhost.com/compare/national-managers/).

Full service in Fort Worth, the rest of Dallas Fort Worth and the Buffalo River region of Arkansas. Co hosting or remote pricing anywhere else in the United States. # Can You Run an Airbnb Remotely? What Must Stay Local

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/running-an-airbnb-from-out-of-town/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Yes, if cleaning, repairs and keys stay local. Turnovers a year in 8 remote markets, drive times from Fort Worth and what runs from anywhere, 2026 data.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

Yes, you can run an Airbnb remotely, as long as three jobs stay local: cleaning and restocking between stays, repairs, and a way into the home when a lock or a key fails. Pricing, guest messages, calendars and reviews can run from anywhere, and that split is how our team runs two homes in the Buffalo River region of Arkansas, about seven hours by road from Fort Worth.

We offer remote help and full service, so we have a stake in your answer. Every number below names its source, basis and date. Checked October 18, 2026.

**Short answer.** A remote 3 bedroom home in the markets below needs a local visit about 29 to 50 times a year, one per turnover, plus repairs and the odd lockout. With a cleaner, a backup, a handyman and keyless entry in place, the screen work can run from anywhere. If the home turns over 45 or more times a year and you live hours away, a hands on manager is usually the safer choice.

## How many times someone must be at the house

Every new stay means a visit: a clean, a restock and a check that nothing is broken. So a remote owner's workload is set by turnovers a year, the nights a home books divided by the average stay. Here it is for a 3 bedroom home in the markets where we offer remote pricing and co hosting, with our two full service markets at the bottom.

****

| Market | Drive from Fort Worth | Nights booked a year, 3 bedroom | Average stay, nights | Turnovers a year, about | Booked ahead, average |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Granbury, TX | 45 min, 40 mi | 126 | 4.3 | 29 | 41 days |
| Glen Rose, TX | 1 hr, 57 mi | 144 | 3.2 | 45 | 46 days |
| Broken Bow, OK | 3 hr 30 min, 211 mi | 135 | 2.7 | 50 | 49 days |
| Wimberley, TX | 3 hr 40 min, 226 mi | 128 | 2.8 | 46 | 54 days |
| Fredericksburg, TX | 4 hr, 237 mi | 128 | 2.6 | 49 | 45 days |
| Hot Springs, AR | 4 hr 55 min, 318 mi | 128 | 3.3 | 39 | 44 days |
| Eureka Springs, AR | 6 hr 30 min, 406 mi | 130 | 2.7 | 48 | 47 days |
| Branson, MO | 7 hr 10 min, 457 mi | 131 | 3.3 | 40 | 50 days |
| Our full service markets, for comparison |  |  |  |  |  |
| Buffalo River region, AR (Jasper area) | 7 hr, 426 mi | 140 | 3.1 | 45 | 46 days |
| Fort Worth, TX | Our base | 155 | 6.8 | 23 | 38 days |

Basis: nights booked are our estimator's likely case for a 3 bedroom home (share of nights booked times 365), from AirROI data for August 2025 to July 2026, read October 16, 2026. Average stay and days booked ahead: AirROI averages for all home sizes, same period, read October 18, 2026. Turnovers: nights divided by average stay. Drive times: OpenStreetMap routes from downtown Fort Worth, no traffic or stops, checked October 18, 2026. Estimates, not a forecast for any home.

- **Short stays mean more visits.** With about the same nights booked, a Fredericksburg home (2.6 night stays) needs about 20 more cleans a year than a Granbury home (4.3).

- **Your home's mix beats the market average.** The Fort Worth home our team runs averages 2.7 nights a stay against 6.8 for its market (every stay booked as of October 16, 2026), so it turns over about two and a half times as often as its row suggests.

- **Busy months stack up.** The three homes our team runs had 26 stays arriving in October 2026, as booked on October 16: 26 cleans in one month. A same day turnover gets the five hours between an 11 AM checkout and a 4 PM check in.

## What must be local, and who does it

Four jobs cannot be done from a laptop. Each needs a named person near the home, and a backup.

| Job | What it covers | Who does it | How often |
| - | - | - | - |
| Cleaning | Turnover clean, laundry, photos, damage check | A local cleaner and a backup | Every stay |
| Restocking | Paper goods, soap, coffee, trash bags, linens | The cleaner counts; you ship, or they buy in town | Every stay |
| Lock and key | A dead lock battery, a failed code, a lockout | A local person with a spare key | Rare, and always urgent |
| Repairs and upkeep | Leaks, hot water, air conditioning, yard, hot tub, freeze prep | A handyman who answers the phone, plus scheduled service | As needed, and by season |

Basis: how the work splits at the three homes our team runs, where people who live near the homes do every one of these jobs.

**Cleaners.** At the homes our team runs, a turnover costs $75 to $200 depending on the home and the group, and guests pay a cleaning fee of $85 to $225 (our cleaners' rates and our listings, October 2026). Each home has a backup cleaner, and it gets used: our Arkansas cleaner does not work holidays or the day after, so holiday turnovers go to the backup.

**Repairs.** In October 2026 our cleaner noticed lukewarm hot water at our Arkansas cabin. A local handyman replaced the old 40 gallon heater on October 13, for $592 in parts and $280 in labor. That is the team a remote owner needs: someone who notices, and someone who fixes.

**The drive.** From Fort Worth, Hot Springs is 5 hours and Branson 7, too far to fix a 2 PM problem before a 4 PM arrival. Even Granbury is a 90 minute round trip for a dead lock battery.

## What runs from anywhere

- **Pricing.** Guests in these eight markets book 41 to 54 days ahead on average (AirROI, August 2025 to July 2026), so a night's price has to be right six to eight weeks out. Peak months book further ahead: October stays in Eureka Springs 73 days, November stays in Broken Bow 72 and July stays in Hot Springs 66, in the same data. Events set their own clock: Fort Worth's NCHA Futurity runs November 16 to December 12, 2026, and the 2027 Stock Show January 15 to February 6. From September 21 to October 16, 2026, our engine logged 133 nightly price changes and 52 minimum stay changes across the three homes our team runs, none needing anyone at a house. Our [dynamic pricing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/) explains floors, gap nights and minimum stays.

- **Guest messages.** Guests write at night and some book late: at our Fort Worth home, weeknight only stays were booked a median of one day before arrival (August to October 2026). Our engine checks messages every 30 minutes, check in details go out on their own three days before arrival, and every Airbnb listing our team runs showed a 100% response rate on October 16, 2026. A remote co host can answer a guest at 10 PM. Only a local cleaner can have the home ready by 4 PM.

- **Calendars.** Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com and a direct site on one calendar, so a night sold on one closes on the others. Of the 35 stays booked at the glass house our team runs as of October 16, 2026, 7 came from Vrbo, Booking.com or our direct site. See our [booking site comparison](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-vs-vrbo-vs-booking-com-for-owners/).

- **Reviews.** Guests are reviewed the day they leave, and every review gets a reply. The glass house is rated 4.9 on Airbnb from 11 reviews, a Guest Favorite, as of October 16, 2026.

Airbnb lets an owner add a co host at one of three access levels, up to full access with pricing and messages, so remote help works inside your listing. Our [co host vs property manager guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-co-host-vs-property-manager/) compares the models and fees.

## Locks, cameras outside only, and supplies

**Locks.** Keyless entry is what makes remote hosting work. Since August 21, 2024, Airbnb has connected Schlage, August and Yale smart locks to listings in the US and Canada: each reservation gets its own code that works only during the stay, and the host is alerted when a lock goes offline or its battery runs low. Keep a second way in that only your local person controls, for the day the battery or the wifi fails.

**Cameras, outside only.** Since April 30, 2024, Airbnb has banned security cameras that monitor any indoor space, even switched off. Outdoor cameras are allowed when the listing discloses where each one is, but never where guests expect privacy, such as an enclosed outdoor shower. Noise monitors that measure sound levels without recording are allowed inside if disclosed, but not in bedrooms, bathrooms or sleeping areas. A disclosed driveway camera and a living room noise monitor show a remote owner arrivals and a party in the making, without watching anyone inside.

**Sensors.** Temperature and water leak alerts on your phone catch a frozen pipe before it floods. The American Red Cross advises keeping the heat at 55 degrees or higher when you are away in cold weather.

**Supplies.** Set a count for each item the cleaner checks at every turnover, and keep two full sets of sheets per bed. At our Arkansas homes the cleaner tells us what is low; we ship most of it, and the cleaner buys small items in town from a credit we keep with them. Amazon would not ship aerosol cans to one of those rural addresses. Our [guest ready checklist](https://listandhost.com/blog/getting-a-home-guest-ready-checklist/) lists what to stock.

## When a hands on manager beats remote help

Remote help, a remote co host or remote pricing, covers the screen work and leaves the four local jobs with you. Full service takes all of it, and usually fits better when:

- **The home turns over 45 or more times a year** and you live hours away. In the table, that is Broken Bow, Fredericksburg, Eureka Springs, Wimberley and Glen Rose.

- **The home has systems on a schedule.** A hot tub needs a check every stay, and the EPA says a household septic system should be inspected at least every three years. Our [hot tub guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/hot-tub-rentals-upkeep-and-earnings/) covers the upkeep.

- **Winters freeze.** A burst pipe needs someone at the home that morning.

- **You have no cleaner yet, or no backup.** Hiring cleaners from far away is often the hardest part.

- **You want Vrbo and Booking.com run too.** Airbnb's co host access covers Airbnb only.

- **You own two or more homes,** or plan to.

Remote help fits when someone you trust lives near the home, you have a cleaner and a backup, stays run longer (Granbury, about 29 turnovers a year) and pricing or messages are the weak spot. Live close and enjoy the work? Our [self managing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/self-managing-vs-hiring-an-airbnb-manager/) has the hours and dollars, and [a solo co host vs full service](https://listandhost.com/compare/solo-co-host/) goes line by line.

## How our remote pricing and co hosting works

Full service in Fort Worth, the rest of Dallas Fort Worth and the Buffalo River region of Arkansas. Co hosting or remote pricing anywhere else in the United States. Outside the full service area, the work splits as this guide describes: we run the screens, your local people keep the hands on work.

- **Remote pricing.** You add us as a co host with pricing access, and we run the rules we use on the homes our team runs: a floor you approve, weekend and event prices, gap nights and minimum stays, every change logged. Priced per listing each month, quoted in writing after a [free look](https://listandhost.com/services/#free-look).

- **Co hosting.** You keep your listing, reviews, cleaner and payouts. We run pricing, every guest message, the cleaning schedule, calendars and reviews, at a fee quoted in writing after a free look. More in the [co hosting section of our services page](https://listandhost.com/services/#cohost).

- **Full service.** In Fort Worth, Arlington, Dallas and the Buffalo River region we also run the local jobs, for 20% of booking revenue (October 2026). Booking revenue is the nightly rent plus any extra guest fees, after the platform's host fee. Taxes and cleaning fees are not part of it. Every line is on our [pricing page](https://listandhost.com/pricing/).

## Questions owners ask

**Can you run an Airbnb remotely?**

Yes, if three jobs stay local: cleaning and restocking, repairs, and a way in when a lock fails. Pricing, guest messages, calendars and reviews can run from anywhere, by you or a remote co host.

**How often does someone need to be at a remote Airbnb?**

At every turnover: about 29 to 50 a year for a 3 bedroom home in the remote markets we cover, using AirROI's average stay for August 2025 to July 2026. Repairs and lockouts come on top.

**Can I put security cameras in my Airbnb?**

Not inside. Since April 30, 2024, Airbnb bans cameras that monitor indoor spaces, even switched off. Outdoor cameras are allowed when the listing discloses each one, never in places such as an enclosed outdoor shower or a sauna.

**How far ahead do remote prices need to be right?**

In the eight remote markets in our table, guests book 41 to 54 days ahead on average (AirROI, August 2025 to July 2026), and peak months up to 73 days out. Set peak month and event prices at least 10 weeks ahead.

**Own a home you cannot drive to every week?** [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) built from your address, your home and live booking data for your market, with the basis for every number. It is an estimate, not a promise of income.
