# Buying a Buffalo River Region Cabin to Rent: The Numbers

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/buying-a-buffalo-river-region-cabin-to-rent/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: What a Buffalo River region cabin grosses by bedroom count, Newton County asking prices on Oct 18, 2026, real costs and the checks before you offer.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

In our estimator’s likely case, a cabin in the Buffalo River region grosses about $21,600 a year with one bedroom, $37,700 with three and $86,700 with six or more, before platform fees and costs (AirROI data for the Jasper area, August 2025 to July 2026). On October 18, 2026, Newton County houses for sale asked 7 to 12 times that likely gross at the middle of each bedroom count, so any house you look at has to prove its own numbers. Dated numbers from the two homes our team runs here follow the checks; our service is [Buffalo River cabin management](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/).

## What a cabin here earns before you buy

AirROI tracked 180 active listings around Jasper from August 2025 to July 2026: $232 a night on average, 37.3% of nights booked and $26,695 a year for the average listing, all sizes together. Our estimator spreads that average across sizes.

| Bedrooms | Likely night | Nights booked, likely | Likely yearly gross | Low to high | Cleaning fee |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| 1 | $150 | 39% (144 nights) | $21,600 | $16,500 to $28,400 | $60 |
| 2 | $200 | 38% (140 nights) | $28,000 | $21,400 to $36,800 | $95 |
| 3 | $270 | 38% (140 nights) | $37,700 | $28,900 to $49,600 | $130 |
| 4 | $360 | 38% (137 nights) | $49,300 | $37,700 to $64,800 | $190 |
| 5 | $480 | 37% (134 nights) | $64,300 | $49,200 to $84,700 | $230 |
| 6 or more | $665 | 36% (130 nights) | $86,700 | $66,200 to $114,000 | $275 |

Basis: List & Host estimator inputs, updated October 16, 2026, from AirROI’s Jasper area data (180 listings, August 2025 to July 2026). The table is our model, not AirROI’s: it spreads the market average using the area’s bedroom mix and size ratios checked against AirROI’s April 2026 cabin market data. Low is a 10% lower rate at the middle listing’s revenue per open night; high is a 10% higher rate at the top quarter’s. Gross is what guests pay for the nights before platform fees, cleaning fees left out, for a home open all year; many listings are not. Cleaning scales the area’s $95 median fee by size.

The spread between homes is wide: the top quarter of Jasper area listings earned $3,767 a month and the middle listing $2,153 (AirROI, same period). Fall sells out and winter does not. On October 13, 2026, our Airbnb search around Jasper found 3% of the 149 entire homes for 8 guests still open for the October 16 weekend, against 42% for a late November weekend and 57% for Christmas.

## Jasper and Ponca are different businesses

| Area | Listings | Average night | Nights booked | Average listing, a year | Average stay | Booked ahead |
| - | - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Jasper area | 180 | $232 | 37.3% | $26,695 | 3.1 nights | 46 days |
| Ponca | 37 | $364 | 28.5% | $31,038 | 2.6 nights | 66 days |

Basis: AirROI public market data, August 2025 to July 2026, read October 18, 2026. Averages across all home sizes.

Ponca sells on high rates with fewer nights. Its average listing earned $98 per open night against $88 around Jasper (AirROI’s revenue per available night), but on about 104 booked nights a year instead of 136, with shorter stays booked about two months ahead. Price those few strong weeks early, hold minimum stays and expect more cleans per night sold. 37.8% of Ponca listings have a hot tub, against 27.8% around Jasper, and Ponca revenue fell 6.2% from the year before, against 3.7%.

Our estimator uses the Jasper area numbers for the whole region, so near Ponca, read its nightly rate as low and its nights booked as high.

## What is for sale now, and the price against gross

On October 18, 2026, Redfin listed 87 houses for sale in Newton County, land left out. Across the 85 distinct asking prices on its list pages, the middle was $370,000 and half asked between $220,000 and $578,900. 37 of the 87 showed a price cut, 18 of them in the last 30 days. Asking is not selling: Redfin’s median sale price, all home types, was $326,769 for the three months ending September 2026, up 0.4% on a year before, with 16 homes sold in September.

| Bedrooms | Houses for sale | Middle asking price | Likely yearly gross | Asking price ÷ likely gross |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| 1 | 8 | $230,450 | $21,600 | 10.7 |
| 2 | 20 | $207,700 | $28,000 | 7.4 |
| 3 | 31 | $469,000 | $37,700 | 12.4 |
| 4 | 14 | $372,000 | $49,300 | 7.5 |
| 5 or more | 12 | $667,450 | $64,300 (5 bedrooms) | 10.4 |

Basis: Redfin list pages for houses for sale in Newton County, read October 18, 2026, grouped by the bedrooms each listing shows. Likely gross from the table above. The last column is the gross multiple. Groups are small, and one listing can move a median a long way.

Read the multiple as a filter, not a valuation. Many of these are full time homes, farms or acreage priced on the land, and some have never hosted a guest. To match the 2 and 4 bedroom groups at about 7.5, a 3 bedroom asking $469,000 would need to gross about $62,500 a year, above our high case of $49,600. Our guide to [the numbers to check before buying a short term rental](https://listandhost.com/blog/buying-a-short-term-rental-numbers-to-check/) shows how to test a seller’s figures.

## The costs a cabin carries

Here is the likely 3 bedroom, as an illustration, not a forecast.

********

| Line | Example | Basis |
| - | - | - |
| Likely yearly gross | $37,700 | Estimator, 3 bedrooms |
| Platform fees and discounts | less $7,050 | 18.7%, measured on 75 stays at the homes our team runs, as booked October 16, 2026 |
| After platform fees | $30,650 |  |
| Full service management, if you hire it | less $6,130 | 20% of booking revenue after platform fees |
| Left for every other cost | $24,520 | Before cleaning, utilities, hot tub care, supplies, repairs, insurance and any loan |

- **Platform fees.** Airbnb’s single fee is 15.5% for most hosts, and hosts who connect through property management software must use it. With discounts and refunds, the platform kept 19.9% of list price on our Airbnb stays (64) and 8.0% on Vrbo (9), as of October 16, 2026.

- **Cleaning.** The Jasper area median cleaning fee is $95 (AirROI, same period). At its 3.1 night average stay, 140 nights is about 45 cleans a year. Guests pay the fee; you pay the cleaner every turn, plus laundry and a holiday backup. Our guest fees in the region are $85 for a one bedroom loft and $225 for a home that sleeps 10.

- **Hot tub upkeep.** 27.8% of Jasper area listings have one, and they averaged $43,474 a year against $20,242 without (AirROI); bigger homes tend to have tubs, so the tub is not the whole gap. Power runs about $27 a month for typical home use (Hydropool’s 187 kWh example at EIA’s July 2026 Arkansas home rate of 14.33 cents), more with guests, and a service visit costs $155 to $320 (Thumbtack, 2026). See our [hot tub guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/hot-tub-rentals-upkeep-and-earnings/).

- **Winter.** On the estimator’s monthly pattern, the likely 3 bedroom grosses about $1,900 in January and $1,700 in February, against $4,300 in June. Heat does not stop with bookings; the American Red Cross advises keeping an empty home at 55 degrees or more in cold weather. Month by month: [Buffalo River cabin income by season](https://listandhost.com/blog/buffalo-river-cabin-income-by-season/).

- **Everything else.** Utilities, internet, supplies, repairs and a written short term rental insurance quote.

## Checks before you make an offer

1. **The road.** Drive it after rain, and in winter if you can. At the homes our team runs, the drive ends on a steep hill of loose gravel, so every listing and check in message tells guests what vehicle to bring. Ask who keeps the road up after ice.

2. **The water.** Many cabins run on a private well. The EPA advises testing one every year for total coliform bacteria, nitrates, total dissolved solids and pH. A general inspection may skip it: the one on the land our team runs excluded the well’s water and the septic system, by its own scope.

3. **The septic, sized for your guest count.** The EPA says a household system should be inspected at least every three years and is typically pumped every three to five, more often with heavy use. A new group every few days is heavy use. Ask the inspector whether the tank and drain field fit the guest count you plan to list.

4. **Signal and internet.** 96.1% of Jasper area listings have wifi (AirROI). The FCC’s National Broadband Map shows which internet providers report service at an address and the mobile coverage carriers report, but the FCC notes that mobile coverage reflects use outdoors, not indoors. Test inside the house with your own phone; in our experience signal is weak at many homes here.

5. **The guest count.** The average Jasper area listing sleeps 5.4 (AirROI), and our October 13 search found 149 entire homes for 8 guests against 481 places for 2. Big homes face less competition, but every extra guest needs a bed, hot water, parking and septic room. Our glass house sleeps 10, and its average group is 4 guests across stays booked through June 2027, as of October 16, 2026.

6. **The records.** Ask for 24 months of platform exports and the bank deposits that match, and plan as if the reviews stay with the seller.

## What a buyer should not count on

**The river.** The Buffalo River Chamber says floating on the upper river is mostly limited to spring and early summer, and fall only in a wet year. A park spokesperson told KY3 in July 2022 that the upper river around Ponca tends to dry up in peak summer. A view of the river is not floatable water in August.

**Park crowds.** The National Park Service counted a record 1,686,348 park visits in 2024 and 1,393,246 in 2025, when May through July brought 49% of visits and September through November 18%. Yet October is the most booked month for rentals in AirROI’s Jasper area data. Cabin guests come for fall color, elk and cool nights.

**What does sell.** A deck with a view, trails, a hot tub and dark skies. The Buffalo National River became the first International Dark Sky Park in Arkansas in June 2019, according to the National Park Service, and Arkansas Tourism sends elk watchers to Boxley Valley at dawn and dusk.

## Questions buyers ask

**How much does a Buffalo River region cabin make a year?**

In our estimator’s likely case, built on AirROI data for the Jasper area from August 2025 to July 2026, gross runs about $21,600 a year for 1 bedroom, $37,700 for 3 and $86,700 for 6 or more, before platform fees and costs. It is a market estimate, not a promise for any house.

**What do houses cost in Newton County right now?**

On October 18, 2026, Redfin listed 87 houses for sale there. The middle of the 85 distinct asking prices on its list pages was $370,000, and 37 of the 87 showed a price cut. Its median sale price was $326,769 for the three months ending September 2026.

**Is Ponca or Jasper better for a rental?**

They are different businesses. From August 2025 to July 2026, AirROI shows Ponca at $364 a night with 28.5% of nights booked, and the Jasper area at $232 with 37.3%. Ponca earns on high rates and fewer nights.

**Can I count on the river to fill a cabin?**

No. A park spokesperson told KY3 in July 2022 that the upper river around Ponca tends to dry up in peak summer. Sell the deck, the trails, the stars and the hot tub.

**Looking at a cabin in the region?** [Run the free estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/?m=buffalo-river#estimator) for its bedrooms, baths and hot tub before you offer, with a low, likely and high case and the basis for every number. It is an estimate, not a promise of income.

# Airbnb or Long Term Rental in Fort Worth and Dallas?

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-or-long-term-rental-fort-worth-dallas/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Airbnb or a lease in Fort Worth and Dallas? 2026 HUD and Zillow rents by bedroom against short term net, the break even occupancy and a free estimate.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

For most Fort Worth and Dallas homes in late 2026, a long term lease leaves more money each month than a short term rental that books at the market's average pace, once platform fees, cleaning, utilities and furniture come out. A short term rental wins when the home can book about half its nights or more at market rates (45% to 57% of nights, depending on city and size, if you run it yourself), when you want to use the home some weeks, or when a lease would get in the way of a sale.

Below: lease rents by bedroom count from HUD and Zillow, what a short term rental grosses and keeps on our free estimator, the costs and risks both ways, and the break even occupancy. We run short term rentals in [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/), [Arlington](https://listandhost.com/arlington/) and [Dallas](https://listandhost.com/dallas/), so weigh our side with that in mind.

## The short answer: when each one wins

- **A lease wins** when the home would book at or below the market average, when you want the same money every month with few hours, or when you do not want to buy furniture or be on call.

- **A short term rental wins** when the home clears the break even line below, when you want to stay there yourself between guests, or when you may sell within a year and want no tenant in the house.

- **Monthly furnished stays** sit between the two; see the middle path below.

## What a lease brings by bedroom count

HUD's Fair Market Rent is the 40th percentile gross rent, meaning rent plus the utilities a tenant pays, for standard quality homes of every kind in the area. The Fort Worth Arlington area covers Tarrant, Johnson and Parker counties; the Dallas area covers Collin, Dallas, Denton, Ellis, Hunt, Kaufman and Rockwall counties.

| Bedrooms | Fort Worth Arlington FY2027 | Fort Worth Arlington FY2026 | Dallas FY2027 | Dallas FY2026 |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| 1 | $1,481 | $1,473 | $1,536 | $1,648 |
| 2 | $1,745 | $1,723 | $1,807 | $1,931 |
| 3 | $2,284 | $2,273 | $2,275 | $2,431 |
| 4 | $2,866 | $2,815 | $2,892 | $3,091 |

Basis: HUD Fair Market Rents, county files for FY2027 (in effect since October 1, 2026) and FY2026 (October 2025 to September 2026), read October 18, 2026. Monthly gross rent, utilities included.

The Dallas figures fell about 6% to 7% from FY2026 to FY2027, while Fort Worth Arlington rose less than 2%, so the two areas now sit within $65 of each other at every size. Zillow's Observed Rent Index, a typical asking rent across homes and apartments, was $1,612 in Fort Worth and $1,604 in Dallas in September 2026, up 1.3% and 1.0% in a year. For single family homes across the metro it was $2,345, close to HUD's 3 bedroom figures. The Census Bureau shows the slack: 11.7% of the metro's rental homes stood vacant and for rent in the second quarter of 2026 (margin of error 2.5 points), against 7.3% nationally.

Below we use HUD's FY2027 figure as the lease rent. It includes utilities, which flatters the lease a little, and a newer or larger house can lease for more. If you have a written lease quote, use it.

## What a short term rental grosses and keeps

Bookings are our estimator's likely case (data dated October 16, 2026): AirROI public market data for August 2025 to July 2026, spread across sizes, with World Cup June and July replaced by the average of May and August.

******************** ********************

| Fort Worth, per year | 1 bedroom | 2 bedrooms | 3 bedrooms | 4 bedrooms |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Nightly rate and nights booked | $140, 158 nights | $185, 155 nights | $250, 155 nights | $335, 151 nights |
| Bookings for the nights | $22,200 | $28,700 | $38,700 | $50,600 |
| Platform fees and discounts, 18.7% | −$4,151 | −$5,367 | −$7,237 | −$9,462 |
| Cleaning per turnover | −$885 (59 at $15) | −$1,311 (57 at $23) | −$1,824 (57 at $32) | −$2,632 (56 at $47) |
| Utilities, internet and streaming | −$2,700 | −$3,300 | −$4,200 | −$5,100 |
| Supplies, 3% of bookings | −$666 | −$861 | −$1,161 | −$1,518 |
| Furnishing spread over 3 years | −$2,000 | −$3,333 | −$5,000 | −$8,333 |
| Left per year, run yourself | $11,798 | $14,528 | $19,278 | $23,555 |
| Left per month | $983 | $1,211 | $1,607 | $1,963 |
| Lease per month, for comparison | $1,419 | $1,672 | $2,189 | $2,747 |

Basis. Platform fees and discounts: 18.7% of guest charges across 75 stays at the three homes our team runs, check ins July 2026 to June 2027, as booked on October 16, 2026. Cleaning: turnovers are nights divided by 2.7, the average stay at our Fort Worth home (October 16, 2026); guests pay the estimator's market cleaning fee ($80, $125, $170, $250) and the cleaner gets the same, so each turn costs the platform's 18.7% share of that fee. Utilities: our example of $225 to $425 a month by size, built from our Fort Worth 3 bedroom's electricity of about $200 to $230 a month in 2026 plus water, gas, trash, internet and streaming. Supplies: our example. Furnishing: the low end of RedAwning's ranges by size ($6,000, $10,000, $15,000, $25,000; updated May 2026) over 3 years. Lease: HUD FY2027 rent less one empty month every two years. Loan, insurance and the yearly bills of owning the house are left out of both sides.

The cleaning line is cautious: at our Fort Worth home guests pay $110 and the cleaner earns $90 a turn (October 2026), so a turn about breaks even after platform fees. Dallas, same method:

| Dallas | Likely bookings a year | Left per month, run yourself | Lease per month |
| - | - | - | - |
| 1 bedroom | $23,000 ($160 a night, 39% booked) | $1,047 | $1,472 |
| 2 bedrooms | $29,700 ($215, 38% booked) | $1,292 | $1,732 |
| 3 bedrooms | $40,100 ($290, 38% booked) | $1,727 | $2,180 |
| 4 bedrooms | $52,400 ($385, 37% booked) | $2,121 | $2,772 |

Basis: our estimator's likely case for Dallas (AirROI, August 2025 to July 2026) with the Fort Worth cost lines and Dallas cleaning fees ($75, $115, $155, $230). Lease: HUD FY2027 Dallas rent less one empty month every two years.

At the market's average pace the lease leaves more at every size: about $580 a month more for a 3 bedroom in Fort Worth and $450 in Dallas. Near the top of the market it flips. The estimator's high case, built on the top quarter of listings, puts a Fort Worth 3 bedroom at $275 a night with 50% booked, $50,400 a year, leaving about $2,342 a month run yourself, $150 more than the lease. A Dallas 3 bedroom at $315 with about 45% booked leaves $2,429, about $250 more. Averages include listings not open every night, so a home open all year can beat them, or not.

## Costs both ways, side by side

| Cost | Lease | Short term |
| - | - | - |
| Furniture | Usually none | RedAwning puts a 3 bedroom at $15,000 to $35,000 (May 2026) |
| Utilities | Often the tenant's | Yours, booked or not |
| Cleaning | At move out | Every stay, mostly paid by the guest cleaning fee |
| Platform fees | No fee per booking | 18.7% of guest charges, discounts included, on our own bookings (October 2026) |
| Management, if hired | Texas average 8.87% of collected rent, plus a placement fee averaging 76.6% of a month's rent (iPropertyManagement, updated September 23, 2026) | Our full service fee: 20% of booking revenue after platform fees, never on cleaning fees (pricing) |
| Empty time | Weeks between tenants | Every unbooked night |
| Wear | One household | About 57 groups a year on our 3 bedroom math |
| Your time | Mostly at move in, move out and repairs | 8.3 hours a week on average in a 2025 PriceLabs host survey |

## Time and risk

- **Vacancy.** One empty month costs a lease a full month of rent, and the Census figure above says tenants have plenty to choose from. A short term rental spreads the risk across every night.

- **Seasons.** A lease pays the same every month. On the estimator's likely case a Fort Worth 3 bedroom books about $2,700 in February and $3,800 in May; a Dallas 3 bedroom swings from $2,400 in February to $3,900 in March. Event weeks run the other way: the Fort Worth Stock Show runs January 15 to February 6, 2027, and our floors for the home we run near the venues those weeks are $299 on weeknights and $379 on weekends. See our [event calendar](https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-event-calendar-for-hosts-2026-2027/).

- **Wear and damage.** Our Fort Worth home collected a $100 damage payment from one guest through Airbnb in July 2026, and $170 in two resolution payments with one September 2026 stay, one of them for extra pets (our booking records, October 2026). Not every loss comes back.

- **Insurance.** The Insurance Information Institute said in March 2026 that standard homeowner policies generally do not cover short term renting. Get a written quote for the use you choose.

- **Management.** Stays with only weeknights at our Fort Worth home were booked a median of one day ahead (August to October 2026), so someone answers fast every day. Our [self managing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/self-managing-vs-hiring-an-airbnb-manager/) estimates 17 to 38 hours a month for one home with about eight stays.

- **Flexibility.** A lease commits the home for its term. A short term calendar can close to new bookings any day, though booked stays still need hosting or a costly cancellation. Our [guide for unsold houses](https://listandhost.com/blog/house-not-selling-short-term-rental/) covers selling while hosting.

## Break even: the occupancy a short term rental needs

The share of nights a short term home must book, at the estimator's likely nightly rate, to leave as much as the lease above. In brackets: the bookings needed per calendar night, booked or not.

| Bedrooms | Fort Worth, run yourself | Fort Worth, both managed | Dallas, run yourself | Dallas, both managed |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| 1 | 57% ($80) | 66% ($92) | 51% ($82) | 58% ($94) |
| 2 | 54% ($99) | 62% ($115) | 47% ($101) | 54% ($116) |
| 3 | 53% ($132) | 61% ($154) | 45% ($130) | 52% ($151) |
| 4 | 52% ($174) | 61% ($204) | 45% ($172) | 52% ($201) |

Basis: the cost lines above, October 18, 2026. Both managed: our 20% fee on the short term side; on the lease side the Texas average of 8.87% plus 76.6% of a month's rent per new tenant and a $247 renewal fee, one each every two years (iPropertyManagement, updated September 23, 2026).

For scale, AirROI puts the average listing at 41% of nights booked in Fort Worth and 38% in Dallas (August 2025 to July 2026), while Airbtics puts Fort Worth at 61% (September 2025 to August 2026). The bar sits above the average listing and within reach of a strong one. Dallas needs fewer nights because its nightly rates run higher at the same HUD rents. Each extra $100 a month of lease rent raises a Fort Worth 3 bedroom's bar by nearly 2 points.

## The middle path: 30 night stays

Furnished stays of a month or more mean one turnover instead of ten. In early October 2026 a four week stay at our Fort Worth 3 bedroom priced at about $112 a night, about $3,100 before cleaning, against HUD's $2,284 lease figure for the size. You still carry utilities, furniture and gaps between contracts. The federal lodging rate for Fort Worth, $192 a night from October 2026 to September 2027, is a rough ceiling on traveler lodging pay, not a price to charge. Our [guide to 30 night stays for traveling nurses](https://listandhost.com/blog/traveling-nurse-30-night-stays-fort-worth/) covers pricing and setup.

## Where List & Host fits

We run short term rentals, not long term leases. Full service covers Fort Worth, Arlington, Dallas and the Buffalo River region of Arkansas for 20% of booking revenue, with co hosting or remote pricing elsewhere ([services](https://listandhost.com/services/)). If your home lands under the break even line, your estimate will show it. Our proof is the homes our team runs, with every figure and how we counted it on our [results page](https://listandhost.com/results/).

## Questions owners ask

**Is Airbnb more profitable than a long term rental in Fort Worth or Dallas?**

At the market's average pace in 2026, usually not, once costs come out. On our estimator's likely case a Fort Worth 3 bedroom run short term leaves about $1,607 a month, against $2,189 from a lease at HUD's FY2027 rent. A home that books like the top quarter of the market can pass the lease if you run it yourself.

**What occupancy does a short term rental need to beat a lease?**

At the estimator's likely nightly rates, about 52% to 57% of nights in Fort Worth and 45% to 51% in Dallas if you run it yourself, or 61% to 66% and 52% to 58% with a manager on both sides, as of October 2026.

**How much does a 3 bedroom rent for in Fort Worth and Dallas?**

HUD's FY2027 Fair Market Rent, in effect since October 1, 2026, is $2,284 a month for the Fort Worth Arlington area and $2,275 for the Dallas area, utilities included. Zillow's typical asking rent for single family homes across the metro was $2,345 in September 2026.

**Can I try short term first and lease later?**

Yes. Keep the furniture budget small and judge the test on payouts after costs. Going the other way is harder, because a lease commits the home for its term.

**Want your own break even line?** [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/): low, likely and high bookings for your home with the basis for every number, to set against your best lease quote. An estimate is not a promise of income.

# Airbnb Pricing Strategy in DFW: Why Weekends Sell Too Cheap

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-pricing-strategy-dfw-weekends-and-events/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Why DFW Airbnb weekends and event dates sell too cheap, the gap we measured in October 2026, and the pricing rules our engine runs. Get a free estimate.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

The Airbnb pricing strategy that works in Dallas Fort Worth prices every night on its own demand: weekends and event dates first and early, weeknights flexible, and a floor under all of it. Many DFW listings, including the home our team runs in Fort Worth this fall, underprice weekends and event dates for three plain reasons: those nights sell weeks before most hosts look, a flat base price with a weekend percentage cannot reach an event weekend, and discounts and automatic cuts land on the nights that need them least. Below is how big the gap was in our October 2026 price checks, why it happens, and the rules our pricing engine runs on homes in [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/), [Arlington](https://listandhost.com/arlington/) and [Dallas](https://listandhost.com/dallas/).

## How big the weekend and event gap is

On October 13, 2026 we checked live Airbnb asking prices for 3 and 4 bedroom homes for 6 guests around Dickies Arena, TCU, West 7th and the Stockyards. Here is what a two night stay asked on different dates.

| Two night stay | What was on | Homes still open | Median total asked | Against midweek |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Tue Oct 20 to Thu Oct 22, and Tue Oct 27 to Thu Oct 29 | An ordinary midweek | 48% and 55% | $463 and $468 | 1.0 times |
| Fri Oct 30 to Sun Nov 1 | Teddy Swims at Dickies Arena, TCU vs Kansas | 38% | $754 | 1.6 times |
| Fri Jan 15 to Sun Jan 17, 2027 | Stock Show opening weekend | 46% | $738 | 1.6 times |
| Fri Nov 13 to Sun Nov 15 | Hot Wheels Monster Trucks, TCU vs Kansas State, Cowboys vs 49ers | 11% | $1,010 | 2.2 times |
| Fri Oct 23 to Sun Oct 25 | TCU homecoming, Mecum Auctions at Dickies Arena | 3% | $1,618 | 3.5 times |

Basis: our live Airbnb search, October 13, 2026, entire homes, first page of results, 5 to 15 comparable homes per stay; homes still open is Airbnb's count out of 214 homes in the area. Totals are nightly rate plus cleaning, before taxes: asking prices, not bookings. Against midweek divides by $466, the average of the two midweek medians. On the fullest weekends the homes left skew pricier, so a high leftover median shows demand, not a sure price. Full method in our [Fort Worth market report for October 2026](https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-short-term-rental-market-report-october-2026/).

Our own records agree. At the 3 bedroom home our team runs in Fort Worth, Friday and Saturday nights averaged $236 from August through October 2026, against $139 for other nights, about 1.7 times. Both are what guests paid per night after discounts, before cleaning fees, with October counted as booked on October 16.

So does market data. AirROI's Dallas figures for August 2025 to July 2026 put the year's average nightly rate at $256 and the peak month, June, at $430. That June held the World Cup matches at the Arlington stadium, and guests booked June stays about 56 days ahead, the longest of any month. The tournament is over, but it shows how far and how early a big event pulls rates.

## Why weekends and events get underpriced

### 1. They sell before you look

At the Fort Worth home our team runs, stays that included a Friday or Saturday night were booked a median of 44 days before arrival, and weeknight only stays a median of 1 day before. AirROI puts the average booking window at 38 days in Fort Worth, 41 in Arlington and 30 in Dallas for August 2025 to July 2026. On October 17, 2026, that home had 11 of its next 17 Friday and Saturday nights booked (65%), against 7 of the 43 other nights (16%).

A host who checks prices once a month is mostly reacting to weeknights. By the time an event weekend looks hot, early guests have bought it at last month's price. It happened to us: two fall 2026 weekends booked weeks ahead at about $209 and $248 a night. By mid October, the comparable homes still open on those weekends, the homecoming and Monster Trucks weekends above, asked medians of $1,618 and $1,010 for two nights. Leftovers skew pricey, so the real gap was smaller. It was still a gap.

### 2. A weekend percentage cannot reach an event

Airbnb's weekend adjustment moves Friday and Saturday nights anywhere from 50% below to 50% above your base price, and works only with Smart Pricing off (Airbnb Help Center, read October 17, 2026). That suits an ordinary weekend. It cannot price a Stock Show Saturday: our ordinary Fort Worth weekends already sold at 1.7 times weeknights, and the busiest event weekend that still had 24 homes open asked 2.2 times midweek. Those dates need their own price, set by date. Airbnb lets a custom price override the weekend adjustment, and allows custom prices on single dates with Smart Pricing on.

Flat pricing is common. A 2018 study of 39,837 Airbnb listings and 1,025 hotels in five markets found hosts make limited use of dynamic pricing compared with hotels, and that experienced hosts with more listings vary prices the most (Gibbs and coauthors). A University of Rochester study of more than 18,000 San Francisco listings from 2015 to 2020 found amateur hosts often keep flat rates that ignore demand, costing up to 15% of seller profit against an ideal benchmark (Yufeng Huang, summary published January 28, 2021). Neither covers DFW, but both match what our scans show.

### 3. Discounts stack on the wrong nights

Early bird, weekly, monthly and last minute discounts all come off the nightly price after you set it, and Airbnb notes an early bird discount can take the guest price below your Smart Pricing minimum. On October 13, 2026, a 15% last minute discount took a $329 Halloween weekend price at the home our team runs to about $280 for guests. Early bird discounts hit event weekends hardest, because those nights sell early. Set event floors knowing what comes off after them.

### 4. Automatic cuts reach event nights

Fill rules lower open nights as the date nears, and they do not know what is on at Dickies Arena unless someone tells them. Our engine taught us this. The Friday and Saturday of the John Summit weekend, November 6 and 7, 2026, had slid to $202 a night before a comp check caught it, while similar homes asked $773 and up for the two nights. We set them back to $249 with a two night minimum on October 9, and they sold on Booking.com about four hours later: about $567 for the stay with cleaning, against a comp median of $704. It sold, but cheap. On October 12 an audit found the same rule set to cut the first Futurity week to $161 and $149 a night. Those nights were locked that day, and every event night is now locked against automatic cuts.

### 5. One night bookings break up the weekend

The minimum stay is part of the price. For the Red River weekend in October 2026, when Texas played OU in Dallas, the Fort Worth home set a three night minimum. It sold as one three night stay at $254 a night, about 50% above that home's $169 average night for October, both after discounts and before cleaning. The exception runs the other way: a single open night between two bookings should drop to a one night minimum, or it never sells.

## Not every event is a sellout

On Thursday, October 8, 2026, the Cowboys hosted Tampa Bay at AT&T Stadium. We priced that night at $449 at the Fort Worth home. Still unsold five days out, it came down to $249, then $199, and sold the day before. A weeknight game across the metro does not fill a Fort Worth house like a Saturday show down the street.

Big dates can also look slow early: on October 13, 46% of homes in our area were still open for the Stock Show opening weekend. One snapshot cannot tell late demand from extra supply, so we hold the event floor and recheck rather than cut. When fewer than one in four homes are left for your dates, hold or raise.

## The rules our engine runs in DFW

Here is how our engine handles weekends and events at the Fort Worth home our team runs. The same rules would run on your home, inside a floor you approve. Our [guide to dynamic pricing](https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/) covers each in detail.

| Rule | What it does | A real example |
| - | - | - |
| Floor | No automatic rule may go below it | $149 a night |
| Event list | Each event date gets its own floor and minimum stay, months ahead | Stock Show 2027: $299 weeknights, $379 weekends, two night minimum. New Year's Eve floor: $549 |
| Event lock | Automatic cuts cannot touch event nights | First Futurity week locked October 12, 2026 |
| Weekend minimum, gap exception | Friday and Saturday need two nights; a one night gap stays bookable | October 7 and 8, 2026 sold as two one night stays between two other stays |
| Fill ladder | Open Friday and Saturday nights 22 to 30 days out drop 5% a week, at most 20% under their first price, never below the floor, never below a weeknight in the same week | Under the earlier rule, 10% a week on every night 22 to 35 days out until October 17, 2026: three weeknights cut from $179 to $161 on September 21, 2026, then sold in a four night stay |
| Weekly comp check | Open nights against nearby homes on the same dates | October 13, 2026: open nights 11% to 25% under the median, so 29 nights went up, Thanksgiving from $225 to $319 |
| Log and read back | Every change logged, written, then read back | 133 price and 52 minimum stay changes across the three homes our team runs, September 21 to October 16, 2026 |

Basis: the engine's settings and change log for the Fort Worth home our team runs, as of October 18, 2026. Floors change as the calendar fills. Our rules and results, not a forecast for any other home.

Raises are the hard part for any engine, ours included. A person approves every big raise, and approved nights go on hold so no automatic cut can undo them. Since October 17, 2026 the engine may also make small raises by itself on open nights 31 to 180 days out, at most 20% a move and three nights per home a week, when it has evidence such as a holiday. It is new and moves few nights, so a person still checks event weekends against comps every week. See how the parts fit on our [how it works page](https://listandhost.com/how-it-works/), and the month by month story on the [Fort Worth results page](https://listandhost.com/results/fort-worth-home/).

## A weekend and event checklist for DFW owners

1. **Load the calendars six months out:** Dickies Arena and Will Rogers in Fort Worth, AT&T Stadium and Globe Life Field in Arlington, American Airlines Center and Fair Park in Dallas, plus college football and holidays.

2. **Price weekends first and by date,** not as one percentage on a weeknight base.

3. **Give every event its own floor and minimum stay,** and lock those nights against automatic cuts.

4. **Check comps weekly:** what similar homes ask for your dates, and how many are still open.

5. **Search your own dates as a guest** to see the price left after every discount.

6. **Keep weeknights flexible.** They book late, and a fast reply wins them.

7. **Write down what each event sold for,** so next year's floors start from your numbers.

Every Fort Worth date we price for, from the NCHA Futurity and the Stock Show to the NCAA rounds at Dickies Arena, is listed with its source in our [Fort Worth event calendar for hosts](https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-event-calendar-for-hosts-2026-2027/), and the Cowboys, Big 12, Cotton Bowl and Rangers dates in Arlington are in our [Dallas and Arlington management guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/dallas-arlington-short-term-rental-management/). Schedules change, so check before you price. Arena shows are in our [October market report](https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-short-term-rental-market-report-october-2026/), and our [Stock Show and Dickies Arena playbook](https://listandhost.com/blog/stock-show-and-dickies-arena-weekends-for-hosts/) covers getting the house ready for event crowds.

## Dallas, Arlington and Fort Worth are not one market

By AirROI's figures for August 2025 to July 2026, Dallas books latest, 30 days ahead on average and 19 for February stays, so a price set in spring is stale by the time most guests look. Arlington books furthest ahead, 41 days, around the stadium calendar, and game day groups want beds and parking for everyone. Fort Worth lives on Dickies Arena and Will Rogers weeks, where the Stock Show and the Futurity lift weeknights too. We offer full service in all three cities for 20% of booking revenue, with every fee on our [pricing page](https://listandhost.com/pricing/). Outside our full service area, the same engine is available as [remote pricing](https://listandhost.com/services/). You can also [see results from the homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/).

## Questions owners ask

**How much more should I charge on weekends in Dallas Fort Worth?**

There is no single number. In our October 13, 2026 scan near the Fort Worth venues, an ordinary weekend asked about 1.6 times a midweek stay, and at the home our team runs Friday and Saturday nights sold at about 1.7 times other nights from August through October 2026. Price each weekend by date, from current comps.

**Should I use Airbnb Smart Pricing for a DFW listing?**

It can handle ordinary weeknights. For weekends and event dates, set your own price by date. Airbnb says its weekend adjustment needs Smart Pricing off and tops out at 50% above your base price, and that discounts can take the guest price below your Smart Pricing minimum (Airbnb Help Center, read October 17, 2026).

**How far ahead should I price event dates in DFW?**

As soon as the dates are published. At the home our team runs, stays with a weekend night were booked a median of 44 days ahead (stays on the books as of October 16, 2026).

**What minimum stay should I set for an event weekend?**

We use two nights for most event weekends and three for the biggest, then let any one night gap left around a booking sell as a one night stay.

**Do event dates always sell for more?**

No. The Thursday night Cowboys game on October 8, 2026 did not fill the Fort Worth home our team runs at $449; it sold the day before at $199. An event floor is a guard against cutting too far, not a target.

**Own a home in Dallas, Arlington or Fort Worth?** [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) with nightly rates by season and the basis for every number. It is an estimate, not a promise: your home, street, photos and reviews all change the answer.

**Sources:** [Airbnb Help Center: weekend adjustment for home listings](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/512) · [Airbnb Help Center: Smart Pricing](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1168) · [Gibbs, Guttentag, Gretzel, Yao and Morton: Use of dynamic pricing strategies by Airbnb hosts (2018)](https://www.emerald.com/insight/content/doi/10.1108/IJCHM-09-2016-0540/full/html) · [Yufeng Huang, Simon Business School: tweaking the pricing algorithm (January 28, 2021)](https://simon.rochester.edu/blog/deans-corner/tweaking-pricing-algorithm) · [AirROI: Dallas Airbnb data, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026](https://www.airroi.com/airbnb-data/united-states/texas/dallas) · [AirROI: Arlington Airbnb data, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026](https://www.airroi.com/airbnb-data/united-states/texas/arlington) · [AirROI: Fort Worth Airbnb data, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026](https://www.airroi.com/airbnb-data/united-states/texas/fort-worth) · [Dallas Cowboys: 2026 schedule](https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/nfl-announces-cowboys-2026-complete-17-game-schedule) · [NCHA: updated dates for the 2026 Futurity](https://nchacutting.com/about-us/news/2026/05/19/ncha-announces-updated-dates-for-the-2026-ncha-metallic-cat-futurity) · [Fort Worth Stock Show and Rodeo: visitor questions](https://www.fwssr.com/p/plan-a-visit/frequently-asked-questions) · [Dickies Arena: event list](https://dickiesarena.com/events/list/) · [Homes our team runs: results and how we count them](https://listandhost.com/results/)


# Airbnb Co Host vs Property Manager in DFW: Costs and Duties

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-co-host-vs-property-manager/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Airbnb co host or full service property manager in Dallas Fort Worth? What each does, 2026 fee ranges, the math on a DFW home and who each one fits.

List & Host team · October 18, 2026

An Airbnb co host joins your listing and runs the work you hand over, usually guest messages, pricing and the calendar, for a fee that 2026 industry guides put at about 10% to 25% of booking revenue, while you keep the listing, the reviews and anything that needs hands at the home. A full service property manager runs all of it, cleaners, repairs and supplies included, for about 18% to 30% in the same guides. In Dallas Fort Worth, which one fits depends less on that gap than on how far you live from the home, how often it turns over and who answers when something breaks at night.

We are a management company that offers both, so we have a stake in your answer. Every outside number below names its source and date, and every number of ours says what it is based on. Checked October 17, 2026.

**Short answer.** Pick a co host if you live near the home, have a cleaner you trust and the home books longer stays. Pick full service if you live out of state, the home turns over every few nights, or you want Vrbo and Booking.com run too. On $25,000 to $60,000 a year in booking revenue, roughly the span from the average DFW listing to the top 10% in data services' 2026 figures, a co host at 15% and a manager at 20% are about $1,250 to $3,000 a year apart.

## Co host vs property manager: who does what

Co hosts vary more than managers do, from guest messages only to nearly full service, so the co host column says what is common and what to confirm.

|  | Airbnb co host | Full service property manager |
| - | - | - |
| Whose listing it is | Yours. You keep the listing, the reviews and the payouts | Varies. Some managers move your home into their own account, so ask |
| Guest messages | Usually included | Included |
| Daily pricing | Often included. Ask how often they check nearby homes | Included |
| Cleaning | Some schedule your cleaner. You usually hire and pay them | The manager finds, schedules and checks the cleaners |
| Repairs and lockouts | You or your local helper, unless the co host lives nearby | The manager sends a local pro. Big costs come to you first |
| Supplies | Often you | The manager restocks and bills you |
| Vrbo and Booking.com | Not covered by Airbnb co host access. Each needs its own setup | Usually all of them on one calendar |
| How they are paid | A share of each Airbnb payout that you set up, or an invoice | A percentage, shown on a monthly statement |
| Typical fee, 2026 guides | About 10% to 25% of booking revenue, up to 30% with cleaning and repairs | About 18% to 30%, up to 35% in some markets |
| Your time | The hands on work stays with you | Approvals and a monthly statement |

Basis: the 2026 fee guides in the next table, and the Airbnb Help Center, checked October 17, 2026.

## What an Airbnb co host does, and what Airbnb lets one do

A co host is a person or a company you add to your Airbnb listing, at one of three access levels you choose. **Full access** covers the calendar, pricing, listing details, reservations and guest reviews. **Calendar and messaging** lets them message guests and see the calendar, not change it. **Calendar** is view only. Only the listing owner can set up or change what a co host is paid.

Airbnb can split each payout for you: the cleaning fee, the cleaning fee plus a percentage, a percentage of each booking, or a fixed amount per booking. The split is worked out from the host's earnings after Airbnb's host fee and covers Airbnb stays only. Vrbo has no co host role and no payout split, so a Vrbo helper gets manager access to your account and you pay them yourself (Hostfully, May 2026).

Airbnb launched its Co-Host Network in October 2024 with more than 10,000 co hosts in 10 countries, including the United States. Airbnb said they averaged 4.9 stars, against 4.62 for property managers with more than 30 active listings, as of September 30, 2024, and footnoted that the rating reflects guest reviews of the listings, not the co host's own work. We are a small team, not one of those large managers, but the lesson holds: size does not earn reviews. Attention does.

Co hosts come in three shapes: **a local host** who co hosts on the side and often answers fast (ask who covers when they travel), **a co hosting company** that runs messages, pricing and the cleaning schedule, and **a remote co host** who runs messages and pricing from anywhere while everything at the door stays with your own people.

## What a full service property manager does

A full service manager takes the whole job: the listing and photos, daily pricing, every guest message, cleaners scheduled and checked after each stay, restocking, repairs by local pros, damage claims, reviews and a monthly statement. You approve the big decisions, such as your lowest nightly price and any repair over an agreed amount. Our checklist of [what a management company should do](https://listandhost.com/blog/what-does-an-airbnb-management-company-do/) lists every item, so you can hold any manager to it.

Two things differ a lot between managers. If the listing moves into the manager's account, the reviews and booking history usually stay with them when you leave. And some managers collect guest payments and pay you later, while others let the platforms pay you directly. Either can work if your statement ties every payout to a booking.

## What each one costs in 2026

Three industry guides published fee ranges this year. All three come from companies that sell management or software, so treat them as ranges, not quotes. We found no published fee survey for DFW alone.

| Source | Date | Co host or partial help | Full service |
| - | - | - | - |
| Awning fee guide | Updated October 1, 2026 | 10% to 15% for half service (marketing and pricing) | 18% to 25% |
| TIDY fee guide | 2026 | 10% to 25% for co hosts, 10% to 15% for half service | 20% to 30%, up to 35% in some markets |
| Hostaway glossary | February 12, 2026 | 10% to 30%, higher when cleaning and repairs are included | Not given |

The percentage is only part of the cost. Ask about:

- **Setup fees.** TIDY's 2026 guide puts onboarding at $500 to $2,000 per home. Some managers charge nothing.

- **Markups.** Repairs are billed at vendor cost, sometimes plus a coordination markup that varies by company, per Awning. Ask about supplies too.

- **The base.** The same 20% can be thousands of dollars apart depending on whether it is taken before or after platform fees and whether cleaning fees count. Our [guide to management fees](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-management-fees/) works through an example.

In both models, guests usually pay for cleaning through the cleaning fee. At the 3 bedroom Fort Worth home our team runs, guests pay $110 and the cleaner is paid $90 a turnover (our listing and our cleaner's rate, October 2026).

## The math on a Dallas Fort Worth home

Data services put the typical DFW listing at roughly $24,000 to $43,000 a year. AirROI's averages for August 2025 to July 2026 are $24,276 in Fort Worth, $24,382 in Dallas and $25,379 in Arlington. Medians run higher: GuestFavorites puts Dallas at $39,712 and Arlington at $38,533 for January to September 2026, and Airbtics puts Fort Worth at $43,000 for September 2025 to August 2026. GuestFavorites puts the top 10% of Dallas listings at $63,323 for the same nine months. Here is what each model costs at three round numbers across that range.

| Booking revenue a year | Co host at 15% | Manager at 20% | Manager at 25% | Gap, 15% vs 20% |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| $25,000 | $3,750 | $5,000 | $6,250 | $1,250 |
| $40,000 | $6,000 | $8,000 | $10,000 | $2,000 |
| $60,000 | $9,000 | $12,000 | $15,000 | $3,000 |

Basis: the rates sit inside the 2026 ranges above, and every fee is taken from the same revenue so the columns compare. Real quotes use different bases and extras. This is an illustration, not a forecast for any home.

What does the gap buy? Mostly the hands on work a co host usually leaves with you. Our estimate for one home with about eight stays a month, from our [self managing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/self-managing-vs-hiring-an-airbnb-manager/): restocking 2 to 4 hours a month, maintenance 2 to 6, and problems such as lockouts 1 to 5. That is 60 to 180 hours a year, so on the $40,000 example the $2,000 gap works out to about $11 to $33 an hour. For scale, PriceLabs' 2025 survey of more than 1,400 hosts found 8.3 hours a week spent on listings in total.

If you live 15 minutes away and enjoy the work, that is a fair trade to keep. If you live in another state, you cannot do those hours at all, and paying a local handy person and someone to restock usually closes most of the gap.

## Why DFW changes the answer

- **Turnovers set the workload.** Every new stay means a clean, a restock and a check. AirROI puts the average stay at 6.8 nights in Fort Worth, 6.2 in Arlington and 5.9 in Dallas (August 2025 to July 2026). The Fort Worth home our team runs near Dickies Arena averages 2.7 nights (every stay booked through June 2027, as of October 16, 2026). At 18 booked nights a month, a 6 night average means about 3 turnovers and a 2.7 night average about 7. A home that hosts [traveling nurses for 30 nights](https://listandhost.com/blog/traveling-nurse-30-night-stays-fort-worth/) suits a co host. A home that sells two night event weekends is a turnover business.

- **Event dates stack the hardest days.** The 2027 Fort Worth Stock Show and Rodeo runs January 15 to February 6, and AT&T Stadium hosts the Big 12 Championship on December 4, 2026. Those weeks bring back to back stays and same day turns, priced months ahead. See our guide to [Stock Show and Dickies Arena weekends](https://listandhost.com/blog/stock-show-and-dickies-arena-weekends-for-hosts/).

- **Guests book late.** Dallas stays are booked 30 days ahead on average (AirROI, August 2025 to July 2026). At our Fort Worth home, weeknight only stays were booked a median of one day before arrival (August to October 2026). A remote co host can answer that guest. Only someone local can get the home ready by afternoon.

- **The metroplex is wide.** Local in DFW can mean an hour in traffic. Ask where the cleaners and vendors are based, and how fast someone reaches your door when the air conditioner quits on a July night.

- **More homes chase the same guests.** AirROI counted 29% more Fort Worth listings than a year earlier, while average revenue rose 2.3% (August 2025 to July 2026). Ask either model how often prices change. Our [dynamic pricing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/) shows what good looks like.

## Who a co host fits

- You live in DFW, close enough to reach the home in about 30 minutes, or you have a handy person who is.

- You have a cleaner you trust, and a backup for the weeks they are away.

- The home books longer stays, so it turns over a few times a month, not a few times a week.

- You list only on Airbnb, or you are happy to run Vrbo yourself.

- You want the listing and reviews in your name and the lowest fee, and you are fine filling the gaps.

## Who a full service manager fits

- You live out of state or travel often, and nobody near the home can handle a lockout or a leak.

- The home turns over often: two and three night stays, game days and event weekends.

- You own two or more homes, or plan to.

- You want [Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-vs-vrbo-vs-booking-com-for-owners/) run from one synced calendar, with no double bookings.

- You want the income without a second job, and one statement a month.

Neither fits everyone. If you live close and like hosting, running it yourself can be the best deal of all. If pricing is your only weak spot, remote pricing costs less than either. Weighing one person against a team? Our page on [a solo co host vs full service](https://listandhost.com/compare/solo-co-host/) goes line by line, and our [15 questions to ask an Airbnb manager](https://listandhost.com/blog/questions-to-ask-an-airbnb-manager/) work for either model.

## Where List & Host fits

We offer both in DFW. Here is what each looks like with us.

- **Full service in Fort Worth, Arlington and Dallas.** 20% of booking revenue, no setup fee, repairs and supplies at cost with receipts, and the platforms pay you directly. Every line is on our [pricing page](https://listandhost.com/pricing/).

- **Co hosting.** You keep your listing, reviews, cleaner and payouts. We run pricing, guest messages, the cleaning schedule and reviews, at a price quoted in writing after a [free look](https://listandhost.com/services/#free-look).

Both are on our [services page](https://listandhost.com/services/), with local detail for [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/), [Arlington](https://listandhost.com/arlington/) and [Dallas](https://listandhost.com/dallas/), and our [Fort Worth Airbnb management guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-airbnb-management-owner-guide/) and [Arlington income by bedroom](https://listandhost.com/blog/how-much-does-an-airbnb-make-in-arlington-tx/) go deeper on two of those markets. Both run on the same engine as the three homes our team runs, one of them a Guest Favorite rated 4.9 on Airbnb as of October 16, 2026. The numbers and how we count them are on our [results page](https://listandhost.com/results/).

## Questions owners ask

**What is the difference between an Airbnb co host and a property manager?**

A co host joins your Airbnb listing with the access you choose, and you keep the listing, the reviews and the payouts. A full service property manager runs the whole operation, cleaners, repairs and supplies included, usually on every booking site. Many co hosts cover messages and pricing only.

**How much does an Airbnb co host charge in DFW?**

Owner and co host agree on it. We found no published survey for DFW alone. 2026 industry guides put co host fees at about 10% to 25% of booking revenue nationally, up to 30% with cleaning and repairs. On $40,000 a year in booking revenue, 15% is $6,000.

**How much does a full service property manager charge?**

Fee guides published in 2026 put full service at about 18% to 30% of booking revenue, up to 35% in some markets, with setup fees and markups sometimes on top. Ask each manager what the percentage is taken from.

**How does a co host get paid on Airbnb?**

The listing owner sets it up: the cleaning fee, the cleaning fee plus a percentage, a percentage of each booking, or a fixed amount per booking, worked out from the host's earnings after Airbnb's host fee. Vrbo has no built in payout split, so the owner pays a Vrbo helper directly.

**Is a co host or a property manager better for an out of state owner?**

Usually a full service manager, or a co host paired with a local cleaner and handy person you trust. Messages and pricing can run from anywhere. Lockouts, leaks and same day turnovers cannot.

**Not sure which one fits your home?** [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) built from your address, your home and live booking data for your market, with the basis for every number. Then run the fee table above on your own figures.

# Fort Worth Short Term Rental Market Report: October 2026

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/fort-worth-short-term-rental-market-report-october-2026/
Updated: 2026-10-17
Summary: Fort Worth short term rental rates by bedroom count, weekends vs weekdays, what is booking now and the event calendar to March 2027. Get a free estimate.

List & Host team · October 17, 2026

This is the October 2026 edition of our monthly Fort Worth short term rental market report. It puts three kinds of numbers in one place: live asking prices we collected ourselves near the event venues, market figures from public data services, and the event calendar for the next six months. Every number says where it came from and when. Owners, buyers, agents and writers are welcome to quote it with a link back to this page. If you own a home here and want a number for it, our [Fort Worth Airbnb management](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/) page has a free estimate form.

## The month in six numbers

| Number | What it is | Basis and date |
| - | - | - |
| 1.6 times | What a two night weekend stay asked compared with a two night midweek stay ($754 against $463 and $468, the median totals) | Our live Airbnb scan of 3 and 4 bedroom homes for 6 guests near the venues, October 13, 2026. Weekends with at least 30% of homes still open |
| 3% | Share of homes in our search area still open for October 23 to 25, ten days out (7 of 214). TCU homecoming was that Saturday | Same scan, October 13, 2026 |
| 46% | Share still open for the Stock Show opening weekend, January 15 to 17, 2027, about three months out (99 of 214) | Same scan, October 13, 2026 |
| $738 | Median two night total asked for that Stock Show opening weekend, cleaning included | Same scan, 14 comparable homes |
| 38 days | Average time between booking and arrival across Fort Worth listings | AirROI, August 2025 to July 2026, read October 17, 2026 |

## The market at a glance

Two services that track Airbnb listings publish Fort Worth numbers. They count differently, so we show both side by side instead of picking one.

| Measure | AirROI | Airbtics |
| - | - | - |
| Period | Aug 2025 to Jul 2026 | Sep 2025 to Aug 2026 |
| Active listings | 1,607 | 1,765 (as of Oct 16, 2026) |
| Listing growth in a year | 29% | 64.5% |
| Nightly rate | $225 average, $165 median | $184 |
| Share of nights booked | 41% average, 43% median | 61% median |
| Yearly revenue per listing | $24,276 average | about $43,000 median |
| Strongest months | June, May and March | October and November |
| Weakest months | January, February and September | August |

Why they disagree on the season: AirROI's year includes the nine World Cup matches at the Arlington stadium, June 14 to July 14, 2026, which lifted that summer far above a normal one. Airbtics points to fall, and fall has also been the strongest stretch so far at the 3 bedroom home our team runs. Both services agree on one thing: supply is growing faster than revenue. More homes are chasing the same guests.

Who you compete with, per AirROI for the same period:

- 85.2% of listings are entire homes or apartments, 38.1% have 3 or more bedrooms, and 45.6% sleep 6 or more.

- 32.9% take only stays of 30 nights or more, so the pool competing for event weekends is smaller than the headline count.

- The average stay is 6.8 nights, far longer than a weekend. Work trips, medical stays and families between homes are common reasons. Our [guide to 30 night stays](https://listandhost.com/blog/traveling-nurse-30-night-stays-fort-worth/) covers that side of the market.

- 41.7% of listings carry Airbnb's Guest Favorite label, 57.2% of hosts are Superhosts, and the average rating is 4.81. A strong rating is the entry ticket here, not a stand out.

- 11.1% of listings are professionally managed and 37.9% have a co host.

## Nightly rates by bedroom count

None of the public sources we checked publishes a dated, Fort Worth only table by bedroom count, so here are the two best references side by side. These are nightly rates before cleaning fees, and they are estimates, not quotes.

| Bedrooms | Red Awning average nightly rate | Our estimate, low to high |
| - | - | - |
| 1 | $153 | $125 to $155 |
| 2 | $197 | $165 to $205 |
| 3 | $285 | $225 to $275 |
| 4 | $405 | $300 to $365 |
| 5 | not published | $400 to $490 |
| 6 or more | not published | $550 to $675 |

Basis: Red Awning's Fort Worth page shows these averages without a date; a 2026 note on the same page says its figures start from 2024 data adjusted for later rate growth. Our estimate is the range our free estimator uses: AirROI's Fort Worth average nightly rate ($225, August 2025 to July 2026) spread across home sizes using the market's own bedroom mix, with the low and high ends 10% under and over the middle. Read October 17, 2026.

Cleaning fees sit on top. AirROI reports that 87.4% of Fort Worth listings charge one, with a median of $126 across all sizes. The 3 bedroom home our team runs charges $110.

A reality check from our own records: that 3 bedroom home, which sleeps 8, averaged $179 a night after discounts from August through October 2026 (October as booked on October 16). That is under both published 3 bedroom figures, because its quiet weeknights sell near a $149 floor instead of sitting empty. Its weekends sell well above the range. Which brings us to the biggest split in this market.

## Weekends versus weekdays

On October 13, 2026 we checked live Airbnb prices for 3 and 4 bedroom homes for 6 guests in the neighborhoods around the Cultural District, TCU, Near Southside, West 7th and the Stockyards. Totals are what a guest sees on the search card for the whole stay: nightly rate plus cleaning, before taxes.

| Two night stay | Also on | Homes still open | Comps | Median total | Middle half |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Tue Oct 20 to Thu Oct 22 | An ordinary midweek | 48% | 11 | $463 | $443 to $614 |
| Tue Oct 27 to Thu Oct 29 | An ordinary midweek | 55% | 13 | $468 | $422 to $614 |
| Fri Oct 30 to Sun Nov 1 | Teddy Swims at Dickies Arena, TCU vs Kansas | 38% | 14 | $754 | $647 to $993 |
| Fri Nov 6 to Sun Nov 8 | John Summit at Dickies Arena | 33% | 13 | $704 | $688 to $908 |
| Fri Nov 20 to Sun Nov 22 | TCU vs Utah, Ty Myers at Dickies Arena | 32% | 14 | $800 | $744 to $895 |

On weekends with a third of homes still open, the median weekend stay asked $754, about 1.6 times the midweek medians of $463 and $468. Per night, all in, that is roughly $377 against $233. Middle half means the 25th to 75th percentile of the comparable homes on the first page of results.

Our own records point the same way. At the 3 bedroom home our team runs, Friday and Saturday nights averaged $236 from August through October 2026, against $139 for other nights, about 1.7 times. Both are what guests paid per night after discounts, before cleaning fees. The timing differs even more: stays that included a weekend night were booked a median of 44 days ahead, and weeknight only stays a median of 1 day ahead. You can see how we count these on the [results page for that home](https://listandhost.com/results/fort-worth-home/).

## What is booking now

The share of homes still open for a date is the clearest live signal of demand. Here is every date we checked on October 13, 2026, out of 214 homes with 3 or more bedrooms for 6 guests in the same search area.

| Stay | Also on | Days out | Homes still open | Median total asked |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Fri Oct 16 to Sun Oct 18 | Phoebe Bridgers at Dickies Arena | 3 | 20 (9%) | $1,028 |
| Fri Oct 23 to Sun Oct 25 | TCU homecoming vs West Virginia, Mecum Auctions at Dickies Arena | 10 | 7 (3%) | $1,618 |
| Fri Oct 30 to Sun Nov 1 | Halloween weekend shows, TCU, Cowboys on Sunday | 17 | 82 (38%) | $754 |
| Fri Nov 6 to Sun Nov 8 | John Summit, two nights | 24 | 71 (33%) | $704 |
| Fri Nov 13 to Sun Nov 15 | Hot Wheels Monster Trucks, TCU vs Kansas State, Cowboys vs 49ers | 31 | 24 (11%) | $1,010 |
| Fri Nov 20 to Sun Nov 22 | TCU vs Utah, Ty Myers, Cowboys vs Titans | 38 | 68 (32%) | $800 |
| Wed Nov 25 to Sat Nov 28, 3 nights | Thanksgiving, Cowboys vs Eagles | 43 | 76 (36%) | $1,237 |
| Fri Dec 4 to Sun Dec 6 | NCHA Futurity, Big 12 Championship, for KING + COUNTRY | 52 | 95 (44%) | $754 |
| Thu Dec 24 to Sun Dec 27, 3 nights | Christmas | 72 | 130 (61%) | $1,108 |
| Wed Dec 30 to Fri Jan 1 | New Year, Flatland Cavalry, Cotton Bowl | 78 | 105 (49%) | $743 |
| Fri Jan 15 to Sun Jan 17 | Stock Show opening weekend | 94 | 99 (46%) | $738 |

Three things stand out.

1. **Weekends with a big local draw go first.** The TCU homecoming weekend was 97% gone ten days out, and the Monster Trucks weekend 89% gone a month out.

2. **The fuller the weekend, the more the leftovers ask.** The three fullest weekends had median asks of $1,010 to $1,618; the three with about a third still open sat at $704 to $800. Cheaper homes sell first, so the homes left are the pricier ones. Treat a high leftover median as a sign of demand, not as a price anyone is sure to get.

3. **Holidays and the Stock Show were still about half open two to three months out.** One snapshot cannot tell whether those dates book later or simply have more homes chasing them. Next month's scan will show how fast they fill.

The calendar of the 3 bedroom home our team runs shows the same split. On October 17, 2026, it was 64% booked for the next 14 nights, 47% for the next 30, 30% for the next 60 and 28% for the next 90. Across the next 60 nights, 11 of 17 Friday and Saturday nights were booked (65%), against 7 of 43 other nights (16%). Weekends fill early; weeknights fill late or not at all.

Dickies Arena seats up to 14,000 for a concert, and the Will Rogers Memorial Center next door hosts the Stock Show and the NCHA Futurity. Cowboys games, the Big 12 Championship and the Cotton Bowl are at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, and their crowds stay across the whole area. Notes for hosts. The Stock Show runs every day for 23 days, so it lifts weeknights too, and its own visitor page warns that lots fill quickly on weekends; guests who stay nearby skip that problem. The Futurity brings riders, owners and families who stay for days, which favors weekly stays. When Fort Worth last hosted the NCAA men's first and second rounds, in 2022, the arena says they sold out with more than 13,000 fans. Looking past March, the arena already lists the NCAA women's gymnastics championships on April 15 to 17, 2027. The Jo Koy date is printed with the year 2026 on the arena's list, while its event link says 2027; we show it as 2027.

## What this means for owners

1. **Price weekends first, and early.** The busiest weekends were nearly gone ten days out, and at the home our team runs weekend stays booked a median of 44 days ahead. A weekend priced late is often a weekend priced after the best guests have booked elsewhere.

2. **Hold your price when the market is nearly full.** When fewer than one in four homes are left for your dates, the homes still open ask far more. That is not the moment to cut.

3. **Treat the Futurity as four weeks of weeknight demand.** It runs November 16 to December 12. Weekly pricing and fast replies to multi night inquiries matter more than the weekend rate.

4. **Set your Stock Show prices now.** About half the homes in our area were still open for opening weekend three months out, with a median ask of $738 for two nights. Price Stock Show weeknights as event nights, because the show runs daily.

5. **Check what guests actually see.** Early bird, weekly, monthly and last minute discounts stack. On October 13, a 15% last minute discount took a $329 nightly price at the home our team runs down to about $280 for guests. Know your final price after every discount.

6. **Compete on the total, not the nightly rate.** Guests compare the whole stay. With most listings charging a cleaning fee, a low nightly rate with a high fee can look more expensive than it is.

7. **Earn the rating.** With listing counts up 29% in a year by AirROI's count and 41.7% of listings already Guest Favorites, photos, reviews and reply speed decide who gets booked.

8. **Keep weeknights flexible.** Weeknight only stays booked a median of 1 day ahead at the home our team runs. A clean home ready on short notice and a reply in minutes win those nights.

Want this applied to your address? [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) with the basis for every number. Estimates are not promises; your home, street, size, photos and reviews all change the answer.

We kept 3 and 4 bedroom homes with reviews from the first page of results, which gave 5 to 15 comparable homes per stay. - **Market data.** AirROI, Airbtics and Red Awning public pages, read October 17, 2026. Each service decides which listings count and whether to report an average or a median, so we show their figures as published.

- **Our own records.** Booking records of the 3 bedroom home our team runs, as of October 16 and 17, 2026. It opened in July 2026, so its record is short and fall is its strongest season so far. See [results from homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/) and how we count them.

- **Events.** Official venue, team and event pages, read October 17, 2026, listed below.

- **Limits.** One snapshot, first page of results only, one part of the city, and 3 to 4 bedroom homes only for the live scan. Other sizes and neighborhoods can price differently.

We rebuild this report every month with a fresh scan, so the next edition can show how fast the holidays and the Stock Show filled. To cite it, please use: List & Host, Fort Worth Short Term Rental Market Report, October 2026, with a link to this page.
