# Stock Show and Dickies Arena Weekends: A Host Playbook

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/stock-show-and-dickies-arena-weekends-for-hosts/
Updated: 2026-10-16
Summary: How Fort Worth hosts can price the Stock Show, Dickies Arena shows and the Futurity, with real comp data and our own lessons. Get a free estimate.

List & Host team · October 16, 2026

In Fort Worth, a few dozen dates a year decide whether a short term rental has a good year or an average one. Most of them sit on two calendars: the Fort Worth Stock Show and Rodeo, and the shows at Dickies Arena and the Will Rogers Memorial Center next door. This is how we plan for those dates at the 3 bedroom home our team runs, with the numbers we saw and the mistakes we made. It is the playbook behind our [Fort Worth Airbnb management](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/).

## The calendar that matters

| Event | When | Why hosts care |
| - | - | - |
| Fort Worth Stock Show and Rodeo | January 15 to February 6, 2027, 23 days | Three weeks of rodeo, livestock shows and crowds. Weekends fill first. |
| Dickies Arena concerts and shows | All year | Up to 14,000 seats for a concert, and some weekends have more than one show. |
| NCHA Futurity | Scheduled November 16 to December 12, 2026 | Nearly four weeks of cutting horse competition in Fort Worth. Riders, owners and families stay for days. |
| TCU home football | Fall Saturdays | Fans and families book Friday and Saturday together. |
| Holidays | Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year | Family visits and longer stays. |

Here is what density looks like. Dickies Arena has Morrissey on October 29, Teddy Swims on October 30 and MercyMe on November 1, 2026: three shows across one Halloween weekend. The next weekend, John Summit plays November 7 and 8. Then Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live runs November 13 to 15. When the arena calendar looks like that, nearby homes should not be priced like an ordinary weekend.

## What the Stock Show looks like from the booking side

The Stock Show runs every day for 23 days, so it lifts weeknights too, not only weekends. The show's own visitor page warns that parking at Will Rogers and Dickies Arena can fill early on Saturdays and Sundays. Guests who stay nearby skip that problem, and many will pay for it.

On October 13, 2026, three months before opening, we checked live Airbnb prices for the Stock Show's opening weekend, Friday January 15 to Sunday January 17, 2027. We looked at 14 comparable homes with 3 or more bedrooms for 6 guests in the neighborhoods around the venues.

| Comparable homes, opening weekend | Two night total |
| - | - |
| Lowest | $500 |
| 25th percentile | $641 |
| Median | $738 |
| 75th percentile | $942 |
| Highest | $1,099 |

At that point, 99 of the 214 homes in that search area, or 46%, were still open for those dates. The home our team runs priced the weekend at $379 a night with a 2 night minimum, which put the total with cleaning at $868, a little above the median. Stock Show weeknights at the home our team runs are priced at $299, against $149 to $199 on ordinary weeknights. These are our asking prices, not results. That home opened in July 2026 and has not hosted a Stock Show yet. We will update this guide after the show.

## Event weekends book early. Weeknights book late.

At our Fort Worth home, stays that included a Friday or Saturday night were booked a median of 44 days before arrival. Stays with only weeknights were booked a median of 1 day before. That gap shapes the whole playbook: get the weekend price right early, and keep weeknights flexible.

- A September weekend booked 61 days ahead at $390 a night, the highest average night the home has sold.

- A 3 night weekend in October, a big football weekend in the area, sold at $254 a night after discounts. We had set a 3 night minimum for those dates, so the weekend could not be broken up by a one night stay.

## Mistakes we made, so you do not have to

**We let weekends sell too cheap.** Two fall weekends at the home our team runs booked weeks ahead at about $209 and $248 a night. One of them overlaps a four day auction at Dickies Arena. By mid October, the comparable homes still open on those weekends asked a median of $1,618 and $1,010 for the stay. Late leftovers tend to be the pricier homes, so the real gap was smaller. But the lesson held, and we raised 23 future weekend nights the same day.

**We let automatic discounts slide an event weekend.** Our fill rules lower prices on open nights as arrival gets closer. The Friday and Saturday nights of the John Summit weekend, November 6 and 7, had slid to $202 a night before our comp check caught it. Similar homes were asking $773 and up for those two nights. We set it back to $249 with a 2 night minimum on October 9, and it sold on Booking.com about four hours later. Comparable homes asked a median of $704 for that two night stay; ours came to about $567 with cleaning. It sold, but it sold cheap. We now lock event weeks so fill rules cannot touch them. You can see the full story on our [Fort Worth results page](https://listandhost.com/results/fort-worth-home/).

**Platform discounts stack.** When we checked Halloween weekend, a 15% last minute discount on Airbnb was taking a $329 nightly price down to about $280 for guests. If you set an event floor, check what guests actually see after every discount.

## The playbook we use

1. **Load the calendars six months out.** The Stock Show schedule, the Dickies Arena events page, the Will Rogers calendar, TCU's football schedule and the holidays.

2. **Set a floor for every event night.** A floor is the lowest price that night may ever sell for. Automatic tools may push above it, never below.

3. **Set minimum stays by event.** Two nights for most event weekends. Three for the biggest. Once the weekend books, open any one night gaps around it to one night stays.

4. **Check comps every week.** Look at what similar homes ask for the same dates, and how many are still open. When fewer than one in four homes are left, hold your price or raise it.

5. **Price Stock Show weeknights as event nights.** The show runs daily, so a Tuesday in late January is not an ordinary Tuesday.

6. **Watch discounts.** Early bird, weekly, monthly and last minute discounts stack. Know the final price a guest sees.

7. **Prepare the house for crowds.** Clear guest limits, parking instructions, quiet hours, and a house manual that answers event questions: where to park, how far to the arena, where to eat late.

8. **Line up cleaners for Sunday.** Event weekends end with Sunday checkouts and often Sunday arrivals. Book your cleaner and a backup before the dates sell.

## What an event weekend is worth

In our October 13 check, two night stays near the venues showed these comp medians:

| Dates | What was on | Comp median, two nights |
| - | - | - |
| Fri Oct 30 to Sun Nov 1 | Three arena shows over Halloween weekend | $754 |
| Fri Nov 20 to Sun Nov 22 | A busy football and concert weekend | $800 |
| Wed Nov 25 to Fri Nov 27 | Thanksgiving | $744 |
| Fri Jan 15 to Sun Jan 17 | Stock Show opening weekend | $738 |
| Tue Oct 27 to Thu Oct 29 | An ordinary midweek stay | $468 |

That is the spread an event calendar creates. Your home's place in it depends on its size, look, reviews and how early you price. Want to see where your home would land? [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/).

## A note for owners who live nearby

Many Fort Worth owners hold back a few event weekends for their own family. That is fine, but block those dates early and on every channel. A last minute owner block on a weekend that already sold means a host cancellation, which can bring platform penalties and cost you the trust of future guests.

## Questions owners ask

**When should I set prices for the Fort Worth Stock Show?**

Set them as soon as the dates are published, usually months ahead. At the home our team runs, weekend stays were booked a median of 44 days before arrival, and the best event weekends often go earlier than that.

**Should I require a minimum stay for event weekends?**

Usually yes. We use two nights for most event weekends and three for the biggest, then allow one night stays to fill any gap left around a booking.

**Do weeknights sell during the Stock Show?**

The show runs every day for 23 days, so weeknights carry more demand than usual. We price Stock Show weeknights at $299, against $149 to $199 on ordinary weeknights. That is our asking price, not a result yet.

**Own a home near the arena?** [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) built from your address, your home and live booking data for your market, with the basis for every number. Or [see results from homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/) and how we count them.

# Self Managing vs Hiring a Manager: Honest Cost and Time

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/self-managing-vs-hiring-an-airbnb-manager/
Updated: 2026-10-16
Summary: The real hours and dollars of running a short term rental yourself, what a manager costs, and the break even math, from a team that runs homes every day.

List & Host team · October 16, 2026

We are a management company, so read this knowing we have a stake in the answer. Our team also runs three homes, so we know what the work looks like day to day. Some owners should manage their own rental. Others are paying for it with time they do not have. This guide lays out the hours, the dollars and the break even point so you can decide with real numbers. Full service in Fort Worth, the rest of Dallas Fort Worth and the Buffalo River region of Arkansas. Co hosting or remote pricing anywhere else in the United States. The options are on our [services page](https://listandhost.com/services/), with local pages for [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/) and the [Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/).

## How much time self managing takes

PriceLabs surveyed more than 1,400 hosts for its Global Host Report 2025. They spent an average of 8.3 hours a week managing their listings, which is about 36 hours a month. 76% said admin work such as bookkeeping and taxes was highly time consuming, and 72% said the same about cleaning and maintenance.

Here is our own estimate for one home with about eight stays a month, close to what our Fort Worth home booked in September and October 2026.

********

| Task | What it involves | Hours a month |
| - | - | - |
| Guest messages | Questions before booking, check in details, help during the stay, checkout, reviews | 4 to 8 |
| Pricing | Checking comps, events and gaps, adjusting nightly rates and minimum stays | 3 to 6 |
| Cleaning coordination | Scheduling each turnover, checking photos, handling late checkouts | 3 to 5 |
| Restocking | Ordering supplies, delivering them, tracking linens | 2 to 4 |
| Maintenance | Finding vendors, letting them in, following up | 2 to 6 |
| Money | Payouts, expenses and records for your CPA | 2 to 4 |
| Problems | Lockouts, broken items, noise complaints, damage claims | 1 to 5 |
| Total |  | 17 to 38 |

Basis: our own operating experience across three homes, checked against the PriceLabs survey average. These are estimates. Your hours depend on how far you live from the home, how many stays you get and how much you automate.

The hours are not the hardest part. The timing is. At our Fort Worth home, stays with only weeknights were booked a median of one day before arrival. Guests message at night, on holidays and during your own vacation. Turnovers happen in the five hours between an 11 AM checkout and a 4 PM check in. Self managing means being reachable for all of it, or paying someone to be.

## What doing it well looks like

Pricing alone is a daily job if it is done right. In the first 26 days our engine ran live, from September 21 to October 16, 2026, it logged 133 nightly price changes and 52 minimum stay changes across the three homes our team runs, all written and read back. Each one was checked against a floor, written, read back and logged. Even so, our October 13 comp check found open dates at our Fort Worth home priced 11% to 25% under the local median, and we fixed them that day. The money is in the details: event floors, minimum stays, one night gaps and discounts that stack. You can see the moves behind our numbers on our [results page](https://listandhost.com/results/).

## What a manager costs

Full service managers commonly charge 18% to 25% of booking revenue. Some add setup fees, markups on repairs and supplies, or take the percentage from a different base. Read our [guide to management fees](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-management-fees/) before you compare quotes, and see [our pricing](https://listandhost.com/pricing/) for what we charge.

## The honest cost table

Example: a home that brings in $40,000 a year in nightly revenue, not counting cleaning fees. The manager column uses 20%, the middle of the common range and also our own full service fee. Every figure is an estimate for illustration.

|  | Self managing | Full service manager at 20% |
| - | - | - |
| Platform fees, about 15.5% on Airbnb | $6,200 | $6,200 |
| Management fee | $0 | $8,000 |
| Software for pricing, messages and calendars | About $300 to $1,200 a year (our estimate) | Usually included |
| Cleaning | Paid from guest cleaning fees | Same |
| Your time | About 200 to 450 hours a year | A few hours a year for approvals and statements |
| Who answers at 2 AM | You | The manager |

On this example, the $8,000 fee buys back about 200 to 450 hours a year. That works out to roughly $18 to $40 for each hour you no longer spend. If your time is worth more than that, or you simply do not have those hours, a manager can make sense before you count any change in revenue. If you have the time and enjoy the work, self managing keeps that money in your pocket.

## The revenue question

A good manager should earn back part of the fee through better pricing, more channels and better reviews. A weak one will not. Nobody can promise you a number, and you should be wary of anyone who does. Ask any manager how often they check comps, who sets the floors, and what they do when a weekend is still open two weeks out. Ask to see a real monthly statement from a home they run.

## The middle options

It does not have to be all or nothing.

- **Co hosting.** You keep the listing in your name, and your reviews stay yours. A co host handles messages, pricing and cleaning coordination. You or a local helper handle anything that needs hands at the home.

- **A launch package.** One time help to set up the home, listing, photos, pricing, lock and cleaner. Then you run it.

- **Remote pricing and listing work.** You handle guests and cleaning. Someone else runs daily pricing and keeps the listing sharp. This works in any market, because it needs no local team.

List & Host offers all three alongside full service management. The [services page](https://listandhost.com/services/) explains each one.

## Who should self manage

- You live within 20 to 30 minutes of the home.

- You have one home and flexible hours.

- You enjoy hosting and answer messages fast, even at night.

- You have a reliable cleaner and a backup.

## Who should get help

- You live far away or travel often.

- You work a full time job.

- You own two or more homes, or plan to.

- Your market runs on events, where pricing mistakes cost the most.

- You want the income without being on call.

## Questions to ask yourself before you decide

1. How many hours a month can I honestly give this, including nights and weekends?

2. Who covers for me when I am sick or away?

3. What is one hour of my time worth?

4. If I hire, what is the fee charged on, and what is billed on top?

5. How do I leave the agreement if it is not working?

Our checklist of [what a management company should do](https://listandhost.com/blog/what-does-an-airbnb-management-company-do/) helps you compare managers line by line. To see what your home could earn either way, [get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/).

## Questions owners ask

**How many hours a week does it take to self manage an Airbnb?**

PriceLabs' 2025 survey of more than 1,400 hosts found an average of 8.3 hours a week. Our own estimate for one home with about eight stays a month is 17 to 38 hours a month, depending on distance and automation.

**Is hiring an Airbnb manager worth it?**

On a home with $40,000 a year in nightly revenue, a 20% fee is $8,000 and buys back roughly 200 to 450 hours. That is about $18 to $40 an hour. If your time is worth more, or you do not have the hours, it often is.

**What is the difference between co hosting and full service management?**

With co hosting you keep the listing and your reviews, and the co host handles messages, pricing and cleaning coordination. Full service management also covers local cleaning, maintenance and everything that needs hands at the home.

**Want to see both options for your home?** [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) built from your address, your home and live booking data for your market, with the basis for every number. Or [see results from homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/) and how we count them.

**Sources:** [Travolution: PriceLabs Global Host Report 2025](https://www.travolution.com/news/more-than-1-400-hosts-find-ai-overwhelming/) · [Awning: Airbnb management fees 2026](https://awning.com/post/airbnb-management-fees) · [Airbnb Help: service fees](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1857)


# How Much Can an Airbnb Make in Fort Worth? 2026 Numbers

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/how-much-can-an-airbnb-make-in-fort-worth/
Updated: 2026-10-16
Summary: Fort Worth Airbnb income from two data services and one real 3 bedroom home: rates, occupancy, weekends and costs. Then get a free estimate for yours.

List & Host team · October 16, 2026

Fort Worth is one of the busiest short term rental markets in Texas. Visit Fort Worth counted 11.5 million visitors in 2024. The Stock Show, Dickies Arena, TCU and the Stockyards pull guests all year. But a busy city does not tell you what one home earns. This guide puts three sets of numbers side by side: two national data services, and one real Fort Worth home our team runs. Then it shows how to build an honest estimate for your own place. If you want the short version for your address, our [Fort Worth Airbnb management](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/) page has a free estimate form.

**Short answer.** Data services put the typical Fort Worth listing at about $24,000 to $43,000 a year in booking revenue, depending on who is counting and how. A well run 3 bedroom home near the event venues can beat the typical listing, but winter weeks and slow weeknights pull the year down. Every figure below says where it came from.

## What the data services say

Two services that track Airbnb listings published Fort Worth numbers this year. They do not agree, and that is worth knowing before you trust any single figure.

| Source | Period | Listings | Occupancy | Nightly rate | Yearly revenue |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Airbtics | Sep 2025 to Aug 2026 | 1,765 | 61% | $184 | $43,000 (median) |
| AirROI | Aug 2025 to Jul 2026 | 1,607 | 41% (average) | $225 average, $165 median | $24,276 (average) |

Why so far apart? Each service decides which listings count, how to treat blocked nights, and whether to report an average or a median. One very expensive estate pulls an average up. Hundreds of private rooms and small apartments pull it down. AirROI also reports that the number of Fort Worth listings grew 29% in a year, while its revenue figure rose only 2.3%. More homes are chasing the same guests, so pricing, photos and reviews matter more every year.

The services also disagree on the best season. Airbtics says demand peaks in October and November and is weakest in August. AirROI names March, May and June as its peak months and January, February and September as its low ones. The fall at the Fort Worth home our team runs was strong, which fits the first view, but one fall is not a trend.

## What one real Fort Worth home booked

Our team runs a 3 bedroom home in west Fort Worth that sleeps 8. It is a short drive from Dickies Arena, TCU and the Stockyards. Its first stay was July 2, 2026, and it is listed on Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com and a direct booking site. Here is what it did from August through October, as of October 16, 2026.

| Month | Nights booked | Share of nights | Average night | Payouts |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| August 2026 | 12 of 31 | 39% | $217 | $3,124 |
| September 2026 | 20 of 30 | 67% | $169 | $3,840 |
| October 2026, booked to date | 24 of 31 | 77% | $169 | $4,742 |

Average night is what guests paid for the nights after discounts, before cleaning fees, taxes and platform fees. Payouts are what the platforms paid after their own fees. They include the cleaning fee guests pay and come before our cleaning, utilities and other costs. October is not over, so its figures are booked, not earned. The full method is on our [Fort Worth results page](https://listandhost.com/results/fort-worth-home/).

Across those three months the home was booked 56 of 92 nights, or 61%, and paid out $11,706. That is about $127 for every night on the calendar, booked or not. We are not turning that into a yearly number. Fall has been the home's strongest stretch so far, and in mid October its November and December calendars were only 23% and 29% booked. The average night also came down as the calendar filled, because quiet weeknights now sell near a $149 floor instead of sitting empty. Payouts still went up every month.

## Weekends and weeknights are two different businesses

The biggest lesson from our first months: weekends and weeknights behave in opposite ways.

- **Price.** From August through October, weekend nights (Friday and Saturday) averaged $236 at the home our team runs. Weeknights averaged $139. Both are what guests paid per night, after discounts, before cleaning, taxes and platform fees.

- **Timing.** Stays that included a weekend night were booked a median of 44 days ahead. Stays with weeknights only were booked a median of 1 day ahead.

So weekends need the right price early, before the good ones are gone. Weeknights need fast replies, a clean home ready on short notice, and a price that still makes sense the day before.

We learned the weekend half the hard way. On October 13 our weekly comp check found that two fall weekends at the home our team runs had sold at about $209 and $248 a night, weeks ahead. The similar homes still open on those weekends asked a median of $1,618 and $1,010 for the stay. Homes left open late tend to be the pricier ones, so that gap overstates it. Still, it told us our weekend base price was too low. We raised 23 future weekend nights that day, and each one was read back and locked so no automatic discount could undo it.

## What drives demand in Fort Worth

- **The Fort Worth Stock Show and Rodeo.** The 2027 show runs January 15 to February 6, 23 days, at the Will Rogers Memorial Center and Dickies Arena.

- **Dickies Arena.** It seats up to 14,000 for concerts and 9,300 for rodeo. Some fall weekends have two or three shows.

- **Will Rogers Memorial Center.** The 120 acre complex next to the arena draws more than two million visitors a year for horse shows, livestock shows and expos. The NCHA Futurity, a cutting horse championship in Fort Worth, is scheduled for November 16 to December 12, 2026.

- **TCU.** Home football weekends, graduations and family visits.

- **Everyday travel.** Work trips, family visits, medical stays and people between homes fill weeknights and longer stays.

Our guide to [Stock Show and Dickies Arena weekends](https://listandhost.com/blog/stock-show-and-dickies-arena-weekends-for-hosts/) covers how we price those dates.

## The costs that come out before you keep anything

| Cost | What to expect | Basis |
| - | - | - |
| Platform fees and discounts | About 15.5% of each Airbnb booking, about 20% with discounts | Airbnb's single host fee for most hosts. Across our 64 Airbnb stays, payouts came to 19.9% under the list price of the nights, cleaning and pet fees, discounts included |
| Cleaning | $90 per turnover at our 3 bedroom home; guests pay a $110 cleaning fee | Our cleaner's rate and our listing, October 2026 |
| Electricity | About $200 to $230 a month | Our Fort Worth home's bills |
| Water, gas, internet, streaming | Varies by home | Budget it monthly |
| Supplies | Paper goods, soap, coffee, linens | Grows with bookings |
| Repairs and wear | Small fixes every month | Set money aside from every payout |
| Insurance | A policy that covers short term guests | Ask your agent |

## A worked estimate you can adjust

Here is the simple math we use to start a Fort Worth estimate. These are examples, not promises. Your home, street, size, photos and reviews all change the answer.

| Example | Occupancy | Average night | Nights sold | Nightly revenue | After a 15.5% platform fee |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Quiet year | 45% | $170 | 164 | $27,880 | $23,559 |
| Middle year | 55% | $195 | 201 | $39,195 | $33,120 |
| Strong year | 65% | $220 | 237 | $52,140 | $44,058 |

Basis: the occupancy range covers both data services (41% and 61%) and that home's fall (61%). The nightly rates cover AirROI's median and average ($165 and $225), Airbtics ($184) and that home's fall average ($179). Nightly revenue leaves out cleaning fees, since those mostly pay the cleaner. From the last column you still pay utilities, supplies, repairs, insurance, any mortgage and, if you hire one, a manager.

Want this math run on your own home with live comps? [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/).

## Five things that move a Fort Worth home up the table

1. **Event aware pricing.** Put the Stock Show, the arena calendar and TCU home games into your prices months ahead, and set floors so automatic discounts cannot slide those nights.

2. **Minimum stays by season.** Two or three night minimums on event weekends. One night stays allowed midweek when the calendar is empty.

3. **Fast replies.** Weeknight guests book the day before. A reply in minutes wins the booking.

4. **Three channels.** Airbnb brought most of our bookings, but Vrbo and Booking.com reach guests Airbnb does not. See [Airbnb vs Vrbo vs Booking.com](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-vs-vrbo-vs-booking-com-for-owners/).

5. **Longer stays for winter.** Weekly and monthly discounts can fill January and February with work and medical stays.

## Questions owners ask

**What is a good occupancy rate for a Fort Worth Airbnb?**

The data services we checked put the typical Fort Worth listing between 41% and 61% of nights booked. Our 3 bedroom home was booked 61% of nights from August through October 2026. Occupancy alone is not the goal: a home that fills every weeknight at a low price can earn less than one that sells fewer nights at the right price.

**How much more do weekends earn in Fort Worth?**

At the home our team runs, Friday and Saturday nights averaged $236 from August through October 2026, against $139 for weeknights, after discounts, before cleaning, taxes and platform fees. Event weekends can go much higher. That is why weekend prices should be set early and protected with floors.

**Want a number for your Fort Worth home?** [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) built from your address, your home and live booking data for your market, with the basis for every number. Or [see results from homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/) and how we count them.

**Sources:** [Airbtics: Fort Worth short term rental data](https://airbtics.com/annual-airbnb-revenue-in-fort-worth-texas-usa) · [AirROI: Fort Worth Airbnb data](https://airroi.com/airbnb-data/united-states/texas/fort-worth) · [Visit Fort Worth: 2024 tourism impact](https://www.fortworth.com/articles/post/visit-fort-worth-celebrates-tourism-growth-35-billion-economic-impact/) · [Fort Worth Stock Show and Rodeo: visitor questions](https://www.fwssr.com/p/plan-a-visit/frequently-asked-questions) · [Dickies Arena: about the arena](https://dickiesarena.com/about/) · [Visit Fort Worth: Will Rogers Memorial Center](https://www.fortworth.com/will-rogers-memorial-center/) · [NCHA: updated dates for the 2026 Futurity](https://nchacutting.com/about-us/news/2026/05/19/ncha-announces-updated-dates-for-the-2026-ncha-metallic-cat-futurity) · [Airbnb Help: service fees](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1857)


# Hot Tub Rentals: Upkeep, Costs and What a Tub Earns

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/hot-tub-rentals-upkeep-and-earnings/
Updated: 2026-10-16
Summary: Does a hot tub pay off in a short term rental? Search data, earnings gaps, running costs and the turnover routine, with sources. Get a free estimate.

List & Host team · October 16, 2026

Few upgrades change a short term rental like a hot tub. Guests search for it, photos sell it, and in cabin markets it can be the difference between a full winter and an empty one. It also adds work at every single turnover. Here is what a tub can earn, what it costs to run, and the routine that keeps guests safe. We run a hot tub at our glass house in the [Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/) and are adding one at our [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/) home this winter.

## Do guests really want it?

Yes. Airbnb's own guide to the amenities guests search for most lists the hot tub sixth, ahead of a washer or dryer, self check in and a grill. In cabin markets it matters even more. In AirROI's data for the Jasper area near the Buffalo National River, 27.8% of listings have a hot tub. Those listings averaged $43,474 a year in revenue, against $20,242 for listings without one.

That gap is not all the tub. Homes with tubs are often bigger and better equipped. Beyond Pricing, a pricing company, reported in October 2026 that hosts in markets such as Atlanta, Oahu, Los Angeles and the North Carolina mountains can charge a 20% to 25% premium for listings with a hot tub. It did not publish its method in detail, so treat that as a direction, not a guarantee.

## Our own experience

The glass house our team runs in the Buffalo River region has a hot tub. It is rated 4.9 on Airbnb and is a Guest Favorite. For October 2026 it has 27 of 31 nights booked as of October 16, at an average of $502 a night. The tub is one reason among many, along with the views, the space and the design, so we do not credit it with a share of that number. See the [glass house results page](https://listandhost.com/results/buffalo-river-glass-house/) for the full picture.

At our Fort Worth home we ordered an entry level 6 to 7 person spa for $3,599.99 before tax, and budgeted about $5,000 all in with wiring and placement. We will add its results to this guide once it has a season of bookings.

## What a tub costs to buy and install

| Item | What to expect | Basis |
| - | - | - |
| The tub | About $3,600 for an entry level 6 to 7 person spa. Larger acrylic tubs cost more. | Our purchase, October 2026 |
| Electrical | A dedicated circuit installed by a licensed electrician. Full size tubs commonly run a 240 volt heater. | Hydropool's example uses a 6,000 watt, 240 volt heater |
| Base | A level pad, or a deck rated to carry a full tub of water and people | Ask your installer |
| Delivery and placement | Varies with access to the spot | Get a quote |
| Cover | A locking cover, replaced when it gets waterlogged | Standard with most tubs |

## What a tub costs to run

| Cost | Estimate | Basis |
| - | - | - |
| Electricity | About $27 to $30 a month for typical home use. Budget more for rental use. | About 187 kWh a month in Hydropool's example, at July 2026 average home rates of 14.33 cents per kWh in Arkansas and 15.88 cents in Texas (EIA) |
| Professional service | $155 to $320 a visit, about $222 on average | Thumbtack's 2026 national cost guide |
| Chemicals, test strips, filters | A monthly line item. Replace filters on the maker's schedule. | Your tub's manual |
| Cleaner time | 15 to 30 minutes per turnover to test, adjust, rinse the filter and wipe the waterline | Our estimate |
| Water | A full drain and refill on a set schedule | Your local water rate |

Rental tubs run harder than home tubs. Guests leave the cover off, soak longer and want it hot on arrival. Plan for the electricity line to run higher than a home example, especially in winter.

## The turnover routine

A home hot tub might see a few soaks a week. A rental tub can see six adults a night, every night. Treat it closer to a public spa than a backyard one.

1. **Test at every turnover.** Check sanitizer and pH before each new guest, not once a week. For public hot tubs, the CDC's targets are 3 to 10 parts per million of free chlorine or 4 to 8 of bromine, and a pH of 7.2 to 7.8, tested at least twice a day. Follow your tub maker's limits too.

2. **Shock, rinse and skim.** Shock after each stay, rinse or swap the filter, and clear debris from the water and the cover.

3. **Drain on a schedule.** Most home spa manuals call for a full drain every few months, sooner with heavy use. A rental counts as heavy use. Put a fixed drain date on your cleaning calendar.

4. **Drain at once after contamination.** Vomit, fecal matter, glass or bath bombs mean drain, clean and keep the tub closed until the water is balanced again. Do not shock it and hope.

5. **Log every reading.** Write down pH, sanitizer and temperature at each turnover. A log protects you if a guest ever raises a health complaint.

6. **Set a safe temperature.** The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission says hot tub water should never exceed 104 degrees Fahrenheit, and advises pregnant women to stay at 100 degrees or below. Post that in the house rules.

7. **Cover and lock.** A locking cover protects children, keeps debris out and holds heat.

## What a tub can earn: the math

Here is a simple way to size it. This is an example, not a promise.

| Line | Example |
| - | - |
| Extra per booked night because of the tub | $25 |
| Booked nights a year | 150 |
| Extra nightly revenue | $3,750 |
| After a 15.5% platform fee | $3,169 |
| Less running costs: power, chemicals, filters, cleaner time | About $1,000 to $1,500 |
| Extra a year before repairs | About $1,700 to $2,200 |

Basis: $25 is 10% of a $250 night, well under the 20% to 25% premiums Beyond Pricing reported. Running costs use the electricity estimate above, raised for rental use, plus our estimates for chemicals, filters and cleaner time. On a $5,000 tub, that example pays back in about two to three years. The bigger effect can be occupancy. A tub puts your home in front of every guest who checks the hot tub filter, and it gives winter guests a reason to come. To size it for your own home, [get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) and mention the tub.

## When a tub is not worth it

- Your electrical service cannot carry another 240 volt load without an expensive upgrade.

- There is no private, level spot that neighbors cannot see into.

- Your cleaner cannot take on tub care, and no service covers your area.

- Comparable homes in your market rarely have tubs and guests do not filter for one. Try the hot tub filter on a search for your area first.

- Your insurance will not cover it, or the premium jump eats the gain. Ask your agent before you buy.

## Listing it right

- Put the tub in the first five photos, with the view if you have one.

- Name it in the title if there is room. Guests search for it.

- Post clear rules: no glass, shower first, no children without an adult, and the set temperature.

- If the tub is ever down, tell guests before they arrive and offer a fair fix. A surprise broken tub is one of the fastest ways to a bad review.

## Questions owners ask

**Does a hot tub increase Airbnb bookings?**

Guests search for it: Airbnb lists the hot tub among the ten amenities guests search for most. In AirROI's Jasper area data, listings with a tub averaged $43,474 a year against $20,242 without, though tub homes are often larger. It is one of the strongest amenities in cabin markets.

**How often should a rental hot tub be drained?**

Most home spa manuals call for a full drain every few months, sooner with heavy use, and a rental is heavy use. Test the water at every turnover, and drain at once after any contamination.

**How much does it cost to run a hot tub?**

In Hydropool's example a tub uses about 187 kWh a month, which is about $27 to $30 at July 2026 average home electricity rates in Arkansas and Texas. Rental use runs higher. Add chemicals, filters, cleaner time and any service visits.

**Thinking about a tub for your rental?** [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) built from your address, your home and live booking data for your market, with the basis for every number. Or [see results from homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/) and how we count them.

**Sources:** [Airbnb: the amenities guests want](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/the-amenities-guests-want-25) · [AirROI: Jasper, Arkansas Airbnb data](https://airroi.com/airbnb-data/united-states/arkansas/jasper) · [Beyond Pricing: the most profitable vacation rental amenities](https://beyondpricing.com/blog/these-vacation-rental-amenities-are-the-most-profitable-plus-a-few-that-are-not) · [Hydropool: how much a hot tub adds to your electric bill](https://hydropoolhottubs.com/Learning-Centre/Blogs/How-Much-Will-a-Hot-Tub-Raise-My-Electric-Bill) · [U.S. EIA: average retail price of electricity by state](https://www.eia.gov/electricity/monthly/epm_table_grapher.php?t=epmt_5_6_a) · [Thumbtack: hot tub maintenance cost](https://www.thumbtack.com/p/hot-tub-cost-per-month) · [CDC: controlling Legionella in hot tubs](https://www.cdc.gov/control-legionella/php/toolkit/hot-tub-module.html) · [Houfy: vacation rental hot tub maintenance and rules](https://www.houfy.com/blog/vacation-rental-hot-tub-maintenance-and-rules-for-hosts) · [CPSC: hot tub temperatures](https://www.cpsc.gov/content/cpsc-warns-of-hot-tub-temperatures)


# Getting a Home Guest Ready: Checklist You Can Print

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/getting-a-home-guest-ready-checklist/
Updated: 2026-10-16
Summary: The full guest ready checklist: safety, beds, baths, kitchen, entry and turnovers, with a version you can print. Then get a free earnings estimate.

List & Host team · October 16, 2026

A guest ready home is one a stranger can open at 4 PM, find everything they need without sending a single message, and leave at 11 AM wanting to come back. That is the bar. This checklist comes from setting up and running the three homes our team runs: a glass house and a cabin loft in the [Buffalo River region of Arkansas](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/), and a 3 bedroom home in [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/). Read it once, then use the printable version at the bottom to walk your home room by room.

## Start with the five hour window

Many short term rentals run on an 11 AM checkout and a 4 PM check in. All three of ours do. That leaves five hours to strip beds, wash linens, clean, restock and inspect before the next guest arrives. Every item on this list is chosen to make that window easier, not harder.

Three choices matter most. Keep at least two full sets of linens for every bed, so the cleaner makes beds with clean sheets while the used set washes. Store every refill in one locked owner closet, so nothing runs out in the middle of a stay. And give your cleaner a written checklist they can follow without calling you. If your home sleeps eight or more, five hours is tight for one person. Plan for two cleaners on big turns, or a third set of linens so laundry can finish after the next guest checks in.

## 1. Safety first

Guests never see alarms or wiring in photos, but safety is one of the first things an insurer, a platform or a city inspector asks about, and it is the part of setup that protects people.

- **Smoke alarms.** The U.S. Fire Administration says to put smoke alarms inside and outside each bedroom and sleeping area, and on every level of the home, including the basement. Test them monthly and replace each alarm 10 years after the date it was made.

- **Carbon monoxide alarms.** If the home has any gas appliance, propane, a fireplace or an attached garage, install CO alarms on every level and outside sleeping areas, as the Consumer Product Safety Commission advises. The CPSC counts more than 200 deaths a year in the United States from accidental carbon monoxide poisoning not related to fire.

- **Fire extinguisher** in the kitchen, mounted where a guest can see it. Check the gauge on every turnover.

- **First aid kit** in a labeled spot, and a flashlight in each bedroom for power outages.

- **An emergency card** with the street address in large print, because a guest calling 911 may not know it. Add the nearest hospital and urgent care, and where the water shutoff and the breaker panel are.

- **Hot tub.** A locking cover, posted rules and a set water temperature. Check the water on every turn.

- **Stairs, decks and railings.** Walk them yourself and push on every rail. Loose boards and wobbly railings are injuries you can prevent.

## 2. The essentials Airbnb expects

Airbnb asks every host to provide what it calls essentials: toilet paper, soap for hands and body, one towel and one pillow per guest, and linens for each guest bed. A listing that checks the Essentials box without supplying them can be penalized, up to removal. Treat that list as the floor. Guests compare your home to a good hotel, and the rest of this checklist is what closes that gap.

## 3. Beds and linens

Sleep is what guests remember. Guests forgive a dated kitchen. They do not forgive a lumpy mattress or a sheet with a stain.

- A waterproof mattress protector and pillow protectors on every bed.

- Two pillows per sleeping spot, one firm and one soft.

- At least two full sets of sheets per bed, and three if you often have same day turns.

- White or light linens, so stains get seen and treated instead of hidden.

- An extra blanket in each bedroom closet.

- Blackout curtains in bedrooms. Night shift workers, light sleepers and families with small children all ask for them.

- If a sofa or daybed counts as a sleeping spot, say so honestly in the listing and keep bedding for it in the home.

## 4. Bathrooms

- Two bath towels, one hand towel and one washcloth per guest, and a bath mat for each shower.

- Shampoo, conditioner and body wash in refillable pump bottles.

- Two spare rolls of toilet paper per bathroom, where a guest can see them.

- A hair dryer, a plunger, and a small trash can with a lid and liners.

- A dark makeup towel, so the white towels stay white.

## 5. Kitchen

Stock the kitchen for a family making breakfast and one simple dinner. That covers most stays.

- Plates, bowls, glasses, mugs and silverware for your guest limit plus two.

- One large pot, one small pot, two pans, a baking sheet, a cutting board and one sharp knife.

- A coffee maker and filters, a kettle, a toaster and a microwave.

- A starter pack: coffee, salt, pepper, cooking oil, dish soap, dishwasher pods, paper towels and trash bags.

- A fridge that is empty and clean at every check in.

## 6. Entry and arrival

The arrival is the first review moment. A guest who stands in the dark trying a code three times will write about it.

- A keypad or smart lock with a new code for every stay. No key under the mat.

- An outdoor light on a timer or a sensor, so the door is lit after dark.

- An arrival guide with a photo of the door, where to park and how to get in.

- For rural homes, directions that work without cell signal and an honest note about the road. If the last stretch is steep or gravel, say so in the listing and again in the check in message. We learned that one at a rural home our team runs.

- The WiFi name and password on a card inside the home and in the check in message, never in the public listing.

## 7. The small things guests mention in reviews

- Fast WiFi. Run a speed test and put the result in the listing.

- Phone chargers by the beds.

- A short house manual: checkout steps, trash day, thermostat, TV and hot tub.

- A few local tips written by a person, not a stack of brochures.

- Real coffee.

## 8. Photos and the listing

Book photos only after the home is fully set up, staged and spotless. The first five photos carry most of the decision, so lead with what makes your home different: the view, the hot tub, the big kitchen, the yard. Every bed in a photo should be made with the linens guests will actually get. Then write the listing to match the photos exactly. A guest who finds what the photos promised gives five stars for accuracy, and accuracy is one of the six ratings Airbnb uses to pick Guest Favorites. Our guide to [Airbnb ranking and Guest Favorite](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-ranking-and-guest-favorite/) covers the rest.

## 9. The turnover routine

A home stays guest ready only with a routine. A good one looks like this after every checkout:

1. The cleaner is scheduled from the booking calendar as soon as a guest books, not the night before.

2. On arrival, the cleaner photographs anything damaged or missing before touching it, so a claim can be filed on time.

3. Beds stripped, linens washed, every surface cleaned, floors done, trash out.

4. Restock from the locked owner closet against a printed par list.

5. A final walk: a photo of each room, thermostat set, hot tub covered, doors locked.

Guests pay for the turn through the cleaning fee. Ours run from $85 at the cabin loft to $110 at the Fort Worth home and $225 at the glass house, set by the size of each home and how many guests it sleeps. We run all three on our own pricing and messaging system, with cleaners scheduled around every booking. You can [see what that system delivers](https://listandhost.com/results/) on our results page.

## Common mistakes we see

- **Listing before the home is finished.** The first reviews carry the most weight. A missing item in week one costs more than a week of waiting.

- **Too few linens.** One set per bed forces same day laundry and rushed cleans.

- **Promising what nature controls.** If a view, a creek or a trail depends on the season or the rain, say so plainly.

- **No backup cleaner.** Holidays and sick days happen. Line up a second cleaner before you need one.

- **No owner closet.** Without one, guests use the spare supplies and the next guest finds none.

Not sure the work is worth it for your home? [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) first, so you know what a guest ready home can earn before you buy a single towel.

## Printable guest ready checklist

Print it, walk the home room by room, and check each box.

### Safety

- Smoke alarm inside every bedroom

- Smoke alarm outside each sleeping area and on every level

- Every smoke alarm tested this month and under 10 years old

- Carbon monoxide alarm on every level and outside sleeping areas (gas, propane, fireplace or attached garage)

- Fire extinguisher in the kitchen, gauge in the green

- First aid kit in a labeled spot, flashlight in each bedroom

- Emergency card: street address, nearest hospital, water shutoff, breaker panel

- Hot tub cover locks, rules posted

- Stairs, decks and railings solid

### Beds

- Mattress protector and pillow protectors on every bed

- Two pillows per sleeping spot, one firm and one soft

- Two full sheet sets per bed, three for back to back turns

- Extra blanket in each bedroom

- Blackout curtains in bedrooms

- Bedding stocked for any sofa bed or daybed you list

### Bathrooms

- Two bath towels, one hand towel, one washcloth per guest

- Bath mat for each shower

- Shampoo, conditioner and body wash in pump bottles

- Two spare toilet paper rolls in sight

- Hair dryer, plunger, trash can with a lid

- Dark makeup towel

### Kitchen

- Place settings for your guest limit plus two

- Pots, pans, baking sheet, cutting board, sharp knife

- Coffee maker, filters, kettle, toaster, microwave

- Coffee, salt, pepper, oil, dish soap, dishwasher pods, paper towels, trash bags

- Fridge empty and clean

### Entry and arrival

- New lock code for this stay

- Door light works on a timer or sensor

- Arrival guide with a photo of the door and where to park

- Honest road note for rural, steep or gravel access

- WiFi card inside the home, never in the public listing

### Extras guests notice

- WiFi speed tested and stated in the listing

- Chargers by the beds

- House manual: checkout steps, trash day, thermostat, TV, hot tub

- A few local tips written by a person

- Locked owner closet stocked to the par list

### Every turnover

- Photos of any damage before cleaning starts

- Beds stripped, linens washed, beds remade

- Surfaces, floors and trash done

- Restocked to the par list

- Final walk: photo of each room, thermostat set, doors locked

List & Host owner guide: listandhost.com/blog/getting-a-home-guest-ready-checklist/

## Quick answers

**How long does it take to get a home guest ready?**

A furnished home can usually be ready in a few weeks: supplies, a smart lock, photos and the listing. An empty home takes longer because furniture delivery times vary.

**Who pays for cleaning between guests?**

The guest, through the cleaning fee you set on each platform. Our guest cleaning fees run from $85 to $225, set by the size of each home.

**Do I need a smart lock?**

No platform requires one, but self check in with a new code for every stay lets guests arrive at any hour and means no keys to lose or copy.

**Sources:** [U.S. Fire Administration: smoke alarms](https://www.usfa.fema.gov/prevention/home-fires/prepare-for-fire/smoke-alarms/) · [CPSC: carbon monoxide information center](https://www.cpsc.gov/Safety-Education/Safety-Education-Centers/Carbon-Monoxide-Information-Center) · [Airbnb Help Center: what are essential amenities](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2343) · [Airbnb Help Center: Guest favorites](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3495)


# Dynamic Pricing Explained for Short Term Rental Owners

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: How dynamic pricing works for a short term rental: floors, event weeks, gap nights and the fill ladder, with our real numbers. Get a free estimate.

List & Host team · October 16, 2026 · Updated October 18, 2026

A short term rental sells a different product every night. A Saturday during a big event and a Tuesday in January are not the same night, and pricing them the same leaves money on the table on one and an empty bed on the other. Dynamic pricing means moving the nightly price, and the minimum stay, with demand. This guide explains how it works in plain terms, using the rules our engine runs every day on the homes our team runs in [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/) and the [Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/). We offer the same engine to owners in other markets through our [remote pricing service](https://listandhost.com/services/).

## Why one price all year loses money

Three numbers from our own booking records, for stays from July to October 2026, show why a fixed price cannot work:

- **Weekends are worth more.** At our Fort Worth home, Friday and Saturday nights averaged $233 and weeknights $143, after discounts, before cleaning, taxes and platform fees. At our glass house, Friday and Saturday nights averaged $535 and weeknights $366, on the same basis. A stay with no nightly split in our records counts at its average night.

- **Event weekends are worth more again.** A three night stay over the Red River weekend in October averaged $254 a night at our Fort Worth home, about 50% above that home's $169 average for the month.

- **Many guests book late.** Of 75 stays booked across the three homes our team runs from July to mid October 2026, 25 were booked less than a week before arrival. A price set months ago and never touched again is wrong for those nights in one direction or the other.

## The parts of a pricing system

Every good pricing system, ours or anyone's, does the same few jobs. Here is each one, with the rule we actually run.

### 1. A floor under every night

The floor is the lowest nightly price any automatic rule may set. It protects the value of the home. Our Fort Worth home's floor is $149 and our glass house floor is $349. No automatic rule ever writes a price below the floor. Platform discounts you choose, like a last minute discount, still come off the nightly price after the fact, so set those knowing where your floor sits.

### 2. Event weeks, written down in advance

We keep a dated list of the events that move demand in each market, taken from official calendars: college football, concerts at Dickies Arena, Cowboys games, holidays and the Fort Worth Stock Show and Rodeo. Each event gets its own floor and its own minimum stay. Two real entries:

- Stock Show, January 15 to February 6, 2027: floors of $299 on weeknights and $379 on weekends, with a two night minimum.

- Red River weekend in October: a three night minimum, so one night bookings cannot break up the weekend.

Event floors are guards against cutting too far. The engine never raises one on its own. If the market for an event is hotter than the floor, a person decides the raise.

### 3. Weekend minimums that know about gaps

Friday and Saturday nights carry a two night minimum, so a single Saturday booking does not strand the Friday. The exception is a gap. If the open stretch is only one night long, the minimum stays at one, because a two night rule would make that night impossible to book.

### 4. Gap nights

A gap night is one open night stuck between two bookings. A home with a blanket two night minimum loses these all year. Our engine finds every one night gap and sets its minimum stay to one night. Short openings sell when the minimum allows it: in October 2026 a two night opening at our Fort Worth home, October 7 and 8, sold as two separate one night stays, both booked on October 7, between a stay that left on the 7th and one that arrived on the 9th.

### 5. The fill ladder

Open nights get cheaper slowly as the date gets closer, inside a fixed window, and never below the floor. The rules:

- The ladder works only on open stretches inside a window, on set nights of the week: Friday and Saturday nights 22 to 30 days out at our Fort Worth home, and Sunday to Thursday nights 15 to 26 days out at our glass house.

- Each night can be cut once a week: by 5% at Fort Worth and 7% at the glass house.

- At the glass house, a Friday or Saturday 35 to 45 days out can take one 7% step, only when bookings for that month's weekends are running behind.

- No night ever goes more than 20% below the price it had when the engine first saw it, and never below the floor.

- A Friday or Saturday is never priced below a weeknight in the same week.

- Nights with a minimum stay of three or more, usually event nights, are never cut.

- The window ends where the platform's own last minute discounts begin, at 21 days for Fort Worth and 14 days for the glass house, so two discounts never stack on the same night.

Those are the settings as of October 18, 2026. Until October 17, every open night in the window was cut 10% a week, 22 to 35 days out at Fort Worth and 15 to 29 at the glass house. A real example from that earlier rule: on September 21, 2026, the ladder cut three open Fort Worth weeknights, October 13 to 15, from $179 to $161, at 22 to 24 days out. Those nights later sold as part of a four night stay.

### 6. Watching for raises

Cutting is only half the job. When most of a week is already booked, the open nights left in it are worth more, not less. Since October 17, 2026 our engine may make small raises by itself on open nights a month or more out, at most 20% a move and three nights per home a week, when it has evidence such as a holiday. A person approves every big raise, and approved nights are put on hold so the fill ladder cannot cut them back down.

### 7. Safety on every change

- The engine never touches a booked night.

- Every change is logged before it is sent, then read back from the calendar to confirm it held. A mismatch sends an alert.

- Each run has a cap on how many nights it may change. A price run that would change more writes nothing and reports it.

- Nights a person sets by hand can be put on hold, and no automatic rule touches a held night.

You can see how the whole system fits together on our [how it works page](https://listandhost.com/how-it-works/), and [see the results from the homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/).

## Our numbers, month by month

| Month, 2026 | Fort Worth nights sold | Fort Worth average nightly | Glass house nights sold | Glass house average nightly |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| August | 12 of 31 (39%) | $217 | 16 of 31 (52%) | $455 |
| September | 20 of 30 (67%) | $169 | 25 of 30 (83%) | $306 |
| October | 24 of 31 (77%) | $169 | 27 of 31 (87%) | $502 |

Basis: accepted stays in our booking records as of October 16, 2026, counted by night. October is not over: it counts stays booked for the rest of the month, not money earned yet. Our pricing engine took over the glass house's prices on September 21, 2026, so most of its nights here were booked before then (every August night, 22 of 25 in September and 15 of 27 in October) and show the home and the season, not the engine. Average nightly is rent after discounts and before cleaning fees, platform fees and taxes, spread evenly across each stay. Past results, not a forecast for any other home.

In September, before the hard floor, low leftover prices and last minute discounts sold 11 nights at the glass house under $200, three of them at $142. The house sold 25 of 30 nights, but the month's average night fell to $306, and 22 of those 25 nights were booked before our engine took over its prices on September 21. On September 28 we set a hard floor of $349 a night on every channel and capped last minute discounts at 10 percent. Every night booked since then has sold at $314 or more. In October, peak fall color season, rate and occupancy rose together.

## What about Airbnb Smart Pricing?

Airbnb's Smart Pricing adjusts your nightly price based on demand, using what Airbnb describes as hundreds of factors about your listing and your area, inside a minimum and maximum you set. It is a fair starting point. Know its limits before you rely on it:

- Airbnb says the price a guest pays can go below the minimum you set, because discounts still apply.

- Weekly, monthly and trip length discounts override Smart Pricing.

- It prices one platform. If you also list on Vrbo and Booking.com, each needs its own prices.

- It does not know your cleaning cost, your event calendar or the nights you would rather leave empty than sell cheap.

## Questions to ask any manager about pricing

1. What is my floor, and who can change it?

2. How do you price event weeks, and where does your event list come from?

3. Do you sell one night gaps?

4. When do open nights start getting cheaper, by how much, and what stops them?

5. Do your cuts stack with the platform's last minute discounts?

6. Who approves a raise, and how fast?

7. Can I see every price change you made last month?

If a manager cannot answer all seven in plain words, the pricing is a guess. Want to see what these rules would do for your home? [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/), with nightly rates by season for your address.

## Quick answers

**What is a price floor?**

The lowest nightly price any automatic rule may set. Our Fort Worth home's floor is $149 and our glass house floor is $349.

**What is a gap night?**

An open night stuck between two bookings. A blanket two night minimum makes it impossible to book, so our engine sets the minimum stay for those gaps to one night.

**Does Airbnb Smart Pricing do the same thing?**

Smart Pricing adjusts nightly prices inside a minimum and maximum you set. Airbnb notes that discounts can still take the price a guest pays below your minimum, and it prices only Airbnb.

**Sources:** [Airbnb Help Center: Smart Pricing](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1168) · [Airbnb Help Center: how search results work](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/39) · [Fort Worth Stock Show and Rodeo: visitor FAQ](https://www.fwssr.com/p/plan-a-visit/frequently-asked-questions) · [Dickies Arena: events](https://www.dickiesarena.com/events/) · [Airbnb Resources: setting a price for longer stays](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/setting-a-price-for-longer-stays-379)


# Buying a Short Term Rental: The Numbers to Check First

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/buying-a-short-term-rental-numbers-to-check/
Updated: 2026-10-16
Summary: Before you buy a short term rental: the gross multiple, proof of occupancy and real costs, with a worked example and our own numbers. Free estimate.

List & Host team · October 16, 2026

A listing that says a home grosses $80,000 a year on Airbnb tells you almost nothing. Gross is not net, last year is not next year, and a calendar that looks full is not proof that anyone paid. Before you offer on a short term rental, check a handful of numbers yourself. This guide walks through the three that matter most, the gross multiple, proof of occupancy and the real costs, with a worked example and the figures from the homes our team runs in [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/) and the [Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/).

## 1. The gross multiple

The gross multiple is the asking price divided by the last 12 months of gross booking revenue. Gross booking revenue here means what guests paid for the nights plus the cleaning fees, before platform fees, and without taxes.

Example: a home asking $400,000 that booked $55,000 over the last 12 months has a gross multiple of about 7.3. The same home at $550,000 would be 10.0. A lower multiple means you pay less for each dollar the home brings in. Run the same math for a long term rental nearby, using a year of rent, and compare. If the short term multiple is not clearly better, the extra work and risk of nightly guests may not pay for itself.

The multiple is a fast filter, not a valuation. It ignores costs, which is why the next two sections matter more.

## 2. Proof of occupancy and revenue

Ask the seller for documents, not a summary. In order of value:

1. **Platform exports for 24 months.** Airbnb's Earnings page can build a CSV file of paid transactions with gross earnings, host service fees, cleaning fees and taxes withheld for each booking. Vrbo and Booking.com have their own reports. Ask for every platform the home was listed on.

2. **Bank deposits that match the payouts.** A payout report and a bank statement that agree are hard to fake.

3. **Booked nights versus available nights, by month.** Occupancy is booked nights divided by nights that were open for sale. Ask how many nights the owner blocked for personal use or repairs, because a calendar full of blocked dates looks booked on a screen.

4. **Average nightly rate and average stay length.** A home that hit its revenue with deep discounts and one night stays costs more to run than one that got there on full price weekends.

5. **Reviews and badges.** Note the review count, the rating and whether the home is a Guest Favorite.

**Plan as if the reviews do not come with the house.** Listings and reviews usually stay with the seller's host account, so a buyer often starts a new listing with zero reviews. Ask the seller to hide or close the old listing on closing day, and settle any future bookings and their payouts in writing.

### Why 24 months, not 12

One year can mislead in either direction. A big event year inflates it, and a year with a long repair hides what the home can do. Seasonality is large even inside one fall. Here is what the homes our team runs did in 2026:

| Month, 2026 | Fort Worth nights sold | Glass house nights sold |
| - | - | - |
| August | 12 of 31 (39%) | 16 of 31 (52%) |
| September | 20 of 30 (67%) | 25 of 30 (83%) |
| October | 24 of 31 (77%) | 27 of 31 (87%) |

Basis: accepted stays in our booking records as of October 16, 2026, counted by night. October is not over: it counts stays booked for the rest of the month, not money earned yet. Past results, not a forecast for any other home.

The same home swung from 39% to 77% of nights sold within three months. A seller who shows you only their best quarter is showing you a different business than the one you will run in February. You can [see results from the homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/) for more of our own numbers.

## 3. The real costs

Gross revenue loses a large share to costs before anything reaches the owner. These are the lines to price before you offer.

- **Platform fees.** Airbnb's single fee is 15.5% of the booking for most hosts on it, and hosts who connect through property management software must use it. On Airbnb bookings at the homes our team runs, the host fee has run from 15.5% to about 16.3% of the booking subtotal, depending on the home. Vrbo and Booking.com set their own commissions; check the rate in each dashboard.

- **Cleaning.** One clean per stay. Guests pay a cleaning fee, but you pay the cleaner on every turn. Our guest cleaning fees run from $85 for a small cabin loft to $225 for a home that sleeps 10, and the homes our team runs average 2.7 to 3.4 nights a stay, so turns add up fast.

- **Utilities.** You pay them, not the guest. Electricity at our Fort Worth home runs about $200 to $230 a month. Add water, trash, internet and any streaming services.

- **Property tax.** Use the seller's last tax bill for the address.

- **Insurance.** A standard homeowner policy may not cover paying guests. Get a written quote for a short term rental policy before you offer.

- **Supplies, repairs and replacement.** Linens, towels, paper goods and coffee every month, plus repairs and furniture that wears out faster with hundreds of guests a year.

- **Management.** If you will not run it yourself, add the manager's fee. Our [guide to management fees](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-management-fees/) shows how to compare quotes.

## A worked example

This is an example to show the method, not a forecast for any home. A Fort Worth home asks $400,000. The seller's exports show $55,000 in gross bookings over the last 12 months.

********

| Line | Example amount | Basis |
| - | - | - |
| Gross bookings, last 12 months | $55,000 | Seller's platform exports (example) |
| Platform fees | −$8,525 | 15.5% Airbnb single fee |
| Cleaning | −$8,100 | 81 turns at $100 each (example): 60% of nights sold, 2.7 night average stay (our Fort Worth average) |
| Electricity | −$2,580 | $215 a month, the middle of our Fort Worth bills |
| Water, trash, internet, streaming | −$2,400 | $200 a month, example; use the seller's bills |
| Supplies | −$1,650 | 3% of gross, example |
| Repairs and replacement reserve | −$2,750 | 5% of gross, example |
| Property tax | −$8,000 | Seller's last tax bill (example) |
| Insurance | your quote | Short term rental policy |
| Management | your quote | If you hire one |
| Left before insurance and management | $20,995 | About 5.2% of the price, before any mortgage |

Notice how fast $55,000 becomes about $21,000, and that is before insurance, management or a loan payment. Now change one input at a time. Drop occupancy to 50% and gross falls with it while property tax and utilities do not. Raise the price to $450,000 and the same $20,995 is about 4.7% of the price, before insurance and management. A deal that only works at the seller's best year is not a deal.

## Check the building

- **Inspections beyond the standard report.** A general home inspection may not cover a well, a septic system, a pool, a hot tub or outbuildings. Order those separately for rural homes.

- **Access.** Drive the road in the rain. A steep or gravel entrance affects which guests can arrive and what the listing must say.

## Red flags

- The seller cannot or will not export platform reports.

- Revenue numbers that come from a projection or a revenue calculator, not bookings.

- One huge month carrying the year, tied to a one time event.

- A long run of blocked dates presented as booked.

- Furniture, linens and supplies not included in the sale.

Before you make an offer, [get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) for the address. We build it from nearby homes and real booking data, with the basis for every number, so you can test the seller's story against the market.

## Quick answers

**What is a gross multiple?**

The asking price divided by the last 12 months of gross booking revenue. A $400,000 home with $55,000 in bookings has a gross multiple of about 7.3.

**Do Airbnb reviews transfer to a new owner?**

Plan as if they do not. Listings and reviews usually stay with the seller's host account, so a buyer often starts a new listing with zero reviews.

**What occupancy should I expect?**

It depends on the market and the season. Across our Fort Worth home and our glass house, the share of nights sold ranged from 39% to 87% month to month between August and October 2026, October as booked on October 16.

**Sources:** [Airbnb Help Center: service fees](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1857) · [Airbnb Help Center: get a transaction history report](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/418) · [Vacasa: transferring a listing to a new owner](https://vacasa.com/homeowner-guides/transfer-vrbo-airbnb-to-new-owner)


# Buffalo River Cabin Income by Season: Month by Month

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/buffalo-river-cabin-income-by-season/
Updated: 2026-10-16
Summary: What each season brings for cabins near the Buffalo National River: Jasper area market data and real monthly numbers from two homes. Get a free estimate.

List & Host team · October 16, 2026

Cabins near the Buffalo National River sell a feeling: bluffs, quiet, stars and a long weekend away. The income comes in waves, and the waves do not always follow the river. This guide walks through the year season by season, with market data for the Jasper area and real numbers from two homes our team runs in the region: a glass house that sleeps 10, and a one bedroom cabin loft next to it. For how we run homes here, see our [Buffalo River cabin management](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/) page.

**Short answer.** AirROI's data for the Jasper area puts the average listing at $26,695 a year with 37% of nights booked. October, May and June are the strong months. January, February and September are the weak ones. A distinctive home can beat those averages by a wide margin, and a hot tub is one of the biggest dividing lines in the data.

## The market in numbers

AirROI tracked 180 active listings around Jasper from August 2025 to July 2026.

| Season | Months | Occupancy | Average night | Monthly revenue |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Peak | May, June, October | 48.9% | $244 | $3,716 |
| Shoulder | All other months | 39.4% | $230 | $2,881 |
| Low | January, February, September | 29.0% | $207 | $1,794 |
| Full year |  | 37.3% | $232 | $26,695 a year |

Two more numbers from the same data stand out. Listings with a hot tub, 27.8% of the market, averaged $43,474 a year, against $20,242 for listings without one. Homes with tubs are often larger, so the tub is not the whole difference, but it is a big part of what guests filter for here. Our [hot tub guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/hot-tub-rentals-upkeep-and-earnings/) covers the costs.

Demand for the area keeps growing. The Buffalo National River logged 1,686,348 visits in 2024, the most on record, up from 1,549,467 in 2023 and 1,326,282 in 2019.

## What our glass house did, month by month

| Month | Nights booked | Share of nights | Average night | Payouts |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| August 2026 | 16 of 31 | 52% | $455 | $7,913 |
| September 2026 | 25 of 30 | 83% | $306 | $7,419 |
| October 2026, booked to date | 27 of 31 | 87% | $502 | $13,720 |

As of October 16, 2026. Average night is what guests paid after discounts, before cleaning fees, taxes and platform fees. Payouts are after platform fees and before cleaning and other costs. October is not over, so its figures are booked, not earned. The home is rated 4.9 on Airbnb and is a Guest Favorite. Full details and our counting method are on the [glass house results page](https://listandhost.com/results/buffalo-river-glass-house/).

## Spring: March to May

Spring is when the upper river is most reliable. The Buffalo River Chamber's river guide says floating on the upper river around Ponca is mostly limited to spring and early summer, possibly fall if it is a wet one, and depends on rain. Waterfalls run after storms and the trails turn green. May is a peak month in the AirROI data.

At our glass house, a mid March 2027 stay was booked seven months ahead at $449 a night. Spring weekends book early for the same reason fall weekends do: people plan Ozark trips around a known window.

## Summer: June to August

June is the area's top revenue month in AirROI's data. Families and big groups travel, and nightly rates peak. But the upper river is a different story by late summer. A park spokesperson told KY3 that in the peak summer season the upper section of the river around Ponca tends to dry up, and that it happens every year.

That matters for how you sell. A listing that promises floating in August will disappoint guests and earn bad reviews. Sell what is always there: the deck, the hot tub, the trails, the view and the dark sky.

Our glass house was booked 16 of 31 nights in August 2026 at an average of $455, mostly by groups of four to eight.

## Fall: September to November

Fall is two seasons in one. September is one of the weakest months in the market data. October is one of the strongest.

**September.** Our glass house filled 25 of 30 nights, but only by selling many weeknights under $200 to people who booked a few days out. The month's average night fell to $306. Full is not the same as profitable. Each of those short stays still needed a full clean and still added wear. On September 28 we set a hard floor of $349 a night, and every night booked since has sold at $314 or more.

**October.** The leaves turn and the elk rut is on. Arkansas tourism notes that September through October is the elk mating season, when bulls bugle in the open fields of Boxley Valley, and that fall weekends draw crowds to the roadside pullouts. Our glass house has 27 of 31 October nights booked at an average of $502, with Friday and Saturday nights at $685, after discounts, before cleaning, taxes and platform fees. October is its best month so far. Our pricing engine took over its prices on September 21, 2026, and 15 of those 27 nights were booked before then.

**November.** Quieter, but still strong early in the month. As of mid October, our glass house had 14 November nights booked, or 47%, at an average of $547, including Thanksgiving at $624 a night.

## Winter: December to February

January has the lowest occupancy in the AirROI data, and February is the lowest revenue month. Holidays are the exception. Our glass house sold Christmas at $799 a night and the week after at $632 a night. An eight night stay in late January was booked six months ahead at $529 a night. As of mid October, though, January and February were only 16% and 18% booked.

Winter also brings snow, ice and slow gravel roads. Tell guests plainly before they book, so normal winter weather never turns into a cancellation dispute. Elk can still be seen at dawn and dusk, and clear cold nights give the best stargazing of the year. A hot tub turns a cold weekend into a selling point.

## A small cabin, month by month

Our one bedroom cabin loft sleeps 4 and went live on September 24, 2026. As a new listing with no reviews, we priced weeknights at $89 and weekends at $149 until it earns its first three reviews. In October it has 16 of 31 nights booked, or 52%, at an average of $97: $113 on weekend nights and $87 on weeknights. October payouts come to $1,709. The launch plan is on the [cabin loft results page](https://listandhost.com/results/ozark-cabin-loft/).

Here is what a full year could look like for a cabin like it, using AirROI's seasonal occupancy and nightly rates near what our cabin will charge once it has reviews. This is an example, not a promise.

| Season | Days | Occupancy | Nights sold | Average night | Nightly revenue |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Peak: May, June, October | 92 | 48.9% | 45 | $140 | $6,300 |
| Shoulder: the other six months | 184 | 39.4% | 72 | $125 | $9,000 |
| Low: January, February, September | 89 | 29.0% | 26 | $110 | $2,860 |
| Year | 365 |  | 143 |  | $18,160 |

Basis: occupancy by season from AirROI's Jasper area data. Rates are set near our cabin's planned prices after reviews, $109 to $129 on weeknights and $149 to $169 on weekends. Cleaning fees are left out because they mostly pay the cleaner. Platform fees and discounts come out of this, about 19 percent across the bookings of the homes our team runs, then utilities, supplies and repairs. A hot tub, strong photos and quick reviews can move a cabin well above the market averages. A thin winter calendar can pull it below. To run this math on your own place, [get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/).

## Five habits that smooth out the seasons

1. **Price weekends early.** At our glass house, stays that included a weekend night were booked a median of 45 days ahead. Weekday only stays were booked a median of 5 days ahead.

2. **Hold floors in slow months.** Decide your lowest price before the slow month starts. A cheap weeknight earns little once platform fees, utilities and wear are paid.

3. **Use minimum stays for holidays.** Both holiday weeks at our glass house sold with three night minimums.

4. **Write for rural arrivals.** Weak cell signal, gravel roads and steep drives need clear directions, photos of where to park, and plain advice on what vehicle to bring.

5. **Sell what is always there.** Views, privacy, the hot tub, trails and stars. The river is a bonus when the water is up.

## Questions owners ask

**What is the best month for a Buffalo River cabin?**

October, May and June are the peak months in AirROI's data for the Jasper area. At our glass house, October 2026 is the best month so far, with 27 of 31 nights booked as of October 16 at an average of $502.

**Can I count on floating to fill summer weekends?**

No. The upper river around Ponca tends to dry up in peak summer, according to the park. Sell the home, the views and the amenities, and treat good water as a bonus.

**How do cabins near the Buffalo River do in winter?**

January and February are the slowest months in the market data. Holidays sell well, and a hot tub helps. Plan for a thin calendar and be clear with guests about winter roads.

Or [see results from homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/) and how we count them.
