# Airbnb vs Vrbo vs Booking.com for Owners: Fees Compared

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-vs-vrbo-vs-booking-com-for-owners/
Updated: 2026-10-16
Summary: What Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com charge hosts in 2026, how each behaves, and where guests at the homes we run come from. Get a free estimate for yours.

List & Host team · October 16, 2026

Most owners start on Airbnb, then wonder whether Vrbo and Booking.com are worth the extra work. The honest answer: usually yes, but not for the reasons people expect. The extra channels rarely double your bookings. They fill gaps, reach guests who never open Airbnb, and protect you if one platform changes its rules. Here is how the three compare in 2026, with what bookings at the homes our team runs show. Our team runs homes this way in [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/) and the [Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/), and offers pricing and listing work to owners anywhere through our [services](https://listandhost.com/services/).

## What each platform charges

| Platform | What the host pays | What the guest pays on top |
| - | - | - |
| Airbnb | A single host fee, 15.5% for most hosts. Airbnb is moving hosts off the old split fee, where the host paid about 3% and the guest paid a separate fee. | Under the single fee, the whole fee comes out of the host payout, so the guest sees no separate service fee. |
| Vrbo | Pay per booking: a 5% commission on the rent and required fees, plus 3% payment processing on what the guest pays. | A service fee on a sliding scale. |
| Booking.com | A commission set in your agreement, typically around 15%. It can vary with location and the options you choose. | In our bookings, no separate guest fee beyond taxes. |

Vrbo also offers an annual subscription in place of pay per booking for some hosts. Check each platform's current terms before you list, because fees change.

## What the homes our team runs show

Our team runs three homes in Fort Worth and the Buffalo River region on all three channels, through one system that keeps calendars and prices in sync. Here is every accepted stay in our booking system from late July 2026 through bookings already made for 2027, as of October 16, 2026.

| Platform | Stays | Nights | Average stay | Average group | Share of booking revenue | Host fee in our records |
| - | - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Airbnb | 64 | 191 | 3.0 nights | 4.0 guests | 83% | 15.7% of the booking subtotal |
| Vrbo | 9 | 30 | 3.3 nights | 4.3 guests | 15% | 5.5% commission, plus processing |
| Booking.com | 2 | 5 | 2.5 nights | 4.0 guests | 2% | 15.0% |

Booking subtotal means the nightly rate plus the cleaning and other fees, after any discounts. On our Vrbo stays, guests also paid a Vrbo service fee of about 12.8% on top of that subtotal. Shares use the booking revenue in our booking system. Counted by bank deposits instead, Airbnb was about 85%, Vrbo about 13% and Booking.com about 1%, mostly because one Vrbo stay was partly refunded to the guest.

Three things stand out:

- **Airbnb is the engine.** It brought more than four of every five dollars across the homes our team runs.

- **Vrbo adds real money.** About 15% of booking revenue. Our Vrbo stays ran a little longer and a little larger, though 9 stays is a small sample. At the glass house, Vrbo brought 6 stays, including a 5 night fall stay and an 8 guest summer weekend.

- **Booking.com is small but real.** Two stays so far: three late September weeknights at the glass house, and a November concert weekend in Fort Worth that sold within hours of a price change.

## The fee math, side by side

Take a three night stay at $250 a night with a $150 cleaning fee: a $900 booking subtotal. Roughly, before taxes:

|  | Airbnb, 15.5% | Vrbo, 5% plus 3% | Booking.com, 15% |
| - | - | - | - |
| Host pays | about $140 | about $72 | about $135 |
| Host keeps | about $760 | about $828 | about $765 |
| Guest pays before taxes | $900 | $900 plus Vrbo's service fee | $900 |

This is an illustration. Your real rates depend on your agreements, your market and the options you turn on. Vrbo's processing fee is charged on the full amount the guest pays, taxes included, so it runs a little higher than shown.

Vrbo looks cheapest for the host, but its guest fee makes the same home look more expensive to the guest. When you set prices, compare what the guest sees on each site, not only what you keep. What matters in the end is what you keep per night, after fees, across the whole year.

## How the platforms behave differently

### Cancellations

Each platform has its own cancellation policies, and you set them separately on each one. At the glass house our team runs, 7 of 35 Airbnb bookings were cancelled before arrival in our first months, all made while the listing had a moderate policy that refunded in full until five days before arrival. We moved it to a firm policy. On Vrbo, the same home uses a strict policy with a full refund only 60 or more days before arrival. Choose the policy that fits your market, then check it on every channel.

### Search and ranking

Each platform ranks listings with its own signals, such as reviews, price, response speed, cancellations and how often the listing books. Reviews do not carry across. A home with 50 Airbnb reviews starts at zero on Vrbo. Expect a slow first few months on each new channel, and price a little sharper until the first reviews land.

## Double bookings: the one risk you must solve

Listing on three sites means three calendars. If they are not in sync, two guests can book the same night, and one of them gets cancelled. Basic calendar links between sites can lag. A channel manager or property management system that connects to each platform directly keeps prices, minimum stays and availability in one place. Our team runs its homes this way: one calendar, one price writer, and every price change read back to confirm it landed. You can see what that system does on our [results page](https://listandhost.com/results/).

## Our recommendation

1. **Start on Airbnb** and earn your first reviews there. That is where most guests are.

2. **Add Vrbo** once the listing is stable, especially for homes that sleep six or more.

3. **Add Booking.com** when your calendar sync is solid and your house rules are written down.

4. **Write each listing for its own site.** Never mention one platform inside another platform's listing, and keep contact details inside each platform's messages.

5. **Compare by what you keep.** Every quarter, look at payout per night after fees for each channel.

Not sure which mix fits your home? [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) and we will include a channel plan.

## Questions owners ask

**Is Vrbo cheaper than Airbnb for hosts?**

On the host side, usually yes: Vrbo's pay per booking terms are a 5% commission plus 3% payment processing, against Airbnb's 15.5% single fee for most hosts. But Vrbo adds a service fee for the guest, so the same home can look more expensive to guests on Vrbo.

**Should I list on all three platforms?**

Most homes do best on Airbnb and Vrbo, with Booking.com added once calendars are synced and rules are written. In our records, Airbnb brought 83% of booking revenue, Vrbo 15% and Booking.com about 2%.

**How do I avoid double bookings across platforms?**

Use a channel manager or property management system that connects to each platform directly, so one calendar controls availability, prices and minimum stays everywhere.

**Want a channel plan for your home?** [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) built from your address, your home and live booking data for your market, with the basis for every number. Or [see results from homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/) and how we count them.

**Sources:** [Airbnb Help: service fees](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1857) · [OwnerRez: understanding Vrbo's service fees](https://www.ownerrez.com/guides/understanding-vrbos-service-fees) · [Hospitable: Booking.com host fees](https://hospitable.com/booking-com-host-fees)


# Airbnb Ranking Basics and How to Earn Guest Favorite

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-ranking-and-guest-favorite/
Updated: 2026-10-16
Summary: What Airbnb says moves a home up in search, the real Guest Favorite and Superhost rules, and nine habits that help. Get a free earnings estimate.

List & Host team · October 16, 2026

Guests choose from the homes Airbnb shows them first. If yours is not among them, nothing else about the home matters: not the hot tub, not the linens, not the price. This guide covers what Airbnb says it ranks on, the real rules for the Guest Favorite badge and for Superhost, and the habits that move a listing up. It applies in any market. Our team runs the same playbook on the homes it runs in [Fort Worth](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/) and the [Buffalo River region](https://listandhost.com/buffalo-river/), and offers it to owners anywhere through our [remote pricing and listing service](https://listandhost.com/services/).

## What Airbnb says it ranks on

Airbnb publishes the main factors behind its search results in its help center. In plain words:

- **Quality.** Photos, ratings and reviews, how you communicate with guests, listing details, customer service history, cancellations and amenities. Airbnb says higher quality listings with better ratings and reviews tend to rank higher.

- **Popularity.** How often guests save your listing to a wishlist, message you and book.

- **Price.** Your total price compared with similar listings nearby. Airbnb says listings priced below comparable listings in the area tend to rank higher.

- **Location.** Homes in places guests like to stay, such as near popular landmarks, can rank higher.

- **Availability.** More open dates and more flexible stay lengths help a listing match more trips.

- **Instant Book.** Instantly bookable listings may rank higher because the booking is confirmed right away.

- **Responsiveness.** For listings that are not instantly bookable, how quickly you answer inquiries and how often you decline requests.

- **Personalization and variety.** A guest's past bookings shape what they see, and Airbnb mixes in different hosts and price points.

New listings are designed to show up well at first and usually appear in search within 24 hours of going live. That early window is the best chance a home gets, so open the calendar only when the home is fully ready. Our [guest ready checklist](https://listandhost.com/blog/getting-a-home-guest-ready-checklist/) covers what to finish before launch.

## What Guest Favorite is

Airbnb launched Guest Favorites on November 8, 2023, as a collection of about 2 million of its most loved homes. At launch, Airbnb said these homes were rated above 4.9 stars on average and scored high in six categories: ease of check in, cleanliness, accuracy, host communication, location and value. It said host cancellations and quality issues for these homes averaged about 1 percent.

The current rules in Airbnb's help center:

- At least 5 reviews in the past 4 years, with at least 1 of them in the past 2 years.

- The overall star rating plus the six category ratings.

- Reliability: the host cancellation rate, how often reviews get removed, and quality incidents reported to Airbnb customer service.

- Homes are compared globally, within their country, or both.

- Eligible homes are evaluated every day. The top 1, 5 and 10 percent also get a gold trophy, a gold badge and a highlight at the top of the listing.

Airbnb does not publish one cutoff score. In practice, every review below five stars weighs a lot while your count is small. With five reviews, a single four star review pulls the average down to 4.8. With fifty reviews, the same review barely moves it. That is why the first months of a listing deserve the most care.

## Superhost is a separate badge

Guest Favorite belongs to a home. Superhost belongs to the host. Airbnb checks Superhost status every three months, looking back over the past 12 months, and awards it four times a year. To qualify, a host needs:

- A 4.8 or higher overall rating.

- Replies to 90 percent of new messages, and an accept or decline on new requests, within 24 hours.

- A cancellation rate under 1 percent.

- At least 10 reservations, or 3 reservations that total at least 100 nights.

Only the owner of a listing is evaluated, not co hosts. That matters if you hire help. In a co hosting setup where you keep the listing, the reviews and the badges stay with your account.

Airbnb also says that for homes, its search looks at the Superhost criteria themselves: host cancellations, responsiveness, and ratings and reviews. So even before you earn the badge, the habits behind it already count.

## What we have seen on the listings our team runs

Our glass house in the Buffalo River region hosted its first guests in the summer of 2026. On September 5, with only four reviews, a logged out search of its area for a family of four showed it first on page one. It is a Guest Favorite today, with a rating near 4.9. Our ranking checks that month pointed to three levers: reviews, the badge, and a price inside the band of nearby homes. Changing the title was not one of them.

Our Fort Worth home also opened in July 2026. By mid October it had 14 Airbnb reviews, 12 of them five stars. One guest summed up why location is a ranking factor:

“Super close to the convention center and downtown area.” Guest, Sep 2026

Both homes run on our own pricing and messaging system. You can [see results from the homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/), month by month.

## Nine habits that move a listing up

1. **Launch ready, priced for the first five reviews.** A home that opens half finished collects its worst reviews when they count most. When we launched our cabin loft, Airbnb's new listing discount of 20 percent was running, and we kept weeknights modest until the first reviews came in.

2. **Turn on Instant Book.** Airbnb says instantly bookable listings may rank higher. Use house rules and guest requirements to screen, not manual approval.

3. **Answer fast, every time.** Superhost needs 90 percent of messages answered within 24 hours. Aim for minutes during the day. Guests who get a fast answer book, and booking is a popularity signal.

4. **Keep the calendar open and flexible.** Availability and flexible stay lengths are ranking factors. Open nights a year ahead, and let a one night gap between two bookings sell as a one night stay. Our [dynamic pricing guide](https://listandhost.com/blog/dynamic-pricing-explained-for-owners/) shows how we handle gap nights.

5. **Price against real comparable homes.** Airbnb compares your total price, cleaning fee included, with similar homes nearby. Check the homes that show next to yours for the same dates and guest count.

6. **Never cancel on a guest.** Host cancellations count against Superhost, against Guest Favorite reliability and against ranking. Keep your calendar synced across every platform so a double booking cannot happen.

7. **Make the listing match the stay.** Accuracy is one of the six ratings. If a feature depends on the weather or the season, say so. A guest who finds less than the photos promised rates accuracy low, even if everything else was perfect.

8. **Fix small problems before they become reviews.** Send a short message the first morning of each stay. A slow drain fixed on day one is a five star stay. Found on day three, it is a four star review.

9. **Follow up after every stay, honestly.** Thank the guest, leave them a review, and ask them to message you first if anything fell short. Never offer anything for a review. Airbnb's review policy says reviews may not be provided or withheld in exchange for something of value, including a discount or a refund.

## What does not work

- **Stuffing the title with keywords.** Guests search by place, dates and guest count, then filter for amenities. A clear title that names the main feature does more.

- **Trading or paying for reviews.** It breaks Airbnb's policy and puts the listing at risk.

- **Pressuring guests to change a review.** Airbnb's policy also bans pressure and coordination around reviews.

- **Pricing far below the market for good.** Price helps ranking, but a home that stays cheap trains the market to expect it. Use floors and event pricing so a slow week does not set your value.

- **Blocking most of the calendar.** Fewer open dates means fewer searches your home can match.

## A ranking check you can run every week

1. Open a private browser window so you are not logged in.

2. Search your area with real dates two weeks and five weeks out, and a realistic guest count.

3. Write down your position, the price Airbnb shows for your home, and the prices of the homes around it.

4. Repeat for one weekend and one weeknight.

5. If you are off page one, check price first, then photos, then minimum stays and open dates.

Ten minutes a week is enough to catch a problem before it costs a month. If you would rather have the numbers in front of you, [get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) and we will show where your home should land against nearby listings.

## Quick answers

**How many reviews does a home need for Guest Favorite?**

Airbnb requires at least 5 reviews in the past 4 years, with at least 1 of them in the past 2 years. Ratings, the six category scores and reliability decide the rest.

**Is Guest Favorite the same as Superhost?**

No. Guest Favorite belongs to a home and is evaluated every day. Superhost belongs to the host and is checked every three months over the past 12 months.

**Does a lower price help my ranking?**

Airbnb says listings priced below comparable homes nearby tend to rank higher. Price is one factor among many, so use price floors to keep a slow week from selling your home too cheap.

**Sources:** [Airbnb Help Center: how search results work](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/39) · [Airbnb Help Center: Guest favorites](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3495) · [Airbnb Newsroom: Airbnb introduces Guest Favorites](https://news.airbnb.com/airbnb-introduces-guest-favorites/) · [Airbnb Help Center: how to become a Superhost](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/829) · [Airbnb Help Center: reviews policy](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2673)


# 30 Night Stays for Traveling Nurses in Fort Worth

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/traveling-nurse-30-night-stays-fort-worth/
Updated: 2026-10-16
Summary: Hosting traveling nurses in Fort Worth: what changes at 28 nights and beyond, how to price a monthly stay and set up the home. Get a free estimate.

List & Host team · October 16, 2026

Fort Worth has a large hospital district just south of downtown, and hospitals there, like hospitals across the country, bring in traveling nurses on contracts that run for months. For a home owner, that is a different kind of guest: one booking instead of ten, one clean instead of ten, and a quiet professional who needs to sleep. This guide covers what changes at 28 nights and beyond, how to price a monthly stay, and how to set a home up for a nurse. If you own in the city, our [Fort Worth management page](https://listandhost.com/fort-worth/) shows how we run homes here.

## Why nurses come to Fort Worth

The Near Southside, just south of downtown, is the city's medical district. Baylor Scott and White All Saints, Cook Children's Medical Center, Texas Health Harris Methodist Hospital Fort Worth and the JPS Health Network all sit in or next to it, with many clinics and medical offices around them. Hospitals fill staffing gaps with travel nurses, and staffing firms describe 13 weeks as the most common contract length, often with an option to extend for another 13.

A nurse on a 13 week contract needs about three months of housing, close to the hospital, quiet enough to sleep after a night shift, and simple to pay for. That is a fit for a furnished home that would otherwise sit half empty on winter weeknights.

## What the federal travel rate says about budgets

The U.S. General Services Administration sets the lodging rate federal employees can be reimbursed when they travel. For Fort Worth and the rest of Tarrant County, the federal year from October 2026 to September 2027 sets lodging at $192 a night and meals and incidentals at $80 a day. The standard rate for places without their own rate is $113 a night.

Travel nurse agencies set their own housing stipends, and those vary by agency and contract, so treat the federal rate as a ceiling for what a traveler might be paid for lodging, not a price to charge. Nurses compare monthly totals. A clean home with utilities and internet included, at a fair monthly price, competes well.

## What changes at 28 nights

Airbnb changes a few things once a stay reaches 28 nights. Here is how they line up for a Fort Worth home booked on Airbnb.

| Stay length | 1 to 27 nights | 28 to 29 nights | 30 nights or more |
| - | - | - | - |
| Airbnb cancellation policy | Your standard policy | Long term policy | Long term policy |
| Airbnb payouts | After check in | Monthly | Monthly |
| Airbnb monthly discount | Does not apply | Applies at 28 nights | Applies |

A few details behind the table:

- **Long term cancellation.** Airbnb's long term policies apply to stays of 28 nights or more. Under Long Term Firm, a guest must cancel at least 30 days before check in for a full refund. After that, the host is paid for nights already spent plus 30 more nights, or for all remaining nights if fewer than 30 are left.

- **Monthly payouts.** For stays of 28 nights or more, Airbnb charges the first month up front and usually releases the first payout by the end of the business day after check in, then pays monthly for the rest of the stay.

## 28 nights or a lease

Some owners cap stays at 28 or 29 nights so every booking runs as a short stay on the platform. Others accept 30 nights or more and sign a written lease. Both are common. Pick one on purpose before the first monthly guest asks.

## How to price a monthly stay

Start from what the same nights would earn as short stays, then account for what a monthly guest saves you.

- **Fewer turnovers.** For October 2026 our Fort Worth home has 10 stays booked over 24 nights, as of October 16. That is 10 cleans, 10 check ins and 10 reviews to earn. A monthly guest is one of each.

- **Fewer empty nights.** A month booked is a month booked. From late July through October 2026, October as booked on October 16, our Fort Worth home sold 26 of 30 weekend nights but only 37 of 70 weeknights. A monthly guest fills the weeknights that short stays leave open.

- **Platform tools.** Airbnb lets you set a weekly discount for stays of 7 nights or more and a monthly discount for stays of 28 nights or more.

A real example: in early October 2026 our Fort Worth home carried a 10 percent weekly and a 25 percent monthly discount on Airbnb. A four week stay priced at about $112 a night, about $3,100 before cleaning. Thirteen weeks at that rate would be 91 nights and about $10,200 before cleaning, as an example, not a quote. Compare that with your own short stay history for the same 91 nights, after cleaning and platform fees, before you set your monthly price.

**Watch the Stock Show.** A 13 week stay that starts in December runs straight through the Fort Worth Stock Show and Rodeo, January 15 to February 6, 2027. Our price floors for those weeks are $299 on weeknights and $379 on weekends, more than double a monthly rate. Price a long stay that crosses the show with that in mind, or start it after the show ends.

## Set the home up for a nurse

- Blackout curtains and the quietest bedroom you have, for day sleep after night shifts.

- Fast, steady WiFi and a real desk for charting and continuing education.

- A washer and dryer in the home. Scrubs get washed constantly.

- Off street parking with a light by the door. Shifts start and end at odd hours.

- A full kitchen stocked for meal prep: food storage containers, a slow cooker, a good knife.

- Utilities and internet included in one monthly price.

- A light clean and linen change every two weeks, offered or included.

- Drive times from the home to each hospital in the listing, measured at shift change.

- A clear pet policy decided up front, since some travelers bring a pet.

Most of this matches our [guest ready checklist](https://listandhost.com/blog/getting-a-home-guest-ready-checklist/). The differences are sleep, laundry and a workspace.

## Where to find nurse guests

- **Airbnb monthly stays.** Set a monthly discount, allow stays of 28 nights or more, and mention the hospital district and drive times in the listing.

- **Furnished Finder.** A listing site built for traveling nurses and other professionals on assignment.

- **Staffing firms.** Ask the agencies that place nurses in Fort Worth whether they keep a list of local furnished housing.

## Screening and paperwork

- Ask for the hospital name and the contract start and end dates. Match the stay to the contract, with a clear way to extend.

- For stays of 30 nights or more, use a written lease, take a security deposit, and photograph the home at move in and move out.

- Keep every message on the booking platform or in writing.

Want to know what a mix of event weekends and monthly stays could earn at your address? [Get a free earnings estimate](https://listandhost.com/estimate/). Our team runs its Fort Worth home this way, and you can [see its results](https://listandhost.com/results/).

## Quick answers

**When does Airbnb treat a stay as monthly?**

At 28 nights. Monthly discounts, long term cancellation policies and monthly payouts all start at 28 nights.

**How long are travel nurse contracts?**

Staffing firms describe 13 weeks as the most common length, and many contracts can be extended.

**Sources:** [GSA per diem rates (Fort Worth, fiscal year 2027)](https://www.gsa.gov/travel/plan-book/per-diem-rates) · [Airbnb Help Center: long term cancellation policies](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3735) · [Airbnb Help Center: payouts for long term reservations](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/285) · [Airbnb Resources: setting a price for longer stays](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/setting-a-price-for-longer-stays-379) · [Fort Worth South: Near Southside health sciences](https://www.fortworthsouth.org/community/whats-here/careers-health-sciences-major-employers/health-sciences/) · [Core Medical Group: length of travel nurse contracts](https://www.coremedicalgroup.com/blog/length-of-travel-nurse-contracts) · [Fort Worth Stock Show and Rodeo: visitor FAQ](https://www.fwssr.com/p/plan-a-visit/frequently-asked-questions)


# What an Airbnb Management Company Does

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/what-does-an-airbnb-management-company-do/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: What a full service short term rental manager should handle, from listing and pricing to cleaning and monthly statements, and what to ask before you sign.

List & Host team · September 29, 2026 · Updated October 18, 2026

If you own a home that could earn on Airbnb or Vrbo, the question is rarely whether it can make money. It is whether you want a second job running it. A full service management company exists to take that job off your plate. Here is exactly what that should include, so you can compare managers apples to apples, and how it maps to [the ways we work with owners](https://listandhost.com/services/).

## 1. Getting the home ready to book

- **A setup list for your home:** linens, towels, kitchen basics, safety items like smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, and the small touches guests mention in reviews.

- **Self check in:** a smart lock or lockbox so guests can arrive any time without anyone meeting them.

- **Photos that sell:** bright, wide, in the right order. The first five photos decide most clicks.

## 2. The listing itself

A good manager writes titles and descriptions for how guests actually search. Guests type places and features, like a river, a hot tub or an arena nearby, not clever phrases. Your listing should also go live on more than one platform. Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com each reach different travelers, and a manager should keep all three calendars in sync so you never get double booked.

## 3. Pricing, every single day

This is where most self managed homes leave the most money on the table. Nightly rates should move with the season, weekends, holidays and local events, and minimum stays should change too, so a two night weekend is not broken up by a one night booking. Just as important are price floors, so a slow week never prices your home far below what it is worth.

## 4. Guests, from first message to five stars

- Fast replies to inquiries, because response time affects both bookings and search ranking.

- Clear check in instructions sent before arrival.

- A check in on the first morning, so small problems get fixed before they become reviews.

- Checkout instructions, a thank you, and a review for every good guest.

## 5. Cleaning and turnovers

Every checkout needs a clean, a restock and a quick inspection before the next guest arrives, sometimes within five hours. A manager should schedule cleaners around every booking automatically, use a checklist, and report damage with photos right away so claims can be filed on time.

## 6. Maintenance

Things break in homes that host hundreds of guests a year. Your manager should have trusted local pros, handle small fixes fast, and bring anything above an agreed amount to you for approval with a quote first.

## 7. Money and reporting

You should get a monthly statement showing every booking, the platform fees, cleaning, repairs and exactly what was paid to you. If a manager cannot show you that clearly, keep looking. Here is [an example of the statement an owner gets and the online view we are building](https://listandhost.com/owner-dashboard/), with combined numbers from the homes our team runs.

## Questions to ask any manager before you sign

1. What percentage do you charge, and is it on booking revenue or on total payout?

2. What is billed on top: cleaning, supplies, repairs, setup, marketing?

3. Do you mark up repairs or supplies?

4. How fast do you answer guests, and who answers at night?

5. How long is the agreement, and how do I leave if I am not happy?

6. Can I block dates for my own use?

At List & Host, all of the above is included in one 20% fee for full service, guests pay the cleaning fee, and repairs and supplies are passed through at cost with receipts. Every fee and cost is on our [pricing page](https://listandhost.com/pricing/). Still deciding between a manager, a solo co host and doing it yourself? See our side by side comparisons: [self managing](https://listandhost.com/compare/self-managing/), [a solo co host](https://listandhost.com/compare/solo-co-host/) and [national managers](https://listandhost.com/compare/national-managers/). Want to see it working? [See results from the homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/). Wondering what your own home could earn? You can [try the instant estimator](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) for a low, likely and high yearly range, each figure with its basis.


# Airbnb Management Fees in 2026

Source: https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-management-fees/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: Full service Airbnb managers usually charge 18% to 25% of revenue in 2026. Here is what that covers, what gets billed on top, and how to compare quotes.

List & Host team · September 29, 2026 · Updated October 18, 2026

The first question every owner asks a manager is the fee. The better question is what the fee covers and what it is calculated on. Two quotes that look far apart can cost the same once the extras are added up, and two quotes with the same percentage can be thousands of dollars apart. This guide shows the usual ranges, the three bases a percentage can be taken from, a worked comparison and the contract terms to read before you sign. Our own offers and what each one covers are on our [services page](https://listandhost.com/services/), and every fee is on our [pricing page](https://listandhost.com/pricing/).

## Typical fee ranges

| Type of management | Typical fee |
| - | - |
| Listing and marketing only | 10% to 15% |
| Remote or hybrid management | 12% to 18% |
| Full service, with a local team | 18% to 25% |
| Luxury or resort markets | 25% to 40% |

These ranges come from public industry guides, listed at the bottom of this page. Local quotes vary. Full service is what most owners want: listing, pricing, guest messaging, cleaning coordination and maintenance, all handled. Remote and co hosting plans cost less because the owner, or a local person the owner hires, handles anything that needs hands at the home.

## What the percentage is taken from

This is where most owners get surprised. A percentage needs a base, and managers use different ones. Here is one example year, used in every table below. It is an illustration, not a forecast for any home:

- Guests pay $40,000 in nightly rent over the year.

- Guests also pay $6,000 in cleaning fees, which go to the cleaners.

- The platform keeps 15.5% of the nightly rent as its host fee: $6,200.

| What the 20% is taken from | Base in the example | Fee for the year |
| - | - | - |
| Everything guests paid, cleaning included, before platform fees | $46,000 | $9,200 |
| Nightly rent before platform fees | $40,000 | $8,000 |
| Nightly rent after the platform’s host fee | $33,800 | $6,760 |

Same percentage, $2,440 apart. Before you compare rates, ask each manager to write down the base in one sentence. If the fee comes out of cleaning fees, the cleaner or the owner pays for it in the end.

## What is usually included

- Creating and optimizing listings on the major platforms

- Daily pricing and calendar management

- Guest communication before, during and after each stay

- Booking management and payment handling

- Scheduling cleaners around every checkout

- A monthly statement with every booking, fee and cost

## What is often billed on top

- **Cleaning:** usually $50 to $350 or more per turnover, often covered by the guest cleaning fee.

- **Maintenance:** the vendor cost, sometimes plus a 5% to 15% coordination markup.

- **Supplies:** toiletries, paper goods, linens and restocking.

- **Recurring services:** lawn, pool or hot tub care.

- **Setup fees:** anywhere from $0 to $1,000.

- **Photography and furnishing:** sometimes billed at cost, sometimes marked up. Ask which.

## How to compare two quotes

Take a realistic year of bookings for your home and run both quotes against it, including every extra. A lower percentage with markups on repairs and supplies can end up costing more than a flat 20%. Here is the example year again, with $3,000 of repairs and supplies. Both quotes are made up for illustration.

************

|  | Quote A | Quote B |
| - | - | - |
| Rate and base | 15% of everything guests paid, before platform fees | 20% of nightly rent after the platform’s host fee |
| Management fee | $6,900 | $6,760 |
| Markup on $3,000 of repairs and supplies | 10%: $300 | None, billed at cost |
| Setup fee | $500 | None |
| Cost in year one | $7,700 | $6,760 |

The quote with the lower percentage costs $940 more in the first year. In later years, without the setup fee, Quote A still costs $440 more. A fee gap of a few points is also small next to pricing. On the example year, every 5% more in nightly rent is $2,000, more than the gap between these two quotes. Ask each manager how often rates change, who sets the floor, and to show you a calendar they run today. Run the same table with your own numbers. Our [free earnings estimator](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) gives you a starting year for your market, and our [guide to platform fees](https://listandhost.com/blog/airbnb-vs-vrbo-vs-booking-com-for-owners/) shows what Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com each keep. Weighing a local team against a large company or one co host? Our comparisons of [national managers](https://listandhost.com/compare/national-managers/) and [solo co hosts](https://listandhost.com/compare/solo-co-host/) put them side by side, with sources.

## Contract terms to read before you sign

The fee is one line. The agreement decides how easy the relationship is to live with, and how easy it is to leave. Read these parts closely:

- **Term and notice.** How long is the first term, and how many days of notice end it? Is there a fee to leave early?

- **Who owns the listing.** If the listing sits in your own account, the reviews and booking history stay with you. If it sits in the manager’s account, they usually stay with the manager.

- **Where payouts go.** Straight to you from the platforms, or through the manager first? Either can work, but you should get a statement that ties every payout to a booking.

- **Repair approvals.** Above what amount does the manager need your yes? Is there a written quote first?

- **Bookings after you leave.** Who hosts stays that were booked before the end date, and who is paid for them?

- **Owner use.** Can you block dates for yourself, and does the manager charge anything for nights you use?

- **Statement timing.** When does the monthly statement arrive, and what does it show?

## Red flags

- A percentage with no written base.

- Markups on repairs or supplies that are not on the statement.

- A long first term with a large early exit fee.

- No monthly statement, or one that shows totals but not each booking.

- Pricing that never changes. A manager should be moving rates for seasons, weekends and local events.

## How List & Host prices

Full service is one flat 20% of booking revenue, inside the usual full service range, with no setup fee. Booking revenue is the nightly rent plus any extra guest fees, after the platform's host fee. Taxes and cleaning fees are not part of it. Guests pay the cleaning fee, and repairs and supplies are billed at cost with receipts, never marked up. Payouts come to you straight from the platforms, your listing stays in your own account, and repairs above an amount you set come to you with a quote first. See [how our pricing engine and statement work](https://listandhost.com/how-it-works/), read [20 owner questions answered](https://listandhost.com/faq/), or [request a 15 minute call](https://listandhost.com/book-a-call/). To see what our fee leaves you on your own home, try the [free earnings estimator](https://listandhost.com/estimate/), or [see results from homes our team runs](https://listandhost.com/results/).

## Questions owners ask about fees

**What is a normal Airbnb management fee?**

Full service usually runs 18% to 25% of booking revenue. Remote and co hosting plans often run 12% to 18%. Luxury and resort markets can run higher. Always ask what the percentage is taken from.

**Is the management fee charged on cleaning fees?**

It depends on the contract. Some managers take their percentage from everything guests pay, cleaning included. Ours is not: booking revenue is the nightly rent plus any extra guest fees, after the platform’s host fee, and leaves out taxes and cleaning fees.

**Can I switch managers without losing my reviews?**

Yes, if the listing is in your own account. The reviews stay with the listing, and the new manager joins it as your host team. If the old manager’s account holds the listing, the reviews usually stay with them, so check this before you sign.

**Sources:** [Awning: Airbnb management fees 2026](https://awning.com/post/airbnb-management-fees)

# Privacy

Source: https://listandhost.com/privacy/
Updated: 2026-10-18
Summary: How List & Host collects, uses and protects the information owners send when they ask for an estimate or contact us.

Updated October 18, 2026

## What we collect

When you request an estimate, an audit or a call, send the application, or contact us, we collect the details you send: your name, email, your listing link or address if you give one, and information about your property. Our forms do not ask for a phone number. We use them only to reply to you and to prepare your estimate, audit or service agreement. We do not sell your information. We share it with no one outside List & Host except the providers named below.

When you use the estimator or the application, the page remembers your answers and the page you arrived on in your own browser only, so you can come back and finish. Nothing is sent until you press the last button, and the saved answers are cleared when it is sent.

## Referrals

When you [refer an owner](https://listandhost.com/refer/), we also collect the details you give us about that owner: their name, their email, the city of the home and how you know them, and your brokerage. The form asks you to confirm the owner agreed to hear from us. We use the owner’s details only to contact that owner about your referral, and yours only to reply to you and to pay the referral to your brokerage if they sign. If the owner tells us no thanks, we do not contact them again.

## If we wrote to you about your home

If we wrote to you about your home, we used public property records and a data company for your mailing address and email. Email stop to team@listandhost.com and we will never contact you again. The code printed on our letter is a reference number for that letter: it holds only a market and a bedroom count. If you type it into the [estimator](https://listandhost.com/estimate/) or open the page from the letter, it is sent with your estimate request or application so we can match it to the estimate we mailed you.

## Owner notes

If you sign up for Owner notes, we keep your email with our estimate requests and use it only to send the notes, about one email a month. Every email has a way to stop, and you can also email team@listandhost.com to be taken off the list.

## Who else handles it

- **Google Forms.** Every form on this site sends your answers to Google Forms, and they are stored in our Google account. See [Google’s privacy policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy).

- **Google Workspace.** Email to our addresses arrives in, and our replies are sent from, our Google Workspace mailbox.

- **GitHub Pages.** Our website is served by GitHub Pages, which keeps standard server logs such as IP addresses. We never receive them.

- **Fonts.** Served from our own site, so no font request leaves it.

- **Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.** We use them to see how our pages appear in Google and Bing results. They show us search terms as totals and never who searched. Nothing on this site sends them anything about your visit.

- **A data company and public property records,** only for owners we wrote to, as the section above says.

## Cookies and counting

This site sets no cookies of its own and runs no advertising, analytics or tracking scripts. We do not count visits today. When a form says we never share your information, it means we never share it beyond the providers named here.

## How long we keep it

| What | How long |
| - | - |
| Estimate, audit, call, application and contact answers | 24 months after our last contact with you, or sooner on request |
| Referral details | Until the referred owner answers, then 12 months |
| Email | As long as Google Workspace keeps it under our settings; we delete threads on request |
| Server logs at GitHub | GitHub’s own retention; we never receive them |
| Owner notes signup | Until you stop the emails or ask us to delete it |

## Your choices

To ask us to delete your information, or to see what we hold about you, email team@listandhost.com or use the [contact form](https://listandhost.com/contact/). We answer within one business day and finish a deletion within 30 days. If we wrote to you about your home, the word stop in a reply ends it.
